### §45 drain round 1 (P3-B6-8 part A drain r1, D1–D14) — corrections, and one prescription overtaken by the code

Ten evaluator findings plus seven nits, all actioned; nothing dropped. Every fix carries a test that FAILS on the pre-fix code, each verified by reverting the fix and watching the assertion fire. The referred `internal/review` deviation was independently reproduced and **RATIFIED**; D7 hardens the input that fix introduced, which the ratification puts in scope.

- **D1 — the preview frame shipped with NO `sandbox`, and that contradicted the platform's own contract.** `review.EscapeFirst()` names the channel `sandboxed-rendered-document-view` and S13.3 calls it "the sandboxed rendered-document view", so this was a conflict with the spec text rather than a missing hardening. Cross-origin blocks a frame reading this document's DOM; it does not stop the frame assigning `window.top.location`, and the surface it would navigate away from is the one that collects a PIN. The frame now rides `previewSandbox` = `allow-scripts allow-forms allow-same-origin allow-popups`, with **every token's grant reasoned on the code** and the withheld ones reasoned too — `allow-top-navigation` (and both sibling forms) is the capability most deliberately absent, and `allow-popups-to-escape-sandbox`, `allow-modals` and `allow-downloads` are named as withheld rather than merely missing. **`allow-same-origin` is safe here for a STRUCTURAL reason, said out loud rather than left to luck:** a preview is served from a different origin than the SPA (the tailnet `preview-<id>.<host>` subdomain, or a loopback port from the preview pool — **`internal/portpool`'s structural default `47600–47619`**, corrected at drain r2 R5: the figure first recorded here was `47900-47919`, which is `internal/api`'s TEST range and not a production port at all; the conclusion was re-verified against the real range and is unchanged, but a security argument must cite the range that ships), so the token restores the FRAME's origin and never this page's — and if a preview were ever served same-origin with the SPA the token would have to go. `referrerPolicy="no-referrer"` joins it: the SPA URL carries the deliverable id and was leaving as `Referer`, and the external preview link already carried `rel="noreferrer noopener"`.
- **D2 — the synthetic strip dropped comments the widget could not reach, on this packet's OWN golden fixture.** The strip asked only whether a placement had a line number; the widget map additionally required the file to be one of the rendered ones AND the line to fall inside a rendered hunk. A placement satisfying the first and failing the second rendered nowhere but the flat list — on the committed body, comment 2 (`mapped`, `site/release.tsx:10`) exactly. That is the invisible-comment class (P-T12-2) on the surface built to prevent it, and the code comments and §45 both claimed the opposite. **`widgetReach` is now the ONE function that answers "will a widget render this here?"**, used by the widget map and complemented by the strip, so the two cannot drift again. A surface with no diff at all passes an empty file list, so nothing has a live position and everything is on the strip — which is the right answer for an image or a binary.
- **D3 — the invariant test could not fail, which is why D2 survived it.** Its first half asserted a `[data-comment]` node exists for every served comment, which is a property of `comments.map` running; its second half recomputed the production predicate verbatim and compared the implementation to a copy of itself. It is now driven from the DOM: for every served comment, the id must appear in a `.diff-widget` **or** on the strip, both sets read out of what rendered — plus the complement check, that no id is in both, and floors on each set so neither half can pass over nothing. Verified together with D2: on the pre-D2 code it fires naming comment 2.
- **D4 — the prescription was overtaken by what the code actually requires, and the real defect was larger.** The finding was right that a durable, undeletable blocker comment was written before the answer and then reported as "nothing was sent", duplicating on retry. But the prescribed reorder (answer first, then guidance) would have LOST the guidance: `verify.ResumeWithGuidance` calls `RecordGuidance` and then `DrainOpen` **inline inside the answer request**, so a comment posted afterwards arrives after the batch it was written for was already consumed. And the deeper defect: `ValidateAnswer` **refuses `revise_with_guidance` with an empty `guidance` list**, so the landed client — which sent `{choice}` and nothing else — could never have worked at all; the test passed because it scripted a 200 for a body the server would have rejected, which is the B6-5 producer-fidelity root cause repeating inside this packet. **The fix is neither ordering: the guidance rides the ANSWER**, as `{choice, guidance:[{text}]}`, so there is exactly ONE write, the platform records and drains it in the correct order itself, a refusal means nothing was written, and a retry cannot accumulate. Severity is no longer this surface's to pick — `Answer.Comments()` marks a guidance point `Blocking` because guidance always names a problem to fix — and the form says so instead of offering a control the schema does not have. The empty-guidance case disarms the button with its reason, and the stale message now says "NOTHING was written — not the guidance, not the answer".
- **D5 — a second subscription whose data was discarded and whose §42 debt was settled anyway.** `key: served ? '' : …` disabled nothing: `useLive` uses `key` only as an effect DEPENDENCY, so the read and the `stream.subscribe()` both ran. Fixed at the CALL SITE, as directed — `useLive` is untouched: `OwnedCommentsBlock` mounts the hook and is rendered only by the surfaces that own the read, while the diff surface passes its own feed down. **A measurement worth recording rather than hiding:** this view's comment read went 4 → 2, not 4 → 1, because ONE subscribed `useLive` mount on this page costs two calls. **The MECHANISM recorded here was inverted, and the assertion built on it had a blind spot — both corrected at drain r2 R3.** It said "a child-mounted `useLive` reads twice per mount (the chat view's exchange sidebar does the same)", but child-ness is not the variable: on `/chat`, `GET /api/chat/sessions` is 1 and `GET /api/chat/files` is 2 — two SIBLING hooks in one component. The real rule is §44-B's own (drain r1, D7), demonstrated there: the FIRST subscriber opens the source and reads once, and a LATER one JOINS and reads twice because `EventStream.subscribe` hands a joiner an immediate synchronous `onResnapshot('connected')`. This page's detail hook is the opener, so previews and comments are both joiners at two. The test asserted `comments === the live /api/previews count` rather than a literal, on the reasoning that a literal would be "a claim about the framework" — but §44-B already pins that claim with its own demonstration, so the literal is a fact the repo proves, and the comparison form failed twice over: a doubled previews subscriber made it 4 === 4 and **passed silently**, and any change to `TryItBlock` failed this test while naming the comment feed as the culprit. Both were reproduced. It is a literal **2** now, with the §44-B pointer as its reason.
- **D6 — `parseDiff` ran bare in render with no boundary anywhere, so one malformed body took the whole app down.** The irony is load-bearing: this packet's deviation exists BECAUSE the server served a body that crashes this parser, and the consumer was left unguarded. `parseUnified` now catches and the failure renders as an ANSWER with its reason and the served text beside it, as text — the same forward-tolerance the unknown-`surface` arm already had. The regression feeds the exact pre-fix shape (a separator line before a real `diff --git` block) and fails on the unguarded code with the original `Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'changes')`.
- **D7 — the fix this packet added interpolated an unvalidated producer string into a wire format.** Not reachable at v0 (every mint passes a constant) and reachable the moment revisions carry producer-named trees, which `MintInput`'s own comment anticipates. `diffLabel` is the boundary check: a name carrying a newline, a carriage return or a tab, or containing `" b/"` (which makes the header ambiguous about where the old path ends), yields the EMPTY label — leaving git's own output untouched rather than emitting a mangled or forged header — and a leading separator is stripped so no `a//abs/path` can compose. **`relabel`'s own comment is corrected to the honest claim:** what makes the exact-string replacement safe is UNPREDICTABILITY (a random temp dir per call), not impossibility.
- **D8** — the accept-outcomes downgrade reason was false and is corrected above; the true reason is the wall-clock/varying-sha one the snapshot-pin bullet already gave. **The other four downgrades were re-checked and all hold.** ⚠ **This correction reached THIS FILE ONLY — `deliverable.test.tsx`'s own header kept the false reason until drain r2 R1.** For a declared downgrade the assertion site is the place that matters (this bullet's own rule: the reasons are named "at its assertion"), so a bookkeeping-only correction was not a correction.
- **D9/D10/D12/D13/D14** — the bundle "before" figure was §44-B's superseded drain-r1 measurement and is corrected to the landing one. `Content-Length` now comes from the FILE via `http.ServeContent` rather than from the recorded `ref.Size`, so the length and the body cannot disagree. **Its DRIVER changed at drain r2 R9**, which made a drifted object a refusal rather than a 200 — so the length claim can no longer be driven by drifting the bytes, and it is driven by a **Range read** instead (206 + `Content-Range` + a partial length is arithmetic only `ServeContent` over the served bytes can produce; a handler setting the recorded size and copying answers 200 with the whole body, verified). Record corrections: three derived object/fallback details not two (**this one also reached this file only — the assertion site still said "two" until drain r2 R2**), **FIVE** forward-promise sites in the scan header not three (§44-B was omitted from the count and so was the scan's own assertion message; this round said "four" and drain r2 R8 corrected it to five over the same enumeration), `SessionPanel` links rather than "links and embeds", and the closure is **not all-MIT** — `diff-match-patch` is Apache-2.0, recorded because three MITs in one bullet read like a claim about the tree. All eight banned tokens now carry a planted probe (four were unprobed), with a per-token loop that fails when one is missing. `answerAtDoor` resolves the route and requires the RESULT to stay under `/api/` on this origin, which is what its comment always claimed — `startsWith` admitted `/api/../evil`.
- **D11 — `scriptedFetch`'s fail-loud design does not reach reads, and that is now recorded rather than discovered again.** `api.ts` catches everything `fetch` raises and turns it into `Unreachable`, which `useLive` renders — so an unscripted READ inside a hook becomes an error state on screen instead of a failed test (B6-7's own F9 hit this). The image and binary surfaces' comment reads are scripted, and a test now asserts those surfaces render the real comment state rather than "The control plane is unreachable".
- **⚠ REFERRAL, adjacent to D10 — RAISED HERE, RULED ON BY THE COORDINATOR AND CLOSED AT DRAIN R2 R9 (see below).** The object route streamed without the hash re-check `review.Store.readObject` performs ("content is never trusted from disk without the pin check"), so a drifted object was served with a now-correct length rather than refused with the `content_drift` answer the handler already gives for missing bytes. This round's cost estimate — hashing on every read being "a real cost for the image trio, which re-reads the same objects once per mode" — was **pessimistic on both halves**, and r2 R9 measured why. The referral was raised rather than silently chosen, which is the part that was right.
- **Counters after drain r1:** unchanged from part A except the web suite and the bundle — migrations **0001–0020**, inventory **99/5/104**, ⚙ **118/33** byte-unchanged, `components.lock` **29** / **240** npm, `package.json`/`package-lock.json` byte-unchanged, catalog **50**, escape-scan allowlist **EMPTY** with the banned set at **8** and the floor at 42 · **44 Go packages** green · web **325 vitest / 19 files** (was 316/19) + typecheck + build. The bundle is **`951.73 kB`** (gzip **`286.71`**) after the round, measured — the sandbox/referrer attributes and the guarded parse cost `1.21 kB`. **$0**, hermetic, nothing pushed.

#### §45 drain round 2 (P3-B6-8 part A drain r2, R1–R9 — FINAL round under the cap)

Nine residuals from an independent re-check that corrected its own earlier report. **Two of them are the same failure mode: a drain-r1 correction that landed in this file and never reached the code it was about** — for a declared downgrade the assertion site is the only place that matters, so a bookkeeping-only correction was not one. Every code fix carries a check that FAILS on the pre-fix code, each verified by reverting it and watching the assertion fire; R1/R2/R5 are record corrections at their assertion sites, where the check is the fact each now cites (named below). Nothing already closed was weakened: D1–D7 and D9–D14 were re-run, and the two whose DRIVERS this round changed (D5's assertion form, D10's length driver) are re-driven rather than dropped.

- **R1 — D8's correction never reached the assertion site, and now does.** `deliverable.test.tsx`'s header still told a reader that a real applied accept "needs a git remote, a broker push and a collision engineered against a moving HEAD" — the exact claim `internal/accept/accept_test.go` refutes. Verified this round: `TestAcceptEndToEnd` applies a real accept against a `t.TempDir` bare remote through the **real broker server + client** (not a fake), `TestAcceptCollisionMergeCard` engineers the collision, and a `fakePusher` is composed in `internal/api`'s fixture world besides — so none of the three is the obstacle. The header now carries the TRUE reason, the one §45's snapshot-pin bullet already gave: a real accept mints a commit whose **sha and timestamps are wall-clock**, and neither can live in a fixed-clock golden body.
- **R2 — D12's correction likewise.** The header said "the **two** object-surface DETAILS … a third and fourth committed detail would prove nothing" while `doubles.ts` derives **three** — `imageDetail`, `binaryDetail`, `notebookDetail`, three `objectDetail(` call sites, counted. It names all three and says a FOURTH would prove nothing.
- **R3 — D5's recorded mechanism was INVERTED, and the assertion built on it had a blind spot that passed silently.** Both fixed; see the corrected D5 bullet above for the mechanism (§44-B drain r1 D7's rule: the first subscriber opens the source and reads once, a joiner reads twice — child-ness is not the variable, and `/chat`'s two sibling hooks at 1 and 2 are the counter-example). **The assertion is now a literal `2` with the §44-B pointer as its reason**, because §44-B pins that number as landed, demonstrated behaviour — a literal is a claim the repo proves, not a claim about the framework. **Both failures of the old comparison form were reproduced, not argued:** with a second `/api/previews` subscriber AND a doubled comments mount planted, the old `comments === live previews count` form **passed at 4 === 4** while the literal form fires with "4 calls where one subscribed mount costs 2"; and with only the previews subscriber doubled, the old form fails on a change to `TryItBlock` while naming the comment feed. Both `D5:` tests share one named constant, so the number has one home.
- **R4 — the superseded tautological invariant test is DELETED.** Its first half asserted a `[data-comment]` node per served comment, which is a property of `comments.map` running; its second half recomputed the production strip predicate and compared the implementation to a copy of itself. **Proved decorative rather than assumed so:** with the D2 defect re-introduced (`widgetReach` treating "has a line number" as reach), the deleted form **passes** while the surviving DOM-driven `D2/D3` invariant fires naming comment 2. Two tests where one cannot fail invites trusting the wrong one; a comment in its place says where the invariant lives.
- **R5 — a wrong number inside a security premise.** D1's `allow-same-origin` argument cited "this package's **47900-47919** pool" as the loopback preview origin. That is `internal/api`'s TEST range and not a production port at all; the shipping default is `internal/portpool`'s **47600–47619** (`portpool.go:40-41`). The conclusion — a preview is a different origin from the SPA, so the token restores the FRAME's origin — was re-verified against the real range and is unchanged, but a security argument must cite the range that ships. (§45's fixture-world bullet also says 47900-47919 and is CORRECT there: that one is the test world describing itself.)
- **R6 — `diff.go`'s label comment contradicted its own code, twice over.** It claimed a leading separator "would compose `a//abs/path`, so the label is always" repo-relative, but `TrimPrefix` strips exactly **one**: `//abs/path.ts` composed exactly that header and `///x.ts` composed `a///x.ts` (the landed test only ever tried one slash). **`TrimLeft` makes the claim true**, driven over one, two and three separators. And the second half: **`../../etc/passwd` survived verbatim into the header the anchor model keys on, and is now REFUSED** — not as a traversal fix (nothing resolves the label against a filesystem) but because the header IS the file identity, and a label that names something outside the tree the revision describes is the same class of lie the absolute form was. Refusal yields the empty label, which leaves git's own output untouched, exactly as the newline and `" b/"` limbs do. A name that merely contains dots (`site/..hidden/v1.2.ts`) still passes, so it stays a boundary and not a wall.
- **R7 — `apiPath` admitted percent-encoded traversal, which is the one thing its comment claimed it did not.** `new URL` does not decode `%2f`, so `/api/..%2fevil` resolved to a path still under `/api/` while Go's mux — which unescapes and THEN cleans — routes it to `/evil`. The guard's claim is about the RESULT, so it now decodes once (once, because the server decodes once: `%252f` stays a literal there too) and re-resolves before deciding; a malformed escape is refused rather than raised into the caller. `..%2f`, `..%2F`, `%2e%2e/` and `%2e%2e%2f` are all refused, and an ordinary encoded segment (`ask%3Ax`) still passes. **One expectation written for this fix was WRONG and is recorded as such rather than made to pass:** `/api/%2f%2fevil.invalid/x` is **admitted**, correctly — decoded it is `/api///evil.invalid/x`, which the mux cleans to `/api/evil.invalid/x`, still on the machine surface. It is a route that does not exist, not a route that escapes; only the `..` families leave.
- **R8 — the scan header's count is FIVE, and the two framings now agree.** `escape-scan.test.ts` said "FOUR landed texts" and enumerated five (its own header, its own assertion message, §41-B, §43, §44-B) — the off-by-one **preserved** from the original, which said THREE and enumerated four. §45's OQ1 bullet framed the same set as "three". The enumeration was always the complete part, so the count moved to five in both places, and drain r1's D10 clause is corrected to five with the reason it was four.
- **R9 — THE REFERRAL, IMPLEMENTED: the object route VERIFIES BEFORE IT SERVES.** A content-addressed route answering with bytes that hash to something other than the sha in its own URL is the response contradicting its own identity — a correctness question, not a hardening preference, and the same family as honest-absence-over-fabrication. Ruled on by the coordinator and implemented as a **narrow exported verified read on `internal/review`**, `OpenObjectVerified`, ratified as a further sanctioned-narrow touch of that package on the same grounds as the diff-header deviation: it is the package that owns object identity. No new vocabulary — a drifted object takes the same **`content_drift`** posture (500) the handler already gave for missing bytes, and the same one `reviewErr` gives for a drifted revision.
  - **Measured, because r1's cost estimate was the reason it was deferred.** Streaming sha256 on the build host runs **3.0–3.9 GB/s**: **68 µs** for a 200 KiB image, 0.56 ms for 2 MiB, 5.4 ms for 20 MiB. And the image trio's "re-reads the same objects once per mode" is **already suppressed by the route's own `Cache-Control: private, max-age=31536000, immutable`** — which is honest precisely because the sha in the path is the hash of the bytes.
  - **The cheapest honest posture, and why it is this one rather than a `ReadFile`.** The hash is taken over the **already-open handle** with `io.Copy` and the handle is then rewound, so it is **constant-memory** and — the part that matters more — what was verified and what is served are the **same inode**: an object replaced by path between two passes cannot slip through, which a verify-then-reopen would not give. `ServeContent` still streams from that handle, so HEAD and Range keep working.
  - **Driven by actually drifting a stored object**, as directed: the manifest row is immutable by trigger, so the BYTES on disk move under a hash that still names the old ones. The route answers 500 `content_drift`, **not one drifted byte reaches the caller**, and a sibling object still serves — so the refusal is about those bytes and not a route that stopped working. Probe: with the verify reverted to a plain `os.Open` the test fires with `got 200`.
  - **D10 is re-driven, not dropped.** Its old driver WAS the drift that is now a refusal, so the length claim is carried by a **Range read**: 206, `Content-Range: bytes 8-13/14`, `Content-Length: 6`, plus a HEAD carrying the full length with an empty body. Probe: with `ServeContent` replaced by a hand-set `ref.Size` length plus `io.Copy`, it fires with `got 200` and the whole body.

The comment now says both halves, and says why the narrower claim is the honest one: objects are written once by rename and never reopened for writing, so the gap is a filesystem the platform does not have. - **OQ3 as landed — a narrow exported `Roster` read in `internal/worker` (`roster.go`), served at `GET /api/workforce`.** This is a **REPORTED widening** of a leaf package, declared and not silent, on the `internal/memory/browse.go` precedent. It is there rather than in the transport for a reason that is structural, not stylistic: a worker's equipment lives in its version's **hash-verified FILE**, and the walk that reads one — `activeDefinition` — performs the S08.3 tamper check on every read. A transport assembling that from SQL would be a second reader of one identity (the §40-C D3 twin hazard) and a reader with no tamper check at that. The **delivery policy** has the same property, so the roster CALLS `Store.Delivery` rather than re-deriving degraded-mode consequences beside it: one expression of S08.7, two consumers.
  - **The visibility line, and why it is deliberately NOT memory's.** `browse.go` has no operator limb, because house authority (D10) is the right to curate the house scope and not a read into somebody's personal store. A **worker is different in kind**: it is audited platform machinery whose approval, promotion, guardrails and domain maturity are all D10 operator acts, so **the operator reads the whole registry** — the runs/telemetry posture (§30). The content-vs-telemetry line still binds conversations (§44) and personal memory (§40-C); it does not reach the machinery that does the work. A member gets S15.10's own rule: **own personal workers plus the household roster**. `rosterVisible` is the ONE expression of that predicate, and a roster read with no viewer is REFUSED rather than answered unscoped.
  - **Driven three ways, and the member limb is the one it exists for.** op / alice / bob against one world, asymmetric in both directions: alice sees the household worker and her own draft and NOT bob's personal automation; bob sees the household worker and his own automation and NOT alice's draft. The non-tautological control runs the same query with the member predicate DEFEATED and asserts bob's automation then reaches alice — without it the three-way test could have been passing because the world happens to carry what it carries.
- **OQ4 as landed — the version→outcome join is DERIVED at the transport, and it is not a catalog query.** S08.4 says "version→outcome is a JOIN, not a system", so this is a bounded scan of `routing.decided` rows that name a worker VERSION ⋈ that run's `verdict.recorded` rows ⋈ the metering seam, on the §42-B decisions-block precedent: it spans the worker registry, the verify family and metering, and none of those is the others' home. **The Layer-1 catalog did not move** — it sits at its 30–50 band ceiling (50/50) and a query there is a gate matter, not this read's. Layer-0 views stay **11**, the catalog stays **50**.
  - **MONEY IS READ, PER RUN, AND NEVER TOTALLED.** Each routed run carries the figures `MeterReader.RunMeter` served and nothing else. There is **no per-version total and no per-worker total**, on the fleet's own reasoning (§42-B): a cross-run sum would be arithmetic nobody performed, and it answers a question this platform does not ask, because each person's account burns separately (D2). The shapes carry no `total`/`sum`/`average`/`aggregate` field for a reader to mistake for one, checked over a REAL served body by a KEY-position regex — a worker's task class is legitimately `summarize`, and a scan that read a value as a field name would be noise rather than a check (§42's path-vs-division lesson in a second shape). Probes in both directions.
  - **⚠ THE FIRST CUT SERVED A FABRICATED ZERO IN PRODUCTION AND PASSED EVERY TEST — found by an adversarial pass, and it is the packet's most useful finding.** `err == nil` was read as "there is a reading". It is not: `Ledger.RunConsumption` FOLDS a run's checkpoint rows, so a run that exists and has recorded no usage yet — **every run between its routing decision and its first checkpoint**, which is the state the newest rows are in — folds to zero tokens, zero cost and zero unpriced calls **successfully**. The surface would have printed `USD 0` for work nobody has measured, which is the exact fabrication §37 exists to forbid. It was invisible because `fixtureMeter` had only TWO arms — a hardcoded figure and an error — so the third, and commonest, production state had no fixture at all. **The fix is in two places and the fixture half is the load-bearing one:** `readMeter` renders an entirely empty reading as the absence it is ("no usage recorded for this run yet"), distinct from a refusal ("no meter reading for this run") because they are different facts; and `fixtureMeter` gained the empty arm for `r-claim`, whose state is `claimed` and which has therefore genuinely run nothing. All three arms are now in the committed bodies, and the probe fires with `got USD 0`. **Recorded as a class, not an incident:** a seam double whose arms are narrower than the seam's real behaviour makes every consumer of it untestable, and this one had been narrow since B6-5.
  - **TWO SCOPES, SERVED AS SENTENCES, because they genuinely differ.** The ROSTER scope is the worker's (household or own); the OUTCOME scope is **the RUN's owner** — a member reading the shared worker sees her own routed runs and not bob's, because another person's run and another person's money are not hers to read (the `readPerson` rule). `roster_scope` and `outcome_scope` ride the body as text, so a narrower reading can never pose as the wider one, and both are rendered on screen. Driven: the operator's reading of the same version is strictly wider than the member's, and the version whose only run is somebody else's renders an **explained** absence rather than an unexplained empty.
  - **FOUR BOUNDS, EACH ON A DIFFERENT COST, and one of them is not about response size at all.** `workforceRosterCap` (200) is the page a person reads. `workforceRoutingCap` (1000) bounds the SQL scan, because the control plane shares ONE writer connection (S02.1). `workforceRunsPerVersion` (20) bounds what one VERSION serves — without it a single hot version consumes the scan budget and every other version reads as "never routed to", which is the shape of lie this surface exists to avoid. And **`workforceMeterCap` (100) bounds the METER fan-out**, which is the expensive part of the whole read and was the first cut's real cost: `Ledger.RunConsumption` opens a **write transaction per run** on that same single connection, so an unbounded loop over routed runs would have been up to a thousand serialized write transactions per page load, on a view that re-reads on thirteen event types. Beyond the bound a row says its figure was not read rather than carrying a number nobody took, and the reading is memoized per run id so a run routed twice is metered once.
  - **THE VERDICT SCAN IS BOUNDED PER RUN, NOT PER REQUEST, and that is what makes "no verdict recorded for this run yet" a sentence a reader can trust.** A global `LIMIT n` over a multi-run scan lets one talkative run consume it, and the runs it starves then render an absence the READING invented — a false statement about verified work rather than a smaller one. A `ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY run_id …)` keeps every run's newest rounds reachable regardless of what its siblings carry, and a run whose own rounds were cut says so. Driven: 25 rounds on one run, all newer than a sibling's single round, and the sibling still gets it — with the probe reverting to the global bound and watching the sibling's verdict disappear.

So the card renders the registry's own vocabulary — tools / skills / knowledge selectors / connectors as REQUESTED, the guardrails row as GRANTED — and says out loud that there is no standing helper roster, pointing at where a helper spawn really is visible: **the `helper-spawn` routing cause on a routed run**, which the outcome rows already carry. A test asserts the served body contains no `helpers` key at all, so "no roster rendered" means the schema has none rather than that the view dropped one.
- **OQ7 as landed — "multi-stage connections" grounds to the registry's own multi-stage data.** A `kind=automation` worker renders its parsed `automation.Workflow` chain: the dialect, the ONE named service, and the ordered steps with their **explicit approval nodes marked** — an outward step becomes a gated proposal and never a direct call (S08.9; D7). The S06 task pipeline stays B6-5's story. Both arms exist in the fixture, so "marked" means something: the read step is unmarked and the outward one is marked, and a defect that marked every step fires the test.

#### §45-B drain round 1 (P3-B6-8 part B drain r1, D1–D11 + two dispositions) — corrections, and one defect class that repeated inside its own fix

An independent evaluation returned FAIL with 13 findings. **Two executor positions were upheld and closed:** the `cursor` 64→84 deviation (the cursor IS the head `event_seq`, so producer-driven workers necessarily advance it, and "cursor 64" and "real producers" cannot both hold) and `Config.NewID` (both mint sites converted, nil defaults to the existing generator, production injects nothing). Every fix below carries a check that FAILS on the pre-fix code, verified by reverting the fix and watching the assertion fire; the two prose-only items say so. **CORRECTED IN PLACE at drain r2: that sentence was a blanket claim and it was not true of D5's SERVER half** — forcing `ScheduleAttachable: false` in `workforce.go` passed every `-run TestWorkforce` test and only the golden-drift check fired, which is a real net but not a localized one. Drain r2 adds the localized assertion (`TestWorkforceScheduleBarIsAServedFactOnEveryGrantedBlock`), so the sentence is true as written now rather than by charity.

- **D1 — THE PACKET'S OWN HEADLINE FINDING, SHIPPED AGAIN THREE LINES AWAY.** §45-B calls the fabricated-zero discovery "the packet's most useful finding" — and the same commit rendered `Budget: USD 0` in **every granted block on the surface**, from its own committed golden. `worker_guardrails` stores both ceilings NOT NULL with a `>= 0` check and `Approve` copies the version's REQUEST verbatim, so a version that asked for no ceiling is granted **0** — and the registry's own request type says exactly that, carrying `omitempty` on both fields. The platform's precedent was already in this package (`api.go`: "no operator budget is persisted anywhere … the ABSENCE is what the meters surface serves — never a zero", S10.1). **Fixed at the boundary:** both ceilings are nil-able on the wire, nil when the row stores 0, and the view renders the reason. **The guard was pointed away from where the defect landed** — `not.toMatch(/USD\s*0\b/)` was scoped to `.routed-cost` cells only — and now quantifies over **every** money span the surface produces. The fixture drives both arms for real: v2 of the release-notes writer REQUESTS ceilings and the automation requests none, so the figure and the absence are both produced by `Approve` rather than by a synthesized body. Probes: serving the stored 0 fires `TestWorkforceUndeclaredCeilingIsAnAbsenceNotAZero`, and the re-pointed span scan catches it in jsdom.
- **D2 — the same defect, flipped the other way, on a LANDED surface.** The new `fixtureMeter` arm (`r-claim` → zeros with no error) is consumed by `reads.go`, which treated `err == nil` as "there is a reading" — the identical defect fixed in `readMeter` one file away — so `tasks.json`'s `cost_so_far_usd` for `r-claim` went `null` → **`0`** and the `/board` card began rendering `Cost so far USD 0` where it had rendered an honest absence. The whole web suite passed in both directions; nothing noticed. **Fixed at the consumer, not by narrowing the double back** (narrowing would recreate the untestable-seam problem §45-B already records): `meterReading` on the projector is now **THE** expression of "does this run have a cost reading", and `reads.go`, `projection.go` and `workforce.go` all go through it. `RunCounters.APIEquivCostUSD` became nil-able with it — tokens stay a plain counter beside it, because a monotonic count at zero is a true reading while a money zero is a price nobody set. Ripple swept: one golden (`run-detail.json`, unchanged — `r-ship` has a real reading), one web type, one render site already using `<Money>`. The §45-B sentence describing what moved **was false as written and is corrected in place** above. Probe: `TestMeterReadingIsOneExpressionAcrossEverySurface` fires when the helper returns `true` unconditionally, and it checks all three surfaces answer the same way for the same run — plus the other direction, that a run WITH a reading still shows it. **THE RIPPLE SWEEP WAS INCOMPLETE, corrected in place at drain r2 (R3/R4):** "all three surfaces answer the same way" held for the ABSENCE and not for the reading. `WorkforceRoutedRun` carried the seam's `Unpriced` marking and `RunCounters` did not, so an unpriced run still printed a bare `USD 0` on the run card — the fabrication class, one surface over — and the helper's own discriminator had a sign-flipped false negative besides. Both are r2's R3 and R4.
- **D3 — the chain was served without its connections, on a premise the dialect contradicts.** The comment said "an arg is a value flowing between them, not a connection". A `{"$from":"steps.fetch.summary"}` arg is not a runtime value: it is a **definition-time edge**, and in the fixture it is the ONLY place `post`'s dependency on `fetch` is written down — so the served chain was a sequence with approval flags and no connections at all, under-delivering the one thing S15.10 names ("how multi-stage procedures connect"). **Serialized selectively:** `$from` references are kept as `needs` (argument name → reference), literals are dropped, because a reference is a connection and a literal is a value. The false premise is corrected at the comment, and `workforce_test.go`'s assertion — which pinned the wrong reasoning by requiring no `args` key at all — now asserts the two edges by name and keeps the no-raw-args check as what it really is. Probes: dropping `needs` fires the chain test; keeping literals fires `TestWorkforceStepReferencesKeepEdgesAndDropLiterals`, which drives a definition carrying one of each. **CORRECTED IN PLACE at drain r2 — the replacement comment was itself false, in both directions, and the fix narrowed the defect instead of ending it.** It claimed "the shape is the dialect's own (automation.resolveArgs)" while running a stricter decoder of its own, so a legal edge was still dropped and a literal was still drawn as an edge; see R1 below. The conclusion of this entry stands; its premise did not, which is exactly the failure mode a correction has to avoid.
- **D4 — a worker that FAILED its S08.3 integrity check rendered none of its granted powers.** The permissions block lived inside the `definition !== null` arm, so a tamper failure hid exactly the half an auditor needs: the powers are recompiled from the guardrails TABLE on every invocation (S08.2) and are unaffected by an unreadable file. A person learned the file cannot be trusted and not what the worker is still allowed to do. **The two are separate renders now** — the REQUESTED equipment goes absent with the file, because that is where it lives; the GRANTED block does not. Probe: re-gating the block fires the test, which drives a single-version worker with `Bash`/`WebFetch`/`C3`/`unrestricted` — grants that appear nowhere else in the body, so no sibling can satisfy it.
- **D5 — S08.7's third consequence was missing, and the card could contradict it.** S08.7 names three; the marking rendered two. Meanwhile the granted block rendered `Attachable to a schedule: yes` unconditionally from a row `Approve` copies **unclamped** from the request — so a degraded-domain worker that requested attachability could say "yes" beneath a marking that never stated the bar. The third consequence is now in the marking, and the schedule row carries the bar when the domain is degraded. **The fixture had to reach it:** all three workers granted `false`, so the automation now REQUESTS `ScheduleAttachable` and the contradiction is produced by the real verb. Probes: removing either half fires the test, and the full-domain worker's row is asserted to carry no bar so the wording is a consequence rather than a constant.
- **D6 — one sentence for two different facts.** "no routed run in this reading" was served both for a version nobody has ever routed to and for one whose only run belongs to another owner, while §45-B claimed the latter renders an **explained** absence. It explained nothing. **Now they differ:** the operator's reading covers every owner, so its empty answer is about the version ("no run has been routed to this version"); a member's covers her own runs, so its empty answer is about what she ran ("no run of yours has been routed to this version"). That is also the most a member's answer may honestly say — "there is a run here you cannot see" would disclose the existence of another owner's run to the person the scope exists to withhold it from — and the test asserts the member's wording carries no such disclosure. Probe: collapsing the two arms fires `TestWorkforceEmptyOutcomeSentencesDifferByReading`.
- **D7 — the meter budget was spent in randomized map order.** `for ver, rows := range grouped` gates on the cap, so past 100 distinct runs WHICH rows carried a figure varied between identical requests — the determinism family — and unlike this surface's three other bounds it was not newest-first. The join now walks the scan's own order (globally newest-first) and applies the per-version bound in it, so the budget is spent newest-first and the map walk is gone. Probe: `TestWorkforceMeterBudgetIsSpentNewestFirstAndDeterministically` seeds 140 routed runs — the cap is unobservable below it — and fires on the map-walk shape with "kept an older row over a newer one".
- **D8 — PROSE ONLY, no code change, and the honest exception to the probe rule.** "which is what keeps a roster of N workers from becoming 2N queries" is true of the JOIN and of nothing else. The roster path is frankly an N+1: per template a domain read, a delivery policy that re-reads the template, and a versions query; per version guardrails, latest validation and latest revalidation. It is left that way deliberately — household scale, and the alternative is hand-written joins duplicating reads the registry owns — so the comment now says what the path is and that **the real bound is the caps, not the query count**. Bolting a grep-for-a-sentence guard onto a prose fix would be a check that tests nothing.
- **D9 — the new card, and the witness it quietly weakened.** `effect:e-digest` is the first committed card with `card.kind: "automation-step"`; nothing asserted on it, and `inbox.test.tsx`'s `toContain('effect')` — previously witnessed uniquely by `e-notify` — became satisfiable by either. **The kind checks are now witnessed BY ID**, both of them, so a card cannot disappear behind its sibling; and a new test pins what the automation-step proposal actually renders through the generic fallback (the verb, the step and the service all reach the screen, beside its High tier and its `approve`/`deny` actions). **B6-6's card vocabulary was NOT grown from inside this packet** — the legibility of the generic fallback is the coordinator's gate question; what this adds is the evidence to decide it against. Probe: renaming `e-notify` in the golden fires the witness assertion.
- **D10 — a §45-B claim made true.** `fxPinDryRunProposal` pinned by `ORDER BY rowid DESC LIMIT 1` while §45-B said "pinned exactly as `e-publish`'s is", and `e-publish` pins by explicit id. It now selects by the proposal's own identity (service + step + verb, unique within a workflow). It failed safely today and would have pinned the wrong effect the moment a second automation joined this world. Probe: pointing the identity at the wrong step fires `TestWebAPIFixtures`.
- **D11 — two of R14's three named readings were missing.** R14 asks for "runs routed, verdict outcomes, cost figures". Only the third was served. Added: `runs_routed`, counted BEFORE the per-version bound so it stays true when the list is cut and scoped like everything else (a member's count is her runs, asserted strictly narrower than the operator's), and `verdict_tally`, the recorded rounds per verdict value, sorted so two identical requests answer identically. **The line held: a count of rows is a reading; money is not summed.** No total, no average, no derived money — the aggregate key scan still passes and still probes both directions. Probes: dropping either reading, or letting the count escape the owner scope, each fire `TestWorkforceServesRunsRoutedAndVerdictOutcomes`. **CORRECTED IN PLACE at drain r2 (R2): both readings were wrong, and "a count of rows is a reading" is exactly how.** `runs_routed` counted routing DECISIONS while its name, its Go doc and its render all said runs — a run re-routed to one version reported as two — and the tally re-counted a duplicated row's rounds AND was silently bounded by `workforceVerdictsPerRun`. A count whose name does not describe what it counts is the fabricated-figure class in another currency; both are fixed in r2 and neither claim above should be read as having been true when it was written.
- **F9 — ACCEPTED, recorded as a known blast-radius property.** A `Domain` or `Delivery` error in `rosterEntry` fails the WHOLE map rather than degrading one worker. That is deliberate and it is safe for a structural reason: `worker_templates.domain` is a foreign key into `domains`, `domains` carries a no-delete trigger (migration 0005), `Delivery`'s guardrails read is guarded by `ActiveVersion`, and `Repoint` requires an approved version — so neither read can be missing for a template that exists. Handling a state the schema forbids is barred by the scope guardrail, and the alternative (a nil-able policy) would have been a second unreachable arm whose only possible default said `requires_review: false`.
- **F12 — THE OPERATOR LIMB RESTS ON A READING, and the reading is recorded rather than asserted flat.** S15.10's parenthetical — "personal workers to their owner, the shared roster to all" — describes the ordinary identity scoping; the coordinator's ruling is that it does not silently repeal S01.9's platform-wide role model, and that worker identity is already operator-visible through `routing.decided` on the runs surfaces, so hiding the roster would be a fig leaf rather than a boundary. **The OQ3 disposition stands on that reading, not on the sentence alone**, and it is carried to the B6 gate as an explicit operator ratification item. The evaluator was right to raise it: OQ3's own text invited the flag.

#### §45-B drain round 2 (P3-B6-8 part B drain r2, R1–R11 — FINAL round under the cap)

An independent re-check confirmed both HIGHs closed and not coming back, and eleven residuals survived. All eleven are actioned below; **R10 is accepted with its grounds and deliberately not changed**. Every fix carries a check that FAILS on the pre-fix code, each verified by reverting the fix and watching the assertion fire — the probe is named per item. **R9 is prose only and says so.** Three of these are the same defect as this packet's own headline finding in a different currency, and two of them were introduced by the fix for the first one.

- **R1 — THE STEP-EDGE PREDICATE WAS A SECOND OPINION, AND IT WAS WRONG IN BOTH DIRECTIONS.** Drain r1's D3 narrowed the missing-connections defect rather than ending it: the replacement comment claimed "the shape is the dialect's own (`automation.resolveArgs`)" while `StepReferences` ran a `json.Decoder` with `DisallowUnknownFields` and a `From *string` of its own. Driven end to end through the real dialect: `{"$from":"steps.fetch.summary","note":"annotated"}` PARSES (`Step.Args` is `map[string]json.RawMessage`, so the document loader's strictness never reaches inside an argument value) and the executor RESOLVES it — `digest` really does receive step `fetch`'s output — while the reader returned `map[]`, showing no connection at all for a step that consumes the previous one's. And `{"$from":""}`, which the executor passes through as the literal it is, rendered as an edge to nowhere. Both are false statements about how the stages connect, which is the one thing S15.10 asks this surface for. **Fixed by deletion, not by a better copy:** the predicate is EXPORTED from the dialect as `automation.Reference`, `resolveArgs` calls it, and `worker.StepReferences` calls it — one expression, the twin-hazard rule this codebase already applies to `rosterVisible`, `meterReading` and `acceptable()`. The false comment is corrected where it stood. Probe: restoring the local decoder fires `TestWorkforceStepEdgesUseTheDialectsOwnPredicate` on both limbs at once (`map[blank:]`).
- **R2 — TWO COUNTS THAT DID NOT COUNT WHAT THEIR NAMES SAY.** `runs_routed` counted routing DECISIONS. A run can be routed to one version more than once — `override` is a cause this fixture world already carries — so re-routing `r-notes` to the same version served **`runs_routed=4` for 3 distinct runs**, while the field name, the Go doc ("how many **runs**") and the render ("N routed in this reading") all said runs. **That is the fabricated-figure class in another currency**, and this packet has now been shown it four times. The tally had the same defect squared: the duplicated row re-counted that run's rounds, so ONE recorded SHIP tallied as **`SHIP: 2`**. And it was **silently bounded** — 25 REWORK rounds tallied as 20, because `workforceVerdictsPerRun` cuts what reaches the tally and `verdicts_truncated` lives per run where the tally never looks. **Both fixed:** the count is of DISTINCT runs (a decision naming no run counts as no run, and its row still renders with both absences stated); each run contributes to a version's tally ONCE; and `verdict_tally_truncated` says the tally is a floor whenever either bound cut it, rendered beside the numbers, because a bound nobody can see is a silent cap. `Runs`'s own doc now says it is one row per DECISION, which is what makes two numbers the right answer rather than a contradiction. Probes: counting rows fires with "runs_routed = 4 for 3 distinct runs"; dropping the per-run dedupe fires with "SHIP: 2 for ONE recorded SHIP round"; dropping the marker fires with "25 recorded rounds tally as 20 with nothing saying the number is a floor".
- **R3 — THE UNPRICED `USD 0`, ONE SURFACE OVER FROM WHERE THIS PACKET KEPT LOOKING.** A subscription lane prices UNPRICED, so the seam serves cost `0` with `Unpriced: true` — and `RunCounters` carried no `unpriced` field, so `GET /api/runs/r-ship` served `{api_equiv_cost_usd: 0}` and `TaskDetail.tsx` rendered a bare **"USD 0"**. That asserts the run was free when the cost is genuinely unknown: reachable in production, and the exact class the nil-able field beside it exists to prevent in the other direction. The map's own `WorkforceRoutedRun` had carried the marking since part B landed, so §45-B's "`meterReading` is THE expression shared by the task list, the run card and the map" was true of the helper and **not true of what the three surfaces render** — corrected in place above. **Additive only:** `RunCounters.Unpriced` mirrors the landed field, `projection.go` sets it beside the figure, nothing else in `reads.go`/`projection.go` moved, and the ripple is one web type plus one render site. **The guard was pointed away from it too** — drain r1's quantified money scan is scoped to `.workforce .money` and `taskdetail.test.tsx` had no money guard at all — so the run card gets its own, quantified over every money span it produces, both directions. Probes: dropping the Go assignment fires `TestRunCardCarriesTheUnpricedMarkingWithTheFigure`; dropping the render fires both new web tests.
- **R4 — THE SAME DEFECT SIGN-FLIPPED, and it withholds a TRUE figure.** `meterReading` keyed on folded MAGNITUDES, and the ledger deliberately prices a local duty call a true $0 on the permanent free tier (the zero-allowance row, S12.1). A run whose recorded work was local folds to zero tokens, zero cost and zero unpriced calls — a real measurement, indistinguishable from a run nobody has touched, served as an absence. **Carried, because it is additive and confined to the seam plus its one shell composition:** `api.RunMeter.Calls` is what the ledger FOLDED, `projMeter` fills it from `RunConsumption.TotalCalls`, and `meterReading` reads `Calls > 0` first. The magnitude arms STAY as the fallback: a seam that does not report a count reports 0, and withdrawing a figure it did serve is the worse of the two errors. Probe: `TestMeteredZeroIsAReadingAndUnmeteredIsNot` seeds a real local checkpoint through the wire contract `internal/local` writes, asks the REAL ledger (1 call, $0 priced, 0 unpriced), and fires on the magnitudes-only predicate with "a MEASURED zero was served as an absence" — plus the other direction, that a run with no checkpoints still has no reading.
- **R5 — A LITERAL PIN THAT PINNED ITSELF.** `if len(first) != api.WorkforceRunsPerVersion` moves both sides together, so it could not fail — the tautology class part A removed twice. It is the literal `20` now, beside `:814`'s real literal. And the export earns its place instead of being deleted: the assertion below it reasons "20 rows is far inside the 100-run meter cap", which is a RELATION between two independent bounds, so that relation is now checked rather than assumed — without it, lowering `workforceMeterCap` would make the budget check fail for a reason unrelated to what it tests. Probe: moving `workforceRunsPerVersion` to 19 fires the literal; the self-reference could not.
- **R6 — THE RENDERED TALLY NUMBER WAS UNPINNED WEB-SIDE.** Every tally in the committed body carries exactly 1 round, so rendering the constant `1` instead of `String(t.rounds)` passed the whole suite. The Go side pins the content, so this was a layering gap rather than an unpinned fact — but a render bug printing the wrong count would have shipped. Pinned with counts that are neither 1 nor each other (7 and 2), asserting the exact rendered pair and the `data-rounds` attribute. Probe: the constant fires it.
- **R7 — A POLICY CONSEQUENCE DECIDED IN THE BROWSER, AND FORGOTTEN ON HALF THE BLOCKS.** `Workforce.tsx` derived the schedule bar from `w.domain.maturity === 'degraded'` — a client-side side-truth the standing readings bar, and a forward-tolerance hole in drain r1's own new code, because a maturity this build has never heard of that ALSO bars schedules would go unmarked even when the server knows it does. The flag also had to be handed to `Grants` by its caller, and `VersionBlock` did not, so **a superseded version in a degraded domain rendered "granted" with no bar at all**. **Served instead:** `WorkforceGrants.ScheduleBarred` is decided where the maturity vocabulary is defined and rides the grants row, so every render of a granted block carries its own and there is no prop to forget. One golden line moved (`wt-digest`'s block gains `schedule_barred: true`) through the real regeneration path. Probes: forcing the server field false fires the Go test; ignoring the served field fires both web tests, including one driven with a maturity string (`quarantined`) no client vocabulary knows.
- **R8 — D5's SERVER HALF, LOCALIZED.** Forcing `ScheduleAttachable: false` passed every `-run TestWorkforce` test and only `TestWebAPIFixtures` fired. Golden drift is a real net, so this was about localization rather than safety — but it made drain r1's blanket "every fix carries a check that FAILS on the pre-fix code" untrue as written. **The assertion was added rather than the claim weakened**, which is the resolution that leaves the sentence true; the r1 preamble is corrected in place anyway, because the claim was false when it was made. No grep-for-a-sentence guard was added. R6's pin closes the other half of the same blanket claim.
- **R9 — PROSE ONLY, and named as the exception.** `api_test.go`'s "nil = counters best-effort (zero)" was falsified by drain r1: a nil meter now serves the cost as an absence. Corrected in place, and so are the two production comments that said the same thing (`MeterReader`'s doc and `Config.Meter`'s), which the finding did not name but which were false for the same reason. No probe: a comment fix carries no check, and bolting a text guard onto one would be a check that tests nothing (the D8 precedent).
- **R10 — ACCEPTED, recorded, not changed.** D10's identity pin (`fxPinDryRunProposal`) drops the `LIMIT`, so two automations sharing service + step + verb would silently pick one row. It is **strictly better than the `ORDER BY rowid DESC LIMIT 1` it replaced** — that one picked the wrong row the moment a second automation joined, this one only when two automations share all three identity fields — and it is unreachable in the fixture world, which carries exactly one automation. Left as it is.
- **R11 — THE INERT-PROBE DISCLOSURE, CLOSED WHERE IT IS THIS PACKET'S.** The re-check swept the class and found most instances are pre-existing B6-5/B6-6 tests, NOT charged here and carried to the gate. The one that is this packet's: `workforce_test.go`'s "non-tautological control" verified a claim about **production** `Ledger.RunConsumption` by asking `fixtureMeter{}` — a stub written to match the claim, so it could only agree. **It asks the real ledger now** (`r-claim` is a real run row with no checkpoints: zeros, `err == nil`, `TotalCalls == 0`), which also grounds R4's discriminator. ## 46. Declarative Web Push, the S15.6 notifier & the S15.12 completeness sweep (P3-B6-9; S15.11–S15.12, S01.8, S01.9, S14.2, S19.5, S07.7 via internal/verify, §29/§31/§32, §41+§41-B, §42+§42-B, §43-B, §44, §45-B)

**The LAST build packet of B6 and of Sinet v0.** It opens migration **0021**, registers **three** new event types, adds the leaf package `internal/push` and the notifier that drives it, completes the PWA, and then sweeps the finished tree against S15.12's four cross-cutting duties plus S19.5's "the React SPA consumes every API built above". After it: the B6 gate. Nothing in it is deferred except the named gate/bring-up/drill items below.

### The fourteen dispositions, as landed

- **OQ1 — OWNED STDLIB CRYPTO, and the vector discipline is what makes that defensible.** The whole send path is Go standard library at 1.26.5: `crypto/ecdh` parses the subscription's `p256dh` directly, `crypto/hkdf` has been stdlib since 1.24, `crypto/aes`+`crypto/cipher` do the GCM, `crypto/ecdsa` signs the JWT. `go.mod`, `go.sum` and `components.lock` are byte-unchanged and `golang.org/x/crypto` keeps its argon2-only role. **`webpush-go` v1.4.0 was never reached for**, so its REPORT is simply that the fallback stayed unused. What answers the crypto-implementation risk is that **RFC 8291 Appendix A publishes a complete worked example**, so `webpush_test.go` pins every intermediate against a number the platform did not produce — ecdh_secret → PRK_key → key_info → IKM → PRK → cek_info/CEK → nonce_info/NONCE → the 86-octet header → the final ciphertext — and then decrypts a freshly sealed body back as a receiver, on random keys, through the SAME `deriveKeys` the sender uses rather than a second copy that could agree with a bug. **Probed three ways** by breaking production code: swapping the HKDF extract's salt and secret fires; reversing key_info's `ua_public || as_public` fires on the ciphertext; `SignASN1` in place of `FillBytes` fires on the signature length. **CORRECTED (drain r1, D9): the first of those was described as firing on `PRK_key`, and it does not.** Measured: it fires on the `deriveKeys` comparison and on the final ciphertext, because the three HKDF CALLS in the step-by-step walk go through the test's own helpers — they pin the RFC's published numbers, not the production call order. The three derivation LABELS *are* production constants and are asserted directly (changing `keyInfoPrefix` or `cekInfo` fires steps 3 and 6 by name, measured). Both halves are real; describing the first as if it were the second is the inert-probe class in a document a reader relies on, and the assertion site now says which is which. Crypto that passes against its own output is worthless, and none of these could.
  - **THE CLASSIC SILENT FAILURE IS THE ONE THIS FILE EXISTS TO AVOID.** JWS ES256 is a raw 64-octet R‖S pair; `ecdsa.SignASN1` produces a DER SEQUENCE that is a *valid signature of the same message*, so it round-trips locally and every push service on earth rejects it. `vapidJWT` assembles the halves with `big.Int.FillBytes` into two fixed 32-octet slots, and the test verifies **through the split a push service performs** — with a DER signature driven through that same verifier and refused, plus a truncated-DER case, plus 64 repeats so a short R or S (roughly one time in 256) cannot pass unnoticed.
- **OQ2 — migration 0021, `/api/push`, metadata-only reads, dead-means-removed.** `push_subscriptions` is owner-CHECK'd with `UNIQUE (user_id, endpoint)`, which is what makes a re-subscribe a REPLACE rather than a second device — the browser hands back the endpoint it already holds, and the answer says `replaced`. **THE ENDPOINT IS A CAPABILITY URL** — anyone holding one can push to that device through the vendor relay — so it is stored, used, and **never served to anybody, the operator included**; `endpoint_hash` is the reference every read surface, every event payload and every log line uses instead. The operator's read is the **household** roster as metadata (the §30 runs/telemetry posture: which devices the notifier may reach is platform machinery, not personal content), a member's is their own, and an unknown identity matches nothing — all three driven at the store and over HTTP. A 404/410 from a push service means the subscription no longer exists there, so the row is REMOVED with a `push.unsubscribed` carrying `reason: push_service_gone`; a 500 is a refusal that leaves the row alone, driven as the control.
  - **REPORTED — a NEW S15.2 FAMILY ROOT.** The family table has no push row: S15.11 names the channel and the payload contract and no root, no owner column, no storage. `/api/push` lands additive-first under S15.2's own contract RULES exactly as `/api/chat` did at B6-7, and a cosmetic table amendment naming the row joins the B6 gate list. The executor never edits `Spec/`.
- **OQ3 — evaluation in `internal/api`, storage and crypto in the leaf `internal/push`, driven by the shell.** "Which cards are pending for identity X" and "how many" are the per-scope projector derivations that already exist here; a second SQL derivation of the same answer elsewhere is the §40-C D3 twin hazard, and it would surface as the badge and the queue disagreeing about what is waiting. So `handleApprovalList` and the notifier now share **one** `rankedApprovals`, and `internal/push` holds only what this package must not.
- **OQ4 — the class comes from the card's OWN stamp; the cadences are read LIVE.** A card is safety-class **iff its snapshot carries `sla.class == "safety"`** — today exactly the S07.7 CatSafety route, which `internal/verify` stamps at card birth. The test marshals a REAL `verify.Card` value, so the key path and the constant are the producer's own and a rename there fails here rather than silently reclassifying every safety escalation. Everything unstamped is approval-class, **including a watchdog flag-now card**: it is urgent in the watchdog's own alert vocabulary and carries no SLA, and inventing one client-side would be exactly the fabrication this phase spent four rounds removing. The producer-side stamp is the operator's to direct (gate note). The three ⚙ keys are read **at evaluation**, so an operator changing one moves the whole inbox — which is what the registry's own "inbox-wide" help text means — and the stamped block stays display data. **(i)** approval-class pushes at ⚙ `verification.card_push_hours` pending and **every further** `card_push_hours` unanswered; **(ii)** `card_remind_hours` 4 h is the INBOX'S OWN staleness marking at v0 and no separate reminder channel is built — it is read so a broken registry is loud, and the notifier does not push at 4 h.
- **OQ5 — the badge IS the inbox's ranked list.** It is `len(rankedApprovals(...))` for that identity, taken **before** the read surface's page bound, because a badge counts what is waiting and not what fits on a page — a capped badge would be a silent cap on a number. Glance agreement is driven against the served `GET /api/approvals` body, and the probe (a plausible constant `1`) fires naming both figures.
- **OQ6 — the minimal push-only service worker is ADMITTED, and this discharges the parked B6-4 SW decision (2026-07-29).** Declarative Web Push is Apple-only, so S15.11's own "Android is standard push" limb requires a service-worker receiver: outside Safari there is no way to hold a subscription without one. `web/public/sw.js` has **no `fetch` handler and may never have one** — every hazard the no-SW posture excluded (a cached shell posing as live data, a deploy that does not take effect on reload, stale assets) belongs to fetch interception. **The cold-launch-offline answer is therefore the browser's own error page**, which is the honest unreachable state S15.12 asks for; there is no offline shell at v0 and the drill OBSERVES that rather than this file asserting it. **ONE COMPOSER SERVES BOTH PATHS**: the server never branches on the recipient — it could not, since a subscription says nothing about what will render it — and the worker is the imperative renderer of the identical JSON.
  - **The file ships verbatim from `web/public`** — no bundler entry, no plugin, no dependency — which is exactly the kind of file that rots unwatched. So the tests **load that file** (`import.meta.glob('../public/sw.js')`, handlers captured off `self`) rather than a copy of its logic, and the escape scan was widened to cover `web/public/*.js` for the same reason.
- **OQ7 — the enrolling origin is recorded per subscription.** `navigate` must be absolute and the control plane binds loopback behind the S01.4 front chain, so it cannot see the origin a person reaches it by; the enrolling page can. It is format-checked server-side (https, or http on loopback — the secure-context rule push itself enforces), stored as a bare ORIGIN with path and query stripped, and it is the prefix of every deep link that device is sent.
- **OQ8 — VAPID custody is control-plane-side at v0, and that is an accepted interim with a NAMED gate item.** The key lives at `<state>/vapid-key.pem`, 0600, written through `O_EXCL` so two processes racing at first boot cannot both believe they created it. Moving custody to the credential broker — the git-signing-key posture — is a hardening-session item: it needs a new broker operation and a secrets-at-rest placement, both sudo-adjacent. The JWT cadence is one signature per push service per several hours, so nothing about the design fights the move. **ROTATION IS DOCUMENTED, NOT AUTOMATED**, and the reason is not laziness: rotating invalidates EVERY subscription in the household, because each browser subscribed with the old public key. A platform that rotated on a timer would silently stop notifying everyone.
- **OQ9 — three types under the Platform family, and FAILURE IS A FIELD.** `push.subscribed` / `push.unsubscribed` / `push.sent`, all ADMIT into family 12 under the same OQ2-(A) broadened reading that homes `worker.*`, `registry.*`, `preview.*`, `local.*` and `chat.*`. No new family, so no S00.9 amendment. A `push.send_failed` sibling was rejected: one act lands one row, and a second type would double-mint the act's shape and force every reader to union two types to answer "when did this card last go out" — **which is the question the dueness derivation asks of these rows**. The row therefore has two duties, and that is deliberate. Inventory **99/5/104 → 102 minted / 5 declare-only / 107 registered**, with `producerTypes()`, both `TestInventoryTotals` pins, the required-field goldens and the third registry-size pin (`internal/history/importwall_test.go`) all moved in the same commit.
- **OQ10 — an owned "This device" panel beside the generated settings form.** Push enrolment is per-DEVICE state living in the browser and in a table, not a ⚙ registry key, so the panel **renders no ⚙ key at all** and §43-B's no-hand-built-registry-control rule is untouched. A dedicated route was rejected: it would grow the URL contract for one control. **Nothing runs on mount that could ask for permission** — a prompt must come from a user gesture, so `enrol` is called from a click handler and from nowhere else, and that negative is driven.
- **OQ11 — tests where a mechanism can carry it, a dated checklist where a judgement cannot.** See the sweep below.
- **OQ12 — VERBATIM UTC is the recorded v0 policy, and the relative/local question goes to the gate.** Every stamp the platform serves is UTC RFC3339 and reformatting one is a transformation of a fact. Uniformity is now checked rather than believed: **only `parts.tsx` renders a `<time>` element**, no app file calls `toLocaleString`/`toLocaleDateString`/`toLocaleTimeString`/`Intl.DateTimeFormat`, and the ONE local-time conversion in the tree is named — `localMidnightISO` in `Filters.tsx`, which composes a REQUEST parameter and renders nothing (§42-B). A relative presentation beside the instant is real operator taste and is a **click-through question**, not a decision this packet takes.
- **OQ13 — `P3/runbooks/week-one-push-drill.md`, and NO guided script.** The hand-steps rule triggers on shell work; this is a phone ceremony plus observation with zero commands in it, so what it needs is zero-choice numbered steps, a results form, and the platform facts with their dates — which is what it has.
- **OQ14 — A then B, in one sitting, both green.** Part A landed as its own commit at the sanctioned seam.

### The notifier: no tickers means no COUNTDOWNS, not no loops

- **DUENESS DERIVES FROM STORED STATE, ALWAYS.** Three inputs and no fourth: the card's own `ObservedTS`, the ⚙ cadences read live, and **the last push for that card read from the event log**. There is no side table (`push_subscriptions` is the only push table and it holds devices, not clocks, asserted by a schema query) and nothing this process remembers between calls. `pushDue` is a pure function so it can be driven exhaustively without a database, which is also what makes it reviewable.
- **RESTART AND SUSPEND SAFETY IS DRIVEN, NOT ASSERTED.** A brand-new store and a brand-new server over the same database answer identically inside a cadence, resume the re-ping after it, and pick up a card **born while the platform was down** on the very next pass — which a wall-clock countdown could not do, and which is the exact failure the dead-man loop's own comment warns about.
- **EVERY ATTEMPT SETS THE CLOCK, including a refusal.** If a failed send left a card due, an unreachable push service would be re-dialled on every pass for as long as it stayed down. The cost is that a transient failure delays the next attempt by one cadence, and the runbook records that rather than leaving it to be discovered.
- **THE SHELL OWNS WHEN**, on the watchdog's own precedent, with three structural constants each carrying a different reason: `notifierTailInterval` 2 s (the EDGE trigger, so "safety escalations push immediately" does not quietly mean "at the next sweep"), `notifierSweepInterval` 5 min (the re-nag baseline — a card ages past its threshold with no event announcing it, and 5 min is far finer than the finest ratified cadence), and `notifierBurstGap` 10 s (a burst floor on the edge path only; a skipped tick does **not** advance the cursor, so nothing is dropped). **The edge trigger is "the head moved", deliberately, rather than a list of card-opening types**: such a list would be a third copy of what the inbox derivation already knows about which producers open a card, and it would fail silently by omission the day a new producer lands. "Something happened, so re-derive" is the frontend's own rule applied server-side, and the evaluation is idempotent so a trigger that opened nothing sends nothing.
- **IDEMPOTENCE IS A PROPERTY OF THE LANDED PATH.** Three back-to-back evaluations send once, and they do so BECAUSE the first pass's real audit row is what the second reads. The tests use the REAL `push.Sender` against a loopback TLS `httptest` service — real encryption, real signing, real audit rows — rather than a recording double that could be written to agree.
- **A PUSH GOES ONLY TO SOMEBODY WHO CAN ANSWER THE CARD, and that is a RECORDED READING.** The operator's ranked list legitimately carries every household member's card, so pushing all of them would wake the operator every 24 h, forever, for decisions the platform itself refuses to let them answer — S15.12 routes approvals "to the decision owner (D10)" and S15.11's subject is decisions reaching the RIGHT person. The BADGE still counts the whole list (OQ5), because that is the number the inbox shows. Driven over one world with the non-tautological control that the operator's own read DOES carry the card and is `answerable: false`.
- **An EXPIRED card is never pushed** — the countdown it displayed has run out, so a notification would send somebody to a decision they can no longer make — and an answered card is not in the derivation at all. Both driven, with a card one day younger as the control.

### The payload, and what leaves this machine

- **The declarative contract, exactly** (W3C Push API §3.3, Working Draft 2025-12-01): `web_push: 8030` and `notification{title, navigate}` required; `app_badge` beside them; `mutable` deliberately ABSENT so the Apple leg renders directly. Headers: `Content-Encoding: aes128gcm`, `Content-Type: application/notification+json`, `TTL`, `Urgency`, `Topic`, `Authorization: vapid t=…, k=…`. All asserted from what ARRIVED at the fake service and was decrypted there — the only reading that proves the encryption, the headers and the contract together.
- **THE TTL IS THE CLASS'S OWN CADENCE**, not an invented number: a message the push service could not deliver before the next one is due has been superseded, and delivering a stale nag after a fresh one is worse than dropping it. So no ⚙ key and no constant is needed for it. `Topic` is a hash of the card id (24 octets of sha256 → exactly 32 base64url characters, Apple's documented ceiling), which coalesces a re-nag onto the notification already on the device and leaks nothing.
- **NOTHING IN THE PAYLOAD IS LIFTED FROM A CARD.** The title is content-light platform vocabulary, `navigate` is the subscription's own origin plus a composed path, the icon is self-hosted, the tag is the card id and the badge is a count — the composer has no access to a snapshot at all. Driven as a property of the WIRE with a planted secret-shaped set, plus the control that the payload does carry its own composed fields, so "no hits" means "nothing leaked" rather than "nothing was sent".
- **REGISTER ROW 2 IS A CHECKABLE NEGATIVE.** `internal/push`'s production code contains **no absolute URL at all** — asserted by an AST scan over string literals (so prose citing a URL is not a hit and a concatenated one still is), with planted probes in both directions. The only address anything dials is `sub.Endpoint`, out of a row a person's own browser enrolled. The register itself is spec-owned and untouched; its operator sign-off stands as a gate TBD.
- **A silent cap is impossible on this path:** an oversized sealed payload is REFUSED with its bound named and audited, never truncated — a shortened ciphertext does not decrypt, so the device would get nothing while the log said sent.

### `navigate` ↔ the router: a cross-language agreement with a golden tie

`navigate` is composed SERVER-side and the URL it must match is produced CLIENT-side by `hrefFor('inbox-item', {id})`, which encodes with JavaScript's `encodeURIComponent`. **Go's `url.PathEscape` is a different rule** — it leaves `:` alone and escapes a different mark set — so using it would send people to a URL the router resolves to another card or to none. `encodeURIComponentJS` implements the JavaScript rule byte for byte, `internal/api` writes the composed paths into `push-navigate.json` for ten real id shapes (including `:`, `#`, a unit separator, the seven unescaped marks, `/?&=+ `, non-ASCII and `%`), and the web suite round-trips each through `matchRoute` for the EXACT id **and** re-composes it through `hrefFor`. The Go side additionally proves the divergence is real: if `url.PathEscape` agreed on `ask:x`, the test fails as unable to catch the substitution it exists for.

### The S15.12 sweep, and what it found

- **R17 — "the SPA consumes every API" is a comparison of two INDEPENDENTLY PRODUCED lists.** `Handler()` now records each pattern as it registers it (`Server.Routes()`), so the server's list is written by the registration calls themselves and no hand-kept inventory exists to compare against itself — the tautology B6-8 shipped once, which hid a live defect. The client's list is extracted from what the app SOURCES **CALL** — corrected in place at drain r2 (R1), where "name" was the whole defect: outside `api.ts` a path literal counted whether or not anything called it — with comments stripped (a file may explain a route it does not call) and `web/public/sw.js` included, because the worker is a real API client. **85 routes, 80 session-required.** A control asserts the recorded list IS the mux's own by asking every literal GET for an answer and requiring it not to be `http.ServeMux`'s own `404 page not found\n` body — with the opposite direction proved on a path that is not registered. Probed three ways: a new route with no consumer fires; an exception that becomes consumed fires; and the SPA ceasing to name `/api/workforce` anywhere fires.
- **REPORTED — 13 GAPS, labelled as gaps rather than hidden among the exemptions.** Nine routes are sanctioned exceptions with reasons (verify-at-act needs no standalone PIN verify; device grants are administration with no ratified UI; the three B2-4 walking-skeleton verbs are superseded; the standalone receipt is served inside the task detail; Layer 2 is reached through a chat turn so its audit row exists). The other **thirteen are real findings and are carried to the B6 gate**:
  - **the whole S15.2 `memory` family has NO SPA surface** (5 routes). Its only consumed edge is the ninth inbox kind's resolve verb. S15's own surface list names no memory browser, so this is a family ROW without a surface rather than an omission inside a built view.
  - **feature 4.5 CANCEL has no control** — `POST /api/runs/{run}/cancel` and `/api/tasks/{task}/cancel` are landed, owner-scoped and unreachable from any surface.
  - **the S10.4 budget editor and the 3.3 pause switch have no controls** — which is why every budget reads UNDECLARED today, honestly, on a fleet surface that offers no way to declare one.
  - **the S13.9 follow-up door is SHOWN AND NOT PRESSABLE** — the review surface serves and renders the door, its route and its `revision` preset, and offers no control that calls it.
  - **the BENCH-REG §4.2.1 opt-in has no control**, so nothing makes somebody a participant.
  - **the S14.10 `ask` and `search` layers have no callers** — `ask` because the assistant routes by GESTURE by ratified design (§44 OQ3), `search` because no surface offers a search box.
  - **DATED CROSS-NOTE 2026-08-05 (P3-UI-2, §48): FOUR of these thirteen are CLOSED and the pins moved 14 → 10 routes over 13 → 9 shapes.** Feature 4.5's two cancel verbs are consumed by the task detail (a state-computed task-level control and a per-run one); the S10.4 budget editor and the 3.3 pause switch are consumed by the fleet. Their four exception entries were REMOVED from the list rather than annotated — the sweep's own stale-entry test forces that the moment a surface calls a route, which is the half of the instrument that keeps the list honest in both directions. The record above is left as it was written, because it was true when it was written; this line is what makes it current.
