### Live-verified facts this code depends on (all re-verified 2026-07-30, and three brief corrections)

Declarative Web Push shipped and unchanged on Apple platforms only (webkit.org/blog/16535 and /16923; nothing in the Safari 26.x or 27-beta posts touches push); no Chromium feature entry; Firefox bugs 1935325 and 1946085 both status NEW. The payload contract is W3C Push API §3.3 (WD 2025-12-01) with `web_push: 8030`, `notification.title` and `notification.navigate` required. Apple: TTL required and positive, Urgency from a closed four-value set, Topic ≤32 base64url characters, 4 KB payload cap, JWT `exp` ≤ one day, refresh no more than once per hour, and no Developer Program membership needed. `window.pushManager` is the shipped declarative surface; `userVisibleOnly: true` is rejected-without by Chrome and Edge; Safari revokes permission for an invisible push. Chromium install criteria still want 192px and 512px icons. Home Screen installation remains a hard prerequisite for any web push on iOS as of iOS 26; classic push floor 16.4, declarative 18.4.

**Three corrections to the brief's carried facts, recorded because a premise that is only accidentally right is not a premise:**

1. **`app_badge` is a WebKit EXTENSION and appears nowhere in the W3C draft** (full spec text checked). The brief called it "absent from the WD text", which is right; what is worth adding is that it is a **string** inside `notification` — WebKit's own shipped example is `"app_badge": "1"` — and that is the shape the platform sends. Non-Apple devices get the badge through the standard Badging API from the same field.
2. **`application/notification+json` is a WebKit PROPOSAL, not normative.** The W3C draft contains no `Content-Type` at all. It is sent because it is the documented interop lever, and the code says so rather than implying it is spec.
3. **Apple's JWT rules are TWO different rules**, and the brief's "exp ≤ 24 h, refresh ≤ once/hour" is right precisely because it keeps them apart. The refusal is for an expiry "more than one day into the future"; the once-an-hour figure is a refresh-rate FLOOR. Conflating them produces either rejected tokens or needless re-signing, which is why `vapidExpiry` and `vapidRenewMargin` are two constants with two reasons.

An independent evaluation returned FAIL with fourteen findings; all fourteen are actioned. **It closed the packet's highest-stakes question by re-deriving it rather than reading it**: it fetched RFC 8291 Appendix A from two sources and wrote its own stdlib-only program with zero repo code, recomputing every intermediate from the published private keys — they match. - **D1 — HIGH: THE RAW CAPABILITY LEAKED INTO EVERY FAILED SEND'S AUDIT ROW.** `*url.Error` from `http.Client.Do` **always** embeds the URL it was handed, and `attempt` returned `err.Error()` straight into `sendEvent.Detail`. Reproduced on the production path: the payload carried `"detail":"Post \"https://…/push/alice-phone\": dial tcp …: connection refused"`. **A transport failure is not an edge case — it is the ORDINARY shape of a failed send** (a sleeping host, a dropped tailnet), so this was the commonest failure writing the one value migration 0021, OQ2, OQ9, `contract.go` and this package's own doc comment all say never leaves. The tests missed it because the only detail-bearing assertion covered a 500, where the detail comes from the response BODY.
  - **Fixed at the ONE boundary where a detail becomes a record**, not at each producer: `Send` scrubs before the audit row and before returning, so the second route in — a push service echoing the request URL back in its own error body — is closed by the same line. `scrubDetail` removes every scheme-bearing URL (greedy to the end, because the secret is the PATH, not the host) and keeps the cap. **CORRECTED at drain r2 (R2): that second claim held for SCHEME-BEARING echoes only** — `urlShaped` requires `://`, so `"path":"/push/…"` and `host/path` both survived. The scrub takes the attempt's own endpoint now and removes its scheme-less spellings too. What survives is the classification a drill actually needs: `dial tcp …: connection refused`, `BadJwtToken`.
  - Driven on the transport path specifically, over the WHOLE row rather than the field, with the control that the detail is not merely emptied. **Probe: revert the scrub and it fires naming the endpoint, the path and the scheme.**
- **D2 — MEDIUM-HIGH: the badge was never reconciled, and the packet's own runbook would have failed on it.** Nothing in `web/src` wrote a badge; the only writer was the service worker's push handler. So after somebody answered their cards the badge held its last PUSHED count for up to a full cadence — and the drill's step 13 checks the badge against the queue immediately after step 11 answers a card, with §3 making it an acceptance criterion. OQ5's glance agreement held only at the instant of composition, which is not what OQ5 says.
  - **`reconcileBadge` writes from the SERVED count**, in the two surfaces that already hold it: the inbox list and the deep-link item surface — the second being where a tapped notification lands and where the drill's own measurement happens. #### §46 drain round 2 (P3-B6-9 drain r2, R1–R3 + R5 — FINAL round under the cap)

Three residuals survived drain r1's re-check, and **two of them share one signature: a fix applied where somebody looked rather than everywhere the defect lives.** All three are closed; none was refused. Every fix carries a check that FAILS on the pre-fix code, verified by reverting it and watching the assertion fire, and the probe is named per item.

- **R1 — MEDIUM: the consumption detector was fixed in `api.ts` ONLY, so in every other app file PRESENCE still meant CONSUMPTION.** D5 made a route count only where something calls `api.<member>(` — but that rule governed `api.ts`'s literals alone. `routesInFreeText`'s final loop still read any unclaimed path literal in any other file as a `GET` consumption, called or not, across roughly twenty files. **Reproduced decisively in two steps:** removing the genuine `/api/workforce` consumption from both real sites made the sweep fire the route as unexplained (correct), and then adding a single never-called `const EVAL_DEAD = '/api/workforce'` to `Fleet.tsx` returned it to green. **A dead string re-hid a real gap** — on the packet's own headline deliverable, and this is the under-reporting class that is worse than not running the check at all, because it will be believed at a gate.
  - **CONSUMPTION IS A CALL IN EVERY FILE NOW, BY TWO DIFFERENT CALLABLE UNITS, and the difference is the point.** In `api.ts` the unit is the MEMBER — a member's literals are the routes it performs (`objectHref` composes a URL an `<img src>` reads and no `request<>` call names it), and the member counts only where an app file writes `api.<member>(`. Everywhere else the unit is the REQUEST, so `classifyFile` must show each literal reaching one. Four resolutions, each with its reason: the typed calls (`post<>`/`request<>`); a direct `fetch(…)` / `new EventSource(…)` whose argument is the literal or a same-file `const`; a **`useLive` key**, which is NOT a request and is resolved as such — `useLive` uses `key` only as an effect DEPENDENCY (§45 D5 measured exactly that, where a blanked key disabled nothing), so the request beside it is the `read` closure and the member map already counts it; and **BY FILE**, for a file whose request call takes an expression the scan cannot resolve.
  - **THE FAILURE MODE IS LOUD, WHICH IS THE HALF THAT MATTERS.** A literal that resolves to nothing is neither counted nor ignored: `unresolvedLiterals()` reports it with its file and the sweep fails. A detector that cannot resolve something says so rather than silently assuming either answer — assuming "consumed" is what hid the gap, and assuming "not consumed" would invent one.
  - **The one place presence still implies consumption is NAMED and asserted to be exactly one file.** `events.ts` opens the stream through an injectable seam — `this.make(this.url(…))`, defaulting to `new EventSource(url)` — so the literal and the constructor are one hop apart and no static resolution reaches it. Its literals count wholesale, `byFileClients()` is pinned to exactly `['./events.ts']`, and `GET /events` is asserted still consumed. A second such file fails the pin.
  - **A SECOND DEFECT FELL OUT OF IT, and it could only have been found this way.** `normalizePath` ended an interpolation at the first `}`, so `api.comments`'s `/api/deliverables/${…}/comments${query({ revision })}` normalized to **`/api/deliverables/{}/comments)}`** — a shape the server does not serve. The route looked consumed only because the `useLive` KEY beside it spelled the shape correctly by hand; the moment keys stopped counting, `GET /api/deliverables/{deliverable}/comments` surfaced as unexplained. **One check passing for another check's reason** is the shape of nearly every finding in this section. `stripInterpolations` matches braces now.
  - **THE REPORTED-GAP LIST DID NOT MOVE: still 14 routes over 13 shapes, both pins green, and the exception list is unchanged in both directions** (nothing became unexplained, nothing on the list became consumed). Every `useLive` key that stopped counting was already covered by its sibling `read` closure's `api.<member>(` call, which is why the partition is identical. Measured: **60 (method, shape) pairs consumed against an 85-route inventory, 23 key literals now explained-rather-than-counted, 0 unresolved.** **And the record stays straight on the other number:** drain r1's detector cascade added **exactly one** gap, `POST /api/memory` — a relayed summary said "three more", which was wrong; `GET /api/health` became a sanctioned non-gap exception with its reason and `POST /api/settings/prices` was never a gap.
  - **Probed three ways, each by reverting the fix and watching it fire:** the old presence rule makes the dead declaration count (`expected [ 'GET /api/workforce' ] to deeply equal []`); the evaluator's own reproduction planted in the REAL `Fleet.tsx` fires the loud report naming `./Fleet.tsx: /api/workforce`; and the old `[^}]*` interpolation rule fires both the normalizer assertion and the unexplained-route list.
- **R2 — LOW-MEDIUM: `scrubDetail` missed a scheme-LESS path, so a capability was still reconstructable from the audit row.** `urlShaped` requires `://`. Against a service echoing three shapes back in its error body the full URL was withheld and **`"path":"/push/alice-phone"` and `"hostpath":"127.0.0.1:44951/push/alice-phone"` both survived into the `push.sent` row** — reproduced on the production path before the fix. The host is discoverable, so a bare path in an audit row is a reconstructable capability: the same finding as D1, one shape further out.
  - **`Send` already held the subscription**, so the scrub takes the attempt's own endpoint and removes its scheme-less spellings — `host+path` before `path`, which contains it, and the percent-escaped spelling as well as the decoded one. The removal is by EXACT match against the one endpoint in hand rather than by shape, so it cannot eat an unrelated message; a path of one character is never removed, because `/` is every URL's. **Probe: revert the endpoint-shape removal and the driven row test fires on both shapes, plus three table cases by name.**
- **R3 — LOW: the enrolment refusal quoted the caller's value back, and there were TWO echo routes rather than one.** `POST /api/push/subscriptions` with `http://web.push.apple.com/CAPABILITY-SECRET-PATH` answered 400 with the endpoint verbatim; so did the **unparseable** case, which the residual did not name — `url.Parse` answers a `*url.Error` whose `Error()` renders as `parse "<the whole URL>": <reason>`. It is genuinely well mitigated (it fires only for endpoints the platform REFUSED, so never a stored capability; it is echoed only to the caller who supplied it; `writeSurfaceErr` does not log), so this was a habit rather than a live leak — **and it is closed anyway, because a refusal is worth more when it says what was WRONG, and a message that quotes an endpoint teaches the next reader that endpoints are quotable.** `vapidAudience` names the fault: the scheme it got, or that no host was named, or the parse error's INNER reason (`invalid URL escape "%zz"`), which names at most a fragment of what it rejected. **Not refused, and one adjacent site deliberately left alone:** `normalizeOrigin`'s three `%q` refusals keep naming the ORIGIN, because an origin is the enrolling page's own address rather than capability material and "origin X has scheme Y" is what makes them actionable; its `url.Parse` echo, which quotes the whole raw value, uses the same fault-only helper. **Probe: both limbs fired on the pre-fix code, naming the secret path.**
- **R5 — ACCEPTED, RECORDED, NOT FIXED: the `api.<member>(` predicate is syntax-fragile, and that is the SAFE direction.** Rewriting a real call as `(api).workforce.call(api, …)` — or destructuring `const { workforce } = api`, or `api?.workforce?.()` — makes `declaredButUncalled()` report `workforce`. Every one of those makes the sweep FAIL, naming the member: a loud over-report rather than a silent under-count, which is the direction a completeness check must fail in. Recorded at the assertion site as known brittleness against future destructuring or optional chaining. It is not a defect and needs no fix.

**Counters after drain r2:** unchanged except the two suites — gofmt empty · vet + build clean · **45 Go packages**, 0 failures, the same **14** pre-existing sanctioned skips (`-v` measured, none introduced) · lockgate **29 / 240 npm** · typecheck + **432 vitest / 23 files** (was 429/23) + build **976.99 kB** (gzip **292.96**, unchanged — no production web file was touched) · migrations **0001–0021**, none opened · inventory **102/5/107**, `internal/eventlog/contract.go` byte-unchanged · ⚙ **118/33**, `internal/settings/index.go` byte-unchanged · `components.lock`/`go.mod`/`go.sum`/`web/package.json`/`web/package-lock.json` byte-unchanged (the stdlib path holds; `net/url` and `slices` are stdlib) · conformance **12** · views **11**, catalog **50** · `built` routes **11** · registered routes **85**, **reported gaps 14 routes / 13 shapes — UNMOVED** · escape allowlist **EMPTY**, banned **8**, floor **50** (`escape-scan.test.ts` untouched) · **zero fixture drift** re-verified through the real regeneration path, `cursor` **86** across 21 bodies · the 18 RFC 8291 vector constants in `webpush_test.go` **byte-identical** (its only edit is the `ScrubDetailForTest` seam signature) · `Spec/`, `Docs/`, `Research/`, `P3/STATE.md` untouched. **Assertion counts per touched test file, pre-r2 → post: `send_test.go` 87→96 · `sweep.test.tsx` 61→73 · `pushapi_test.go` 29→32 · `webpush_test.go` 74→74 · `push_test.go` 68→68 · `push.test.tsx` 77→77 · `deliverable.test.tsx` 246→246 · `workforce.test.tsx` 183→183.** Nothing went down, no floor was lowered, no scan narrowed and no fixture nudged. **$0**, hermetic, nothing pushed.

**No refusals this round.** All three residuals reproduced as described before anything was changed; R1's proof turned up a second defect the report could not have seen (the interpolation normalizer), and R3 carried a second echo route the report did not name. R5 is recorded as accepted, per its finding.

#### §46 post-cap coordinator item (P3-B6-9, RES-1 — implemented inline; the drain cap was exhausted)

The final re-check returned **FAIL on a single LOW residual**, and closed everything else by re-driving it. **The claim it was told to disbelieve — "the gap list did not move" — it proved rather than accepted**, and the method is worth recording: it extracted the drain-r1 detector into a module, temporarily exported the drain-r2 one, ran both over the same sources and **diffed the consumed PAIRS rather than the totals**. Old 62, new 60; the two that left are junk and neither is a served route (`GET /api/deliverables/{}/comments${query({` — the brace bug's own output — and a concrete query id). **Zero entered. Real-route coverage 60 → 60.** So the identical answer is an exact match on real routes with only garbage removed, not two category changes cancelling. It also **generalized the normalizer bug** as directed: running the old first-brace normalizer and the new brace-matched one over every path literal in `api.ts` produced **exactly one disagreement in the whole tree**, `api.comments` — and it is not now accidental by a different route, because deleting **both** hand-written `useLive` keys from `Deliverable.tsx` leaves the sweep green through the real `api.comments(` call.

- **RES-1 — the R1 signature survived inside the one exempted file, which is the last place presence still implied consumption.** `classifyFile`'s `byFile` branch counted **every** literal in `events.ts` wholesale. Proved by the re-check: with the genuine `/api/workforce` consumption removed the sweep fires correctly, and then **one never-called `const EVAL_DEAD = '/api/workforce'` dropped inside `events.ts` returned it to 27/27 green** — a dead string re-hiding a real gap, the exact defect R1 closed everywhere else, surviving in the one place the fix deliberately declined to reach. **The fix is the one the re-check named:** `BY_FILE_LITERALS` pins the two strings a by-file client may have counted for it (`/events` and `/events?${qs}` — that file's own SSE route), so the exemption now says both **which file** may resolve by expression and **which strings** it may resolve; anything else in it falls through to `unresolvedLiterals()` and fails the sweep loudly with its filename. **Probe: with the re-check's exact dead line planted in the real `web/src/events.ts`, the sweep fires `expected [ './events.ts: /api/workforce' ] to deeply equal []`; reverted, 27/27 green.** The one-file pin stays and still fires on a second by-file client — the two guards now compose rather than one covering for the other.
- **What this item can and cannot claim.** It was implemented after the cap, so **no fresh adversarial pass reviewed it** — but it is confined to the sweep's own detector, it carries a probe that fails on the pre-fix code, and the fix was specified by the pass that found it rather than invented afterwards. Two of the three post-cap items across B6-8 and B6-9 have now carried a failing probe; part A's five could not, and said so.
- **Counters at landing, measured by the coordinator:** gofmt empty · vet + build clean · `go test ./... -count=1` **45 packages, 0 failures**, with **14 sanctioned pre-existing env-gated skips — the correct number, not zero** (`--- SKIP` counted directly; the "0 skips" figure carried in earlier records this phase was asserted from output that never counted them, and is corrected here) · lockgate **29 / 240 npm** · typecheck + **432 vitest / 23 files** + build **976.99 kB** (gzip **292.96**) · **zero fixture drift** through the real regeneration path · migrations **0001–0021** · inventory **102 minted / 5 declare-only** · ⚙ **118 keys** with `internal/settings/index.go` byte-unchanged · frozen paths byte-verified against the pre-packet commit `c10b77a` (`index.go`, `go.mod`, `go.sum`, `components.lock`, `web/package.json`, `web/package-lock.json`, `internal/benchmark/registered.go` — **all unchanged, which is the stdlib path of OQ1 confirmed at the lock rather than claimed**). **$0**, hermetic, **zero pushes left this machine**, no host change.

## 47. The design foundation: styling substrate, the token pour, bundled type & the shell restyle (P3-UI-1; S15.1, S15.3–S15.4, FC-v1, S16.2–S16.4, §41+§41-B, §42)

The first packet of the UI batch. Its design authority is the operator-approved `P3/design/design-approach-proposal.md` (approved 2026-08-04, free text in its §6), **subordinate to the spec on all behavior** — and this packet changed **no** behavior: API contracts, events, scoping and routes are untouched, `routes.ts` is byte-unchanged, and no surface component's data consumption moved.

- **The substrate, through the rail.** `tailwindcss` + `@tailwindcss/vite` **4.3.3** enter as devDependencies with ONE `kind: toolchain` lock entry (they release in lockstep; they split the day the live versions differ). Tailwind is a **compiler**: the plugin reads `@import "tailwindcss"` in `index.css` and emits only the utilities the sources use. No Tailwind code is reachable from the binary, which serves compiled assets alone — so §41's embed/serve posture is untouched and its "No CSS framework" sentence is superseded **datedly, in place**, never silently. **The runtime set is CLOSED and was fixed by the proposal:** `@base-ui/react` 1.7.0, `lucide-react` 1.28.0, `clsx` 2.1.1, `tailwind-merge` 3.6.0, `class-variance-authority` 0.7.1, `tw-animate-css` 1.4.0, `@fontsource-variable/inter` + `@fontsource/jetbrains-mono` 5.3.0. Every pin was **re-verified live against registry.npmjs.org at adoption** (version, licence, deprecation, and package NAME — `@base-ui/react` has been renamed once already); **CORRECTED 2026-08-04 (drain r1): ten of the eleven carried a research-time pin and all ten matched exactly, so nothing drifted. The eleventh, `@fontsource/jetbrains-mono`, had NO research-time version to match** — the sourcing doc named the package without one and the brief's adoption table recorded it as “live” — so for it the registry read at adoption IS the pin, 5.3.0, rather than a confirmation of anything. Saying “all eleven matched” claimed a check that could not have been performed. That fetch is the packet's one network act, $0.
- **The shadcn CLI is a GENERATOR, never a runtime dependency** (OQ1(a)): exact-pinned devDependency + `kind: toolchain` entry, the Vitest precedent, so UI-2..7 can generate reproducibly. `web/components.json` and the `@/*` alias (mirrored in `vite.config.ts` and `tsconfig.app.json`) are its sanctioned scaffold mechanics. **RECORDED FINDING — the reason this packet's kit is hand-written:** at 4.16.1 `shadcn add` resolves items by STYLE (`/r/styles/<style>/<item>.json`) and every addressable style resolves to the **Radix** track — a dry run of `add button` declares a `radix-ui` dependency, which is outside the closed set and named NOT-ADOPTED. `--base` is an `init`-only flag, and the config value that reports `base: base` (style `base-ui`) is not an addressable registry style. So nothing was installed and nothing was generated. **UI-2..7 must re-seat any generated component's `radix-ui` imports onto the pinned `@base-ui/react` before it lands, or hand-write it** — and `radix-ui` is never installed to make a generator's output compile.
- **The alias is resolved from the working directory, not `import.meta.url`.** The harness imports `vite.config.ts` through Vite's own transform to assert the dev-proxy rules, and there `import.meta.url` is not a file URL. Every invocation that reads the config (`vite`, `vite build`, `vitest`) runs with `web/` as its working directory, which is also the config's root. `devproxy.test.ts` stays unmodified and green.
- **The token pour, and the collision it forced.** `index.css` defines the shadcn base set on `:root` **from the Nexus values** — `#07070d` base, the violet-tinted translucent `rgba(148,148,190,α)` neutral family (one material everywhere, never plain gray), `#7c5cff` primary with the `#7c5cff → #22d3ee` gradient as identity, the `#eaeaf4`/`#9a9ab2`/`#5e5e78` text ramp, the 14px/9px radius pair — plus the Sinet extensions shadcn has no name for (six status hues, `--grad`/`--grad-soft`, `--accent-glow`, shadow and blur tiers, `--sidebar-w`, the aurora hues). **Dark-first:** the dark values sit directly on `:root` with `color-scheme: dark`; no light ramp is built and a half-built one would be worse than none. **REPORTED CONFLICT, resolved rather than papered over:** two landed token names — `--accent` and `--muted` — are also shadcn base names with *incompatible* meanings (landed: brand violet and dimmed **text**; shadcn: a hover **surface** and a muted **surface**). Both cannot sit on `:root` at once. The resolution is that **`@theme inline` decouples the utility name from the variable name**: `--accent`/`--muted` keep their landed meanings (which is what re-bases every landed surface with zero structural edits), the shadcn surface semantics live on `--accent-surface`/`--muted-surface`, and `--color-accent`/`--color-muted` are bound to *those* — so `bg-accent` means what shadcn means while `var(--accent)` means what this stylesheet has always meant. `--color-brand` exposes the identity violet as a utility. Without this, a later primitive using `bg-accent` would have rendered solid-violet hovers and lavender "muted" fills.
- **The legacy nine are re-pointed, not frozen** (the coordinator's ratified reading): `--bg --panel --fg --muted --line --accent --ok --warn --bad` keep their names and meanings and take the new values, so every surface built before this packet re-bases onto the Nexus language without one structural edit and each sheds its own CSS in its own later packet. Freezing them would have shipped a two-palette app. A test asserts both halves — the names survive **and** none of the nine pre-packet values is left anywhere in the sheet — because either alone passes for the wrong reason.
- **New code references tokens and utilities, never raw hex.** Raw hex lives in the `:root` token block and nowhere else; a ramp is derived with `color-mix()` (the connection pill's chip colours are the worked example: `color-mix(in srgb, var(--green) 9%, transparent)` is the one chip formula, expressed once, from a token).
- **Type is bundled, never fetched.** Inter (variable weight axis) for prose and **JetBrains Mono for every number, id, timestamp and status token**, with `tabular-nums` — imported as package CSS from `main.tsx` so Vite bundles the `.woff2` files into `dist/assets` under content hashes and the binary embeds them. Nexus and Odysseus both reached for the Google Fonts CDN; this platform must not, and the built `dist` is grepped for any external **asset** reference — `src=`, `href=`, `url()` — to prove it. **The claim is about ASSETS, and a bare `https?://` grep can never be clean on a React production build — recorded here so no future packet re-litigates it (drain r1).** The shipped chunk legitimately carries non-fetching external URL LITERALS that arrive with the pinned picks and predate this packet: React's minified-error links (`react.dev/errors/`), a Redux error link, JSON-Schema `$id` identifiers, and `w3.org` XML/SVG/MathML **namespace constants** — which are identifiers rather than addresses and are never dereferenced. None is an asset reference; the asset-shaped grep returns empty, and that is the checkable form of “zero CDN”. Honest measurement rather than a silent cost: of the 417.30 kB of font assets — **15 files, CORRECTED 2026-08-04 (drain r1): 7 Inter woff2 + 4 JetBrains Mono woff2 + 4 JetBrains Mono woff. The landing text said 16; the SUM was right and the COUNT was wrong** — the four `.woff` fallbacks (112.07 kB) and the five non-latin Inter subsets (85.17 kB) are **bundled but never served** to this platform's readers — the packages expose no finer entry point, and this is named in the lock entry's watch rows as a tightening candidate rather than left to be discovered.
- **Motion is gated twice, on purpose.** Every animation the stylesheet starts is authored inside `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference)` — so a reduce reader gets the **static composition** (a still aurora, a solid dot) rather than an animation started and then clamped — and a global `reduce` kill switch neutralizes animation, transition and scroll behaviour outright as the backstop that catches anything a later packet forgets, including `tw-animate-css` utilities. A structural test extracts the gate blocks, lists every `animation:` outside them, and carries a planted probe in both directions.
- **The kit's motion is authored-gated too, and scanned where it lives (drain r1, D4/D7).** The stylesheet's animations are gated in the stylesheet and checked by `design.test.ts`; the KIT starts its motion from Tailwind utilities instead, which that detector cannot see because they never appear in `index.css`. So the same rule is enforced at the one place the kit can express it: **every `transition-*` and `animate-*` utility in `web/src/ui` carries `motion-safe:`** — the Modal overshoot, the Drawer slide, the Toast entry/exit, the Button and Panel hover transitions and the Skeleton sweep — asserted by a scan over the kit sources with a planted probe in both directions. The global `reduce` kill switch stays the backstop; this is the authored gate the proposal asks for, so a reduce reader gets the static composition rather than an animation clamped to nothing. **The two detectors' scopes are therefore complementary and neither is redundant:** `design.test.ts` owns stylesheet-declared motion, `ui/kit.test.tsx` owns utility-declared motion.
- **The skeleton SHIMMERS, as the proposal says, and the sweep is why it is still not a figure (drain r1, D7).** A band of the panel neutral travels across the block on a gated `skeleton-shimmer` keyframe. It was a pulse at landing, which was not what the design authority specifies. The sweep is also the safer shape: a travelling band never stops anywhere, so unlike a filling bar it cannot be misread as a position — the figure-free requirement is met by the mechanism, not only by the absence of text.
- **One breakpoint, not two (drain r1, D8).** The Drawer widened at Tailwind's `sm:` (40rem) at landing, which introduced a second responsive seam beside the shell's own 48rem. It now widens at `md:` — 48rem, the landed breakpoint — so the sheet becomes a 520px panel at exactly the width the sidebar appears, and full-width below it.
- **Density is two root classes and nothing else.** `density-comfortable` (the default, applied on `<html>`, and its values also sit on `:root` so a tree that never receives the class still renders correctly) and `density-compact` switch the same `--density-*` spacing scale — Nexus's density comes from small type over roomy boxes, so compact tightens the boxes and leaves the type ramp alone. **No persistence** (web storage is banned by §41-B and a stored preference would need a server-side home that does not exist), **no switcher control**, **no ⚙ key invented**. A test asserts both blocks declare the *same* variable names with *different* values — a name in one and not the other is a value silently falling back.
- **The shell restyle.** One fixed `aria-hidden`, `pointer-events:none` aurora field (four radial gradients at 5–13% opacity) behind everything; a blurred sidebar carrying the gradient logo mark and the grouped nav; a blurred topbar carrying the connection pill, the who-line and Sign out; scrolling content. **Grouping is presentation and cannot reorder or drop a link:** `navGroupOf` maps a route id to a label and the sections are the *consecutive runs* of that label over the table's own nav order, so every navigable route is walked exactly once, in table order, and one with no label still renders in its own unlabelled run. `routes.ts` is byte-unchanged and the landed assertion that the rendered hrefs equal `routes.filter(nav).map(pattern)` passes **unmodified** — which is what proves the claim.
- **Phone-first holds through the restyle** (§41-B): the same markup is a wrapping band above the content at 375px and a `--sidebar-w` column only inside the `min-width: 48rem` query; no layout container pins a pixel width at phone width (`.shell-side`, `.shell-body` and `.nav-group` joined the asserted list); the connection LABEL is never hidden.
- **Preflight compatibility, ledgered.** Tailwind's preflight zeroes the browser type rhythm the landed per-surface sections were written against, so four owned base rules give heading, paragraph and list rhythm back. They are compatibility, not design, and they leave with the last surface section.
- **The primitive kit — one home, `web/src/ui/`, with `cn()` in `web/src/lib/utils.ts`.** The export contract UI-2..7 build on, fixed here (a rename after this packet is a recorded deviation, not a drift): `Button` (variant primary | secondary | ghost | danger, size sm | md), `Panel` (optional `head`), `Chip` (tone), `StatusDot` (tone, `live`), `StatTile` (label/value/icon/tone/foot), `Modal`, `Drawer`, `Skeleton`, `EmptyState` (`what` + `why`), `Timestamp` (variant live | audit), `ToastProvider`/`useToast`, `cn`, and the shared `Tone`/`tones`/`toneStyle`. Every component and every variant is RENDERED in the harness — S16.4 #5 is behavioural, and a variant nobody renders is a class string nobody has checked.
- **Hand-written on the ratified Base UI track, styled with utilities.** The kit declares NO global class names, so it cannot collide with a landed selector — `.chip` and `.panel` both already exist in the sheet with their own meanings, and the harvest warned about exactly that. `Modal`, `Drawer` and the toast stack ride `@base-ui/react` for the things a control room should not re-implement (focus trap, escape stack, portal, live region, ARIA); the look is ours.
- **The one chip formula, written once.** A tone is a TOKEN NAME, never a colour: `toneStyle` binds `--tone` to `var(--<tone>)` and one string — `text-(--tone)` over `color-mix(…9%…)` fill and `color-mix(…25%…)` border — serves all seven. A test asserts every tone emits the SAME class string, so a hue that grew its own rule fails.
- **Two deliberate absences, both asserted.** `StatTile` has **no count-up**: Nexus animated tiles from zero, and for the seconds that runs the screen shows a figure the platform never served — whether that is admissible against the no-fabricated-numbers invariant is a surface decision, not a kit default. `Skeleton` is a shape and never a figure: no text, no fraction, no horizon, because the API serves none (§42). The kit adds no progress, percentage or ETA primitive and the landed scans still say so.
- **Toasts cap at four, and nothing was installed to get them.** `@base-ui/react`'s toast provider carries the live region, the hover pause and the stacking; `limit={4}` marks the overflow `data-limited` rather than dropping it, so nothing is silently lost. Four is a structural constant with a named reason — more is a wall rather than a notification. No toast library entered the tree (`sonner` and every sibling stay NOT-ADOPTED).
- **The D5 timestamp primitive, and a REPORTED deviation.** `Timestamp` renders the served UTC RFC3339 in `<time dateTime={ts}>`; `audit` renders that alone, `live` puts relative time BESIDE it and never in place of it; an empty stamp renders the landed `Absent`, and an UNPARSEABLE one renders verbatim with no label, because inventing "3m ago" for an instant we could not read is precisely the fabricated number the invariant forbids. **The brief's "refreshes on a coarse interval" is NOT implemented with a timer.** §32's no-ticker rule is scanned for tree-wide (`sweep.test.tsx`, `chat.test.tsx`) on the ground that a timer is a second source of currency that keeps running when the feed is down — and a ticking "3m ago" beside data the platform stopped receiving is that hazard exactly. The label re-derives at RENDER, which on a live surface the feed drives; when the feed stops the label stops with the data it describes, and the connection pill says why. **No call site was migrated:** `parts.tsx`'s `Stamp` still serves every audit site it already served, and applying `live` is UI-4's row.
- **The landed `<time>` scan was WIDENED, not weakened.** `sweep.test.tsx` pinned timestamp rendering to `parts.tsx` alone; the D5 answer ratified a second primitive, so the list is now `['./parts.tsx', './ui/Timestamp.tsx']` — a third file, or a view rendering `<time>` inline, still fails; each named primitive is asserted to still exist so the list cannot pass by naming a dead file; and the file is additionally asserted to keep the served UTC in `dateTime`. Its sibling "no view formats a date itself" is unchanged and still bans localization: relative-beside-verbatim is an addition, localizing an instant is a transformation of a fact.
- **The kit is not in the production bundle yet, and that is correct.** Nothing shipped imports it — this packet builds no surface work beyond the shell chrome — so the JS is byte-for-byte the size it was before the kit landed and `@base-ui/react` appears in the chunk zero times. What DID land is its CSS: Tailwind scans sources, so the kit's utilities are compiled (36.40 → 52.94 kB, gzip 8.62 → 11.35). The `@base-ui/react` JS cost lands the day UI-2 first mounts a primitive, stated here so that growth is expected rather than discovered.
- **The migration ledger** (R20 — tokens land first and coexist; **no landed per-surface rule was deleted or renamed this packet**): `shell`/`connection state` — shed at UI-1, done. `oversight surfaces (B6-5)` + `task detail, fleet, filters` → UI-5. `the approval inbox` → UI-6. `the settings tab` + `the assistant` → UI-6. `the S15.8 review surface` + `the S15.10 workforce map` → UI-7. The preflight-compatibility block leaves with the last of them. New primitive classes must not collide with landed selector names — `.panel` already exists and keeps its meaning.
- **Measured at landing (P3-UI-1), against the pre-packet reference re-built from a pristine `HEAD` worktree rather than quoted:** JS **976.99 → 981.17 kB** (gzip **292.96 → 294.55**), CSS **18.17 → 52.94 kB** (gzip **4.21 → 11.35**), `index.html` **1.77 → 1.80 kB**, fonts **0 → 417.30 kB** across **15** new assets (7 Inter woff2 + 4 JetBrains Mono woff2 + 4 JetBrains Mono woff — DATED CORRECTION 2026-08-04 at landing: drain r1 corrected the other two "16" sites, this bullet's count was the missed third, caught by the drain re-check). The JS delta is **+4.18 kB raw / +1.59 kB gzip** and **CORRECTED 2026-08-04 (drain r1) it is the seven lucide icons plus the shell's own new markup, and nothing else**. The landing text attributed it partly to `@base-ui/react` and the three class utilities, which contradicted this same section's other measurement: nothing shipped imports the kit, so none of them reaches the production chunk and `@base-ui/react` appears in it zero times. What the number does prove is the tree-shaking claim — a surviving icon barrel would have been hundreds of kB. The SPA stays un-split. Counters: lock **29 → 38** entries, npm coverage **240 → 574**; vitest **432/23 → 465/26** at executor landing, **469/26 after drain r1** (+2 toast, +2 scan tests); Go **45 packages**, 14 sanctioned pre-existing skips.
- **REPORTED — the packet made one Go change, and the brief's "zero `.go` changes" counter could not hold.** `internal/watchlist/seed.go`'s `LockEntryNames` is a Go slice, and a landed test (`TestEveryLockEntryResolvesToASeededWatchRow`) requires **every** `components.lock` entry to resolve to a seeded watch row — S16.4 #9, asserted rather than assumed. So any adoption at all forces a data-only append there. Nine names were added; no logic, no behaviour, `go.mod`/`go.sum` byte-unchanged. This is the landed machinery working as designed: an adoption without its watch registration fails the build.

## 48. Controls I — cancel, pause-my-automation & the budget editor (P3-UI-2; S15.5–S15.6, S10.4/S10.8, S02.3, S15.2, proposal §3, §39+§39-B, §41-B, §42+§42-B, §46, §47)

The second packet of the UI batch, and the first that mounts the kit in production. It builds no verb: all four are landed, and this packet is the surface that finally presses them. Its design authority is the operator-approved proposal, **subordinate to the spec on all behavior** — and behavior moved in exactly one place, named below and sanctioned in advance.

- **THE ONE BACKEND CHANGE, sanctioned before the build started (OQ1).** `PauseStore.Paused` existed, the scheduler consulted it, and **no handler called it** — so a pause control could report what it had just done and nothing else, which is a control that cannot tell you what is true. `GET /api/meters` now serves an `automation` block: one `{owner, paused}` per person the response is already about, read from the SAME store the pause verb writes. **No new route, no new event, no scoping change, no migration, no ⚙ key.** The subjects are the lanes' own owners under the caller's scope, plus the caller themselves whenever the request is not narrowed to somebody else — that one addition is not a widening (a member's entire scope IS their own id, and the operator may read anybody's), and it is there because **a person who has run nothing has no lane row to carry their switch**. A store that fails, or is not wired, renders as an **absence with its reason**: reporting "not paused" because the read broke is the one answer a stop switch must never give. The shape mirrors the file's own landed `MeterView` (`states` / `absent`) rather than inventing a second absence idiom.
- **It is proven from the store, not from the verb.** The battery drives the real verb, then **writes the store behind the handler's back and re-reads** — the field has to follow, or it is a memory of an act rather than a reading of a switch. Both absence arms are driven (a failing read carries the failure's own text; an unwired process says "not wired"), and the member/operator legs are asserted in the non-tautological direction: the member's read carries their own switch **alone**, and the operator's carries the household with exactly one of them paused.
- **The golden fixture world gained the SWITCH and deliberately not the BUDGET (OQ4 as executed).** `fixtureServer` now wires the real `metering.Pause`, and `driveFixturePause` flips **bob's** switch through the real verb as the **operator** — so the committed `meters.json` carries a genuinely paused person beside two open ones, and the administer path is a served fact. A second body, **`meters-member.json`** (the same read as alice), makes "a member is offered their own switch and nobody else's" a claim about a served body rather than about a render. **No `Budgets` store is wired there, and that is the point:** the lane gauge in that world is `fixtureMeter`, so a declared budget would commit a body whose Layer-0 budget view reported a declaration while the gauge block beside it reported none — **the exact contradiction §39-B drain D2 fixed**. The declared half's real tie already exists where the real gauge is (internal/shell's HTTP-level test declares through the verb and requires the two halves of one response to agree), so the post-declare READ arm stays hand-scripted here and cites it. The alternative — teaching a test double to compute pressure — would be a second implementation of the S10.4 gauge, which is what D4 and §11 exist to forbid.
- **The `cursor` moved 86 → 87, in lockstep across every committed body, and it could not have done otherwise.** One real `decision.recorded` row is what a real pause flip mints. The flip is driven LAST (after the workforce and push seedings, for the same stated reason), so every other body's `event_seq` sits exactly where it was and only the head moved. Regeneration is drift-free on a re-run. `workforce.test.tsx`'s hand-built body carried the old figure inertly and is trued to 87 — the §46 D14 correction, applied to itself.
- **Four api.ts members, named for what they do, each with a real caller in the same change:** `cancelRun(run)`, `cancelTask(task)`, `declareBudget(body)`, `setAutomationPause(body)`. The types transcribe the Go wire shapes field for field (`CancelOutcome`, `TaskCancelOutcome`, `BudgetRecord`+`BudgetDeclared`, `AutomationPause`, and the read's `AutomationState`/`AutomationView`), snake_case as served. Both cancels are **path-only**: the run or task IS the request and the actor is the session's. `declaredButUncalled()` stays exactly `['health']`.
- **The sweep's pins moved deliberately: 14 → 10 routes over 13 → 9 shapes**, four exception entries **removed** (not annotated), with the dated cross-note in §46. The stale-entry test fired the moment the surfaces called the verbs, which is exactly what it is for.
- **`web/src/controls.tsx` is a NEW file and is deliberately not in the kit.** The kit styles surfaces and does not re-open §42's honesty rules; what lives here IS one — that an `applied:false` is neither a success nor a failure, and that a 409 is a re-read rather than a fault. It builds FROM the kit (`Modal`, `Button`), declares no colour, and starts no motion, so it needs neither of the kit's two scans. **The act-outcome vocabulary is four values, not the landed two**, each because a verb in this packet serves it: `applied` (something changed) · `noop` (`applied:false` — the run had already ended, the switch was already there) · `retry` (a 409: the subject moved, so re-read and decide again) · `failed` (the server refused and said why). `noop` and `retry` take no error styling; the distinction survives in `data-outcome` for anything that needs to tell them apart. **The classification is from the server's machine CODE, never from its prose.**
- **The re-read is unconditional, including after a refusal.** A refusal is often the platform telling you that what you are looking at has moved, so `useAct` re-reads on every path. Nothing in this packet flips a rendered state itself (§42 — REST is the truth, frames are the trigger), and the tests assert the run's rendered state changes only through the read.
- **Cancel mounts on the task detail only (OQ3), at two grains.** A task-level control in the header region, rendered **only while some run has not ended**; a per-run control beside each non-terminal run in the receipts block. `Board.tsx` and `MissionControl.tsx` are byte-untouched — the CardFace is pinned "nothing more" by its own comment and tests, and mission control's restyle is UI-5's. **State-computed from ONE list, read the other way round:** `cancellable(state) = !terminalStates.includes(state)`, so there is no second vocabulary to drift. **An unrecognized state is OFFERED rather than hidden** — the same forward-tolerance the kanban vocabulary takes (§42): the client owns no state vocabulary, and the verb refuses what it cannot cancel; hiding the control would make a future server state silently uncancellable from every surface.
- **The confirm says what the mapping does for the state the run is IN**, and asserts nothing beyond it: running/draining stops now through its own shutdown ladder; parked closes and takes its open question card with it, with no resume; queued is withdrawn before it starts with its queue row settled in the same breath; claimed/new may be refused because it is mid-dispatch. No "deleted", no "rolled back". The task-level confirm counts what it is about to act on from served state and says that one refusing run fails the whole call. **No tour, no hint, no spotlight** — the self-teaching layer is UI-5..7's.
- **The task cancel is itemized and never overclaims.** Every `runs[]` disposition renders on its own line with its own `data-outcome`; `kanban_status` is spoken only when `applied:true`, so a no-op task cancel says nothing was cancelled and never relabels the task — the client half of drain D4's rule.
- **The pause control is TWO POSITION VERBS, one row per person the read serves.** Whose switches appear is the server's answer, so the operator's administer path needs no picker and no free-text person, and a member's UI simply has one row. Both buttons render on both positions, so the 400 the verb serves for a missing position **cannot be produced by this control**. **No confirm dialog**: it is reversible, its explainer is already on screen beside it, and a ceremony around a reversible switch teaches people to click through ceremonies.
- **P-T08-4 is visible in both layers.** Before the act, the explainer says it in plain words: new background work stops being started, running work parks at its next safe boundary, **nothing queued and nothing parked is thrown away**, and talking to the platform yourself is never held back. After the act, the served `detail` renders **verbatim** in both directions, and `changed:false` renders as the honest already-there repeat rather than as a change. The resume story's run-level half is a `Link` to the inbox where the parked run's own release lives (OQ2: "resume — I was wrong" is already surfaced there and is a different verb on a different subject; this packet points at it and re-implements nothing).
- **The budget editor renders no figure, and that is the design.** The declared budget, the pressure and the remainder are all served and render where they are served — in the meters panel, absences and all — so the editor offers the ACT and nothing else. An editor printing its own copy of them would be a second answer to a question the platform already answers, and the moment they disagreed one of the two lines would be a lie. Pre-declaration the two landed absence texts render byte-identically (`MissionControl.tsx` is untouched); post-declare the response renders (`prior` as old→new, its ABSENCE as the honest "there was no budget on this lane before") and the re-read gauge is what shows the new figures.
- **D5, kept at the input.** The unit label on the field is the SERVED string (`budget_unit` off the Layer-0 view) and is empty before any declaration, because before one the platform has served no unit at all — so the field carries no unit rather than one this client made up, and the explainer names the unit in words. A probe asserts no `$`, `usd`, `dollar`, `€`, `£` or `cost` token renders anywhere in the editor, and no arithmetic over any budget figure exists in the tree.
- **Client pre-validation mirrors the verb's own bound (`> 0`, integer) and never answers for the server.** It holds an obviously-refused request back; anything that fires renders the server's own refusal text, the pause pointer in the `period_tokens` refusal included.
- **Authority is stated, not inferred, and it is the verbs' own rule.** `useMayAct` in `Fleet.tsx` answers "may the signed-in person act on this owner's subject?" as **own + operator-any** (D10, §39-B OQ4), with the operator limb mirroring the server's `isOperatorRead` — dev posture included, because that is the predicate the read on the other side used. This is the B6-6 D9 lesson applied: a control the door would refuse is an invented authority, and a hidden control the door would allow is an invented refusal. **A member handed a household body is still offered nobody else's controls** — asserted in that sabotage direction, over the operator's own served body.
- **REPORTED DEVIATION — `Fleet.tsx` reads the session itself.** The shell holds the session and hands `me` to the surfaces that need it (`Board`, `MissionControl`, `Deliverable`), but `App.tsx` is frozen for this packet, so this surface reads the one identity source directly (`GET /api/auth/session` — §41-B: identity comes from there and nowhere else). It is a second READ of one source, never a second source. Hoisting it to the shell's own read belongs to the packet that reopens the shell (UI-5). Until the session lands nothing is actionable: you cannot be offered an act before the platform knows who is asking. **The task detail needs no such read** — its own read is owner-scoped, so a member never obtains a cross-owner body and the control cannot render over one; the test asserts exactly that, through the read's own 403.
- **Every act lands where decisions already render, by consuming what the backend already emits.** A cancel mints no decision row — it rides `run.state_changed`, which the task detail already subscribes to; the budget and the pause mint `decision.recorded`, which the fleet already subscribes to. **`live.ts` is byte-unchanged**, and both frame paths are asserted with the landed frame patterns. The §42-B documented miss stands untouched: a person-level pause or budget decision is not a task decision, no landed surface renders a person-level decision feed, and building one would exceed the freeze.
- **The primitive package now has a WALL, added by the packet that first mounts it.** `@base-ui/react` is imported by exactly `ui/Modal.tsx`, `ui/Drawer.tsx` and `ui/Toast.tsx` and nowhere else in the tree, asserted over the whole app tree with a non-vacuity check that names two surfaces the scan must have reached. A surface importing the dialog directly would carry its own focus trap, escape stack and ARIA — three things noticed only when they disagree.
- **Bundle, measured and itemized rather than attributed by reasoning.** Against the UI-1 reference (JS **981.17 kB** / gzip **294.55**, CSS **53.78** / **11.52**, 15 font assets / 417.30 kB): now **JS 1075.55 kB / gzip 326.01** (**+94.38 / +31.46**), **CSS 53.84 / 11.53** (+0.06 / +0.01), `index.html` 1.80 kB and the fonts **unchanged**. The step was split by two controlled builds that were reverted immediately, not by inference: with the three primitive-backed kit components stubbed to plain DOM the chunk is **1021.42 kB / gzip 307.68**, so **`@base-ui/react` (dialog + toast) is 54.13 kB raw / 18.33 kB gzip** — the cost §47 said would land the day UI-2 first mounted a primitive, landing. With `cn()` stubbed to a plain join the chunk is **1048.40 / 317.23**, so **`tailwind-merge` + `clsx` are 27.15 kB raw / 8.78 kB gzip**, their first production import (UI-1 measured them at zero because nothing shipped imported the kit). The remaining **13.10 kB raw** is `class-variance-authority` plus this packet's own source. Nothing is unattributed; the SPA stays un-split.
- **Counters at landing.** gofmt empty · vet + build clean · `go test ./... -count=1` **45 packages, 0 failures** · lockgate **38 entries / 574 npm** · typecheck + **503 vitest / 26 files** (was 469/26) · migrations **0001–0021**, none opened · event inventory **102/5/107**, `internal/eventlog/contract.go` byte-unchanged · ⚙ **118/33**, `internal/settings/index.go` byte-unchanged · `components.lock` / `go.mod` / `go.sum` / `web/package.json` / `web/package-lock.json` byte-unchanged · Layer-0 views **11**, catalog **50** — **no canned query added**, so the band ceiling was not touched · escape allowlist **EMPTY**, banned **8** · `routes.ts` / `router.tsx` / `events.ts` / `live.ts` / `index.css` / `App.tsx` / `Board.tsx` / `MissionControl.tsx` / `Inbox.tsx` / `History.tsx` / `parts.tsx` all byte-unchanged · **zero fixture drift** through the real regeneration path, `cursor` **86 → 87** · **no ⚙ key invented and none read client-side**; no new client number beyond the verb's own `> 0` bound, which is the contract mirrored rather than a constant. **$0**, hermetic, no host change, nothing pushed.
- **Assertion counts per touched test file, pre-packet → post, MEASURED** (one method for both sides: assertion-bearing lines — `expect(` on the web side, `t.Error*`/`t.Fatal*` on the Go side): `taskdetail.test.tsx` **65 → 123** (+15 tests: state-computed presence, the confirm flow, every outcome leg, task itemization, the scoping legs, the frame path, phone width) · `fleet.test.tsx` **26 → 102** (+18 tests: the switch's served position, both scoping directions, the P-T08-4 legs, the editor's whole path, the units probe, the frame path, phone width) · `ui/kit.test.tsx` **56 → 61** (+1: the primitive-import wall) · `meters_verbs_test.go` **65 → 76** (+2: the served switch position and its two absence arms) · `apifixtures_test.go` **85 → 86** (+1: the driven pause flip's own failure check) · `sweep.test.tsx` **74 → 74** (pins moved, assertions unchanged) · `workforce.test.tsx` **183 → 183** (one inert `cursor` figure trued). Nothing went down, no scan narrowed, no floor lowered.
- **The seams UI-3/4 inherit, and nothing beyond them.** (1) The confirm idiom: kit `Modal` + a plain-words what-this-does sentence + an act row (danger for destructive, primary for declarations, ghost dismiss) + the outcome in place + the re-read. (2) The verb-button pattern, state-computed from served state only. (3) The `[data-outcome]` contract with its four honest arms. (4) The editor-form idiom: labelled fields, wire-sourced unit labels, server refusal texts verbatim, pre-validation that never replaces the server's answer. (5) The api.ts discipline: a member per verb, types transcribed field for field, every member called. **Not built here and deliberately:** the benchmark opt-in and the memory family (UI-3), history ask/search and the D5 call-site application (UI-4), every host-surface restyle and the whole self-teaching layer (UI-5..7), `ToastProvider` in the production tree (UI-7), and any person-level decision feed (unlanded, unratified).
- **AGPL attestation.** Zero Odysseus code, CSS, markup or asset is in this packet. Its pattern study was read as ideas only, and the two things this packet took from anywhere — confirm-before-fire and outcome-in-place — are the landed Inbox's own idiom generalized, which is this codebase's.

#### §48 drain round 1 (P3-UI-2 drain r1, D1–D7) — one promise the backend does not keep, three drifted transcriptions, and the legs that were rendered but never fired

The fresh-context evaluation returned FAIL on 5 findings (1 medium, 4 low) plus nits, having first verified what mattered most: **all four recorded deviations hold** (including the §39-B citation behind the fixture-world budget refusal and the single-identity-source reading behind `useMayAct`), the fixture world regenerates with **zero drift**, and the OQ1 sanction was not exceeded. F5 — the caller's own laneless row inside the automation subject set — was **coordinator-ACKED as within the sanction's intent**; no change. Seven items triaged, all seven applied, none refused.

- **D1 (MEDIUM) — the task confirm promised an atomicity `stage.CancelTask` does not have.** The verb walks its runs in order and **each `cancelOne` commits on its own** (cancel.go:221–233), so a run refusing mid-dispatch stops the walk with everything already cancelled **still cancelled**. The confirm said "the whole request is refused and nothing is cancelled" — a promise the platform does not keep, on the one screen where a person is deciding to stop work. It now says what happens: the request stops there, the runs already cancelled stay cancelled, and the page re-reads so you can see how far it got. **The same lie lived in `controls.tsx`'s generic 409 note**: `nothing fired — re-read it and decide again` is true of a SINGLE-SUBJECT verb (the one transition it would have made is the one refused) and false of a multi-subject one. `refusalOf`/`useAct.run` now take an optional `conflictNote`, the default is exported as `nothingFired` with the reason on it, and the task verb passes its own. Both directions are asserted: the task 409 says the walk stopped part-way and must NOT contain "nothing fired"; the run 409 still says it.
- **D2 — a scripted body that no handler produces.** The no-op task-cancel fixture carried `kanban_status: 'executing'` under a comment claiming the server sends the task's unchanged column. It does not: `TaskCancelOutcome` is built with no `Kanban`, the field is set only inside the `if out.Applied` branch, and the json tag carries no `omitempty` — so production serves `""`. Corrected to the served zero value, and the false comment replaced with why it is zero. (The render was already correct — the column is spoken only when `applied` — so this was a probe drifting from the handler, which is the inert-probe class this packet was told to avoid.)
- **D3 — three refusal strings transcribed byte-exact (R22).** The cancel verbs authorize through `authorizeOwner` (reads.go:444–452), whose 403 is the bare word `forbidden` and whose 404 is `run not found` — **not** `readPerson`'s S01.9 sentence, which belongs to the `?person=` filter and never reaches these verbs. The pause 404 is the full served `no such person "ghost": a budget or a pause is declared for somebody` (meters_verbs.go:465). Each now carries its source beside it.
- **D4 — every control now has BOTH authority directions fired, not merely rendered.** Added: the operator cancelling **another owner's** run (the default session is alice-as-operator; the subject is bob's, and the fetch log proves the POST); the operator declaring **bob's** budget (`{person:'bob', lane:'zai', …}`); a **member** flipping their own switch (`{person:'alice', paused:true}`) and declaring their own budget — both under a member session over the member-scoped served body. The render-scoping legs were already there; these are the acts. Same pass: the two confirm arms that had copy and no assertion — **claimed/new** ("being dispatched right this moment") and the **unrecognized state** ("the platform decides which ending applies") — are asserted, with a negative on both that no arm invents a deletion or a rollback.
- **D5 — the budget field parsed loosely, which is the wrong kind of forgiving.** `Number.parseInt('3.5')` is 3 and `parseInt('3e5')` is 3: both would have fired a **different figure from the one typed**, silently. `wholePositive` refuses anything that is not a plain run of digits, the reason renders in the form, and nothing is sent. Both cases are tested, each asserting the input really holds what was typed so the refusal is about the value rather than about a field the harness never filled.
- **D6 — the token contract reaches the figures.** The served prior figure in the outcome line and both numeric inputs render `font-mono tabular-nums` (§47: every number, id, timestamp and status token), as do the run-id spans in the new cancel markup. `ActOutcome.note` is a `ReactNode` so a figure inside a sentence can carry its own treatment without the sentence being assembled from parts; the rendered text is asserted to still read as one sentence.
- **D7 — a claim narrowed to what is true, dated.** The executor's landing report (not the commit message — attribution corrected 2026-08-05 at landing, drain-re-check nit) said a split "would have left a red intermediate". What is true is narrower: the sweep's stale-entry test precludes splitting **consumption from its bookkeeping** inside one commit — it fires the moment a surface calls an excused route — and says nothing about the brief's pre-authorized **A/B seam** (cancel / the fleet pair), which stayed available the whole way. Single-sitting was a choice, not a constraint, and it landed. Recorded here rather than by rewriting a commit message.
- **Counters after drain r1:** typecheck ✓ · vitest **511 / 26 files** (was 503/26) · build ✓ · gofmt empty · vet + build clean · `go test ./... -count=1` **45 packages, 0 failures** over the real dist · lockgate **38 / 574**. Bundle **MEASURED after the round, not predicted: JS 1076.30 kB / gzip 326.26** (from 1075.55 / 326.01 — **+0.75 kB raw / +0.25 gzip**, which is the corrected confirm copy, the conflict-note seam and the strict parse, and nothing else), **CSS 53.84 / 11.53 — UNMOVED**, because `font-mono` and `tabular-nums` were already compiled for the kit and a second consumer of a utility costs nothing. `index.html` and the fonts unchanged. **Assertion counts, pre-drain → post:** `taskdetail.test.tsx` **123 → 138** (+4 tests) · `fleet.test.tsx` **102 → 120** (+4 tests). Nothing went down; no production `.go` file was touched this round, and no fixture was regenerated.

## 49. Controls II — the standing benchmark opt-in & the S09 memory family (P3-UI-3; S09, S15.2/S15.6, S15.9, BENCH-REG §2/§3/§4/§14/§15/§17, proposal §3, §39-C, §40-C, §41-B, §42, §43, §46, §47, §48)

The third packet of the UI batch, and the batch's widest: a **new route family** and its surface, six landed gate verbs pressed for the first time, and the consent flip that makes somebody a benchmark participant. It landed as one sitting; the pre-authorized A/B seam stayed available and was not needed.

- **THE ROUTE TABLE GREW, for the first time since it was written (OQ2, ratified).** `routes.ts` gains `memory /memory` (nav) and `memory-entry /memory/:id` (nav:false), and the `RouteID` union with them. The ban §41-B records is on **RENAMES** — a published path is what a deep link and a push `navigate` field were written against — and an addition publishes a path nothing pointed at before. S09.4's v0 activation table *requires* one ("Manual L2 — human-direct entries via workspace UI [XREF:S15]") and the pinned route test's own comment anticipated it. The entry route exists so a conflict edge naming another entry is navigable in both directions, the S15.11 deep-links-always-land ethos.
