#### §49 drain round 1 (P3-UI-3 drain r1, D1–D6) — two unexercised arms, one of which was hiding a real defect

The fresh-context evaluation returned FAIL on 2 LOW (both test-coverage) plus 6 nits, having first verified what mattered most: the fixture story holds (zero drift, `cursor` 89 in lockstep, the `?status=active` narrowing confirmed landed rather than asserted), the OQ1 wall holds structurally, both directions of the content-vs-telemetry line hold, the retire/delete copy is word-true, and the opt-in explanation is faithful. All three recorded deviations were verified sound. Six items triaged, six applied, none refused.

- **D1 — the 404 arm was never fired.** `memoryScopeRead` answers every entry-scoped route `404 memory entry not found` (internal/api/memory.go:716–718), 404 BEFORE 403 so an unknown id cannot become an existence oracle, and nothing in the battery had ever seen it. Both halves now are: the READ arm (the surface renders the served sentence and no entry, no verbs, no invented deletion story) and the fired-VERB arm — a retire on an entry that had gone between the read and the act, which is a real race — asserted as `failed` carrying the server's own words, with the negative that it is NOT dressed as a 409's re-read-and-decide-again.
- **⚠ D2 — the composition test found a REAL DEFECT the isolated arms could not.** The delete's answer was held by the button that fired it. A successful purge turns the entry into a tombstone, the tombstone branch drops the verbs, and the verbs took their own outcome line and the four honest limits down with them — so at the exact moment a person reads what a deletion did not reach, it disappeared. The isolated test passed only because its scripted re-read still answered with a live entry. **The purge answer now belongs to the PAGE**, which is the entry's own surface, and it survives the re-read that removes the control; the served sentence has exactly ONE home there, asserted in both directions (present on the page, absent from the outcome line). Locked by the sequence the finding names: swap the scripted read to the post-delete body, fire, and require delete → re-read → tombstone arm → the answer still standing.
- **D3 — a confirm sentence that was true for one reader and false for the other.** The retire confirm said purging is "a separate right with its own control below". For an OPERATOR retiring somebody else's entry there is no control below — there is the absence note saying the purge is the owner's alone — so the copy pointed at a door that was not there, on a destructive confirm. It is now posture-aware and true both ways: the owner is told the control is below, and everybody else is told the right belongs to whoever wrote the entry and that nothing here will purge it. Asserted in the operator posture, with the negative that the owner's clause does not render.
- **D4 — record truth, in both places.** `WithForms`'s doc comment still claimed to be "the ONE read of the blind-pair form data" and to spare an unwired process the question; the standing opt-in panel made both false. Corrected in place with the reason and a pointer here. And this section's own "exactly one non-cursor line" is corrected above, dated: one logical change, three physical lines.
- **D5 — a refusal cost the person their draft.** The write dialogs reset on every open, so a gate refusal — dialog closed, act refused, reason on screen — meant retyping the whole entry to fix one field. The reset is now conditional on the last act NOT having been refused, and the outcome is deliberately no longer cleared on open, so the distinction survives a dialog the reader opened and closed again. An APPLIED write still starts the next entry clean, and the edit form still re-syncs from the SERVED entry on a clean open, so a version somebody else superseded meanwhile prefills as it now is. All three legs asserted, including that the retried write carries the preserved body rather than a re-typed one.
- **D6 — a fixture helper that could serve the wrong caller's world silently.** `memoryRoutes()` keyed alice's browse and the operator's by URL alone, so a test mounted as one person could assert the other's body and pass — the exact scoping mistake those two committed bodies exist to catch. The helper now takes the subject (`'alice' | 'op'`), and the session and BOTH browse keys move together, with the hazard written at the helper. Driven both ways.
- **Counters after drain r1:** typecheck ✓ · vitest **561 / 27 files** (was 556/27) · build ✓ · gofmt empty · vet + build clean · `go test ./... -count=1` **45 packages, 0 failures** over the real dist · lockgate **38 / 574**. Bundle **MEASURED after the round: JS 1108.76 kB / gzip 334.02** (from 1108.48 / 333.90 — **+0.28 raw / +0.12 gzip**, which is the posture-aware confirm copy, the lifted purge block and the conditional draft reset, and nothing else), **CSS 54.90 / 11.72 — UNMOVED**, `index.html` and the fonts unchanged. **Assertion counts, pre-drain → post:** `memory.test.tsx` **146 → 179** (+5 tests, 32 → 37) · `Inbox.tsx` carries a comment-only change; `doubles.ts` carries the D6 CODE change (posture-explicit `memoryRoutes('alice'|'op')` + the new `signedInAsOperator` export — described in the D6 bullet above; this counter line originally called it comment-only, corrected 2026-08-05 at landing, re-check nit). Nothing went down; no production `.go` file was touched this round, and no fixture was regenerated.

## 50. Controls III — history ask/search, the C-1 login fix, the D5 timestamp map & the two cosmetic S00.9 amendments (P3-UI-4; S14.10, S15.2/S15.5, S00.9, S01.9, BENCH-REG §13, proposal §3, §37, §41-B, §42, §46, §47, §48, §49)

The fourth packet of the UI batch, and the one that closes the layer ladder: the S14.10 query surface has offered four verbs since B5-8B and a surface pressed two of them. It also carries three things that are not controls at all — a client-side auth defeat, a ratified render decision applied across the tree, and the first post-freeze `Spec/` edit of the batch. **Two walls were declared before the build started and are policed below: `App.tsx`'s diff, and `Spec/`'s.**

- **⚙ NONE consumed and NONE created, and that is the requirement.** `internal/history` declares and reads no registry key at all (§37), the client reads none, and the one client-side number in the packet is not a number: the empty-question refusal mirrors the transport's OWN bound (`historyQuestion`, historyapi.go:197–204) rather than introducing a second one. `internal/settings/index.go` byte-unchanged at **118/33**.
- **ZERO production `.go` change, and this time the counter held.** Every read this packet consumes was already routed at B6-1. The one Go file that moved is `internal/api/apifixtures_test.go` — test-only, under the §49 fixture-driving precedent.
- **Two api.ts members, each with a real caller in the same change:** `historyAsk(q)` and `historySearch(q)`, both typed `Answer` because that is what the transport serves. `declaredButUncalled()` stays exactly `['health']`. The sweep's pins moved **3 → 1 routes over 3 → 1 shapes**, two exception entries **removed** rather than annotated, with the dated cross-note in §46.
- **A DISAMBIGUATION CARD IS AN ANSWER, and the honest posture is the one that ships everywhere.** The ask layer has no local tier wired in any test process, in the fixture world, or on an unwired dev host, so it takes internal/history/layer1.go:154's branch and returns its card with its own reason at 200, audit intact. That is not a degraded mode to apologize for — it is the tier-F surface, deterministic and $0, and it is what the committed body carries. The card's reason, question, and every choice's name, category and description render **verbatim**; the panel's error banner never sees it.
- **A CARD CHOICE SELECTS THE QUESTION; IT DOES NOT FIRE IT (OQ2 as disposed).** The landed `onChoose` fired the chosen catalog name with whatever slots the picker happened to be holding — and a card born of a free-text ask holds another question's slots or none, so the reader would have received a different question's answer under the heading of the one they clicked. The choice now lands where a Layer-1 question is asked from: the picker selects it, its own slots render EMPTY, and the person fires deliberately. The card is deliberately **not** cleared — it is the context the choice was made in. Asserted with the fetch log (nothing fired), then driven through to the deliberate ask.
- **Search sends `q` VERBATIM, and the reason is that redaction is somebody else's property.** The store redacts the question, strips the markers that left, matches only what survives, verifies each hit against the marker-free body and bounds every excerpt (search.go:81–145). A client that pre-stripped anything would be a second implementation of the rule the guarantee rests on, free to disagree with it. Excerpts and notes render **as served** — including a `[REDACTED:…]` marker inside excerpt text, which is there on purpose (internal/history/search_test.go:88–95: the excerpt must show that something WAS redacted rather than silently omit it) — and a question that was nothing but a secret renders its three notes and no rows, as an answer rather than an error.
- **THE BAND WALL WAS NOT TOUCHED.** The catalog is exactly **50**, Layer-0 views **11**, and `internal/history` is byte-unchanged. Neither control needed a canned entry: `ask` and `search` are layers over the catalog that exists, not new questions in it.
- **`busy` and `held` are two facts, and the panel's four gestures share one answer slot.** The in-flight marker is the SOURCE (`'' | 'view' | 'query' | 'ask' | 'search'`) rather than a boolean, so a form's own button can say "this request is mine and it is in flight" — which is not the statement "this form is not ready to send". A held form states its reason at the field and fires **nothing** (fetch-log-empty asserted, whitespace included, because the server trims before it refuses). The §49 N7 idiom, applied to a read rather than an act: these are queries, so there is no confirm dialog — a ceremony around a read teaches people to click through ceremonies.
- **The draft survives an answer AND a refusal.** Fixing one word must not mean retyping the sentence, on a surface whose whole premise is that asking again is an act. The server's own refusal sentence renders through `describeError` and the question stays where it was.
- **The lower-confidence flag's home holds, asserted in both directions.** `AnswerView` flags exactly `layer === 2`; an ask answer is `canned` and a search answer is `deterministic`, and neither wears it — the ask stops at its card and never falls through (historyapi.go:25–28; the store's `TestLayer2IsNotReachedBySilentFallthrough`). `data-confidence` renders on every answer, and the same shared component still flags a layer-2 body. **No History-surface control names `GET /api/events/open-sql`:** Layer 2 is reached through the assistant's chat-turn escalation so the turn record exists, and that exemption is unmoved.
- **NOT LIVE, still.** `data-live="query-instrument"` stands, no `useLive` was wired for the new verbs, nothing subscribes and no ticker entered. Reads mint nothing, which is why the golden `cursor` did not move.
- **THE FIXTURE POSTURE IS HYBRID, and the search half is a REAL corpus (OQ3 as disposed).** Both committed bodies are produced by the REAL handlers over the fixture world. For search that required the corpus to exist at all: `history_fts` was empty, and §38 D12's lesson is that a search assertion over an empty index passes while proving nothing. `indexFixtureHistory` runs the REAL B5-8A projector (`retention.Index`) over the world's own event log, so the rows, refs, kinds, owner column and write-time redaction are all the indexer's — never this file's idea of what it writes. The committed answer carries **two rows across two kinds and two owners**, with the projector's two ref shapes (a run id, and an `event:<seq>` ref for a row with no run), because a one-row body would let the list render, the per-row ref and the owner column all be right by accident. The pass **appends no event** — it writes `history_fts`, `run_event_rollup` and its own cursor row inside one WriteTx — so the head `cursor` could not move, and it did not. The two arms the real corpus does not contain (a marker inside an excerpt; the nothing-but-a-secret note) stay hand-scripted per test, each citing its Go file:line, exactly as §49's error contracts do.
- **REPORTED, and deliberately not fixed here: a Go doc comment that disagrees with what the handler serves.** `internal/history/search.go:79` says the answer's columns are `{event_seq, kind, ref, user_id, excerpt}`. The SELECT list has a bare `rowid` with no alias (search.go:105), so SQLite reports the column name `rowid`, and the committed body — produced by the real handler — carries `["rowid","kind","ref","user_id","excerpt"]`. No landed test asserted either name, which is why it survived. **The comment is wrong, not the code**, and the fix is a one-word production `.go` edit this packet is barred from making; the committed body now pins the served truth so the next packet that opens the file has the evidence in front of it. Flagged rather than silently rendered around: the client renders the columns as served and names none of them.

- **The two committed questions are EXPORTED from `doubles.ts`, and the encodings were verified rather than assumed.** A test that types one question while a double answers another would be a fixture pretending to be a reply, so the strings and their request keys have one home. Go's `url.QueryEscape` (which produced the bodies) and the client's `URLSearchParams` (which produces the request) were run against both questions and compared: byte-identical, so the committed body really is the answer to the URL the client sends.
- **`cursor` stayed 89 across all 25 pre-existing bodies and the two new files carry none** — `history.Answer` has no cursor field. Regeneration is drift-free: the only files the writer produced were the two new ones.

#### C-1 — the dev-posture login defeat, fixed one layer above where it looked

- **The root cause is client-side and the server posture was CORRECT.** `SessionAuthenticator` resolves every session-less request in dev posture to the fixed dev identity (identity.go:83–97), whose own note says "sessions still win when present, so the full login flow is exercisable in dev" (identity.go:74–76). `App.tsx`'s "no /login once there is a session" arm made `authed` permanently true there, so the picker could never render and `api.logout()` cleared nothing the next resolve would not hand straight back. **Zero Go change was needed and none was made.**
- **The discriminator is the WIRE's own marker, checked against the served shapes.** `session.dev === true` is set in exactly one place: the dev fallback. `handleAuthSession` serves it as `{authenticated:true, dev:true}` with **no `user` object** — the branch that populates one runs only `if !id.Dev` (auth_handlers.go:91–104) — where a real session serves `{authenticated:true, user:{…}}` with `dev` omitted, and real cookies always win (identity.go:84–92). **Production is byte-equivalent:** without the fallback `dev` is never true and both arms behave exactly as they shipped. The batch's named hazard was a jsdom-passes/production-false arm in this exact area, so the doubles were written FROM the handler rather than from the client's convenience.
- **THE WALL HELD. `App.tsx`'s diff is exactly two things:** one `devFallback` const + the `session.dev !== true` clause on the bounce arm, and the header affordance block. The session machinery, `useConnection`, the nav grouping, `navGroupOf`/`navIcons` and every route arm are untouched; `routes.ts`, `router.tsx` and **`Login.tsx` are byte-unchanged** — the picker always could render here, and this was the one layer that would not let it.
- **The affordance SHIPS, because reachable means an affordance and not a URL you have to know (OQ4 as disposed).** Under the dev fallback the header renders a `Link` to `/login` labelled "Sign in"; a Sign out is not rendered, because it would revoke nothing and the re-read would return the same identity — a control that cannot honour its own label. The who-line keeps its honest `dev`. **No invented state:** the client renders the two states the server serves and never synthesizes a third; the dev identity keeps browsing, because deny-by-default reads are the server's job and already hold.
- **The full cycle is asserted with the FETCH LOG, not with renders alone:** fallback → picker on /login with no bounce → real login POST → the session re-read serves the real user → Sign out appears and /login bounces again → logout POST + re-read → fallback, with the Sign-in link back. **The production-shape tests passed UNMODIFIED** — the no-session redirect and the landed Sign-out test both run under real sessions — and the missing negative was added rather than assumed: a real session is still bounced off /login to its `next`.

#### D5 — the map applied, and the rider answered per surface

- **The rider (carried from UI-1) is answered YES everywhere, and `live` was dropped nowhere.** Every live-classified surface is stream-driven — MissionControl, Filters, TaskDetail, Inbox, Chat, and ParkedUntil's hosts — so the label re-derives exactly when its data changes. Between frames it freezes WITH the data it describes, which is the ratified design, and the connection pill plus `Freshness` cover feed-down. **Two freeze directions, and they run opposite ways:** a past stamp freezes toward UNDERSTATING age (it reads fresher than it is); the inbox's future stamps (`expiry_at`, `engine_expiry_ts`) and every park horizon freeze toward OVERSTATING the time left. Both are corrected only by the instant beside them, which is why UTC-never-dropped is asserted at every migrated surface — and the server enforces real expiry regardless of what any label says.
- **The map was applied exactly: 12 sites + `ParkedUntil` migrate, 18 stay `Stamp`.** MissionControl :148 · Filters :155/:171/:234 · TaskDetail :65/:405/:454 · Inbox :395/:444/:452/:864 · Chat :1085, plus `parts.tsx`'s `ParkedUntil` (hosts: Board, Fleet, MissionControl ×2, Filters). The eighteen record sites keep `Stamp` deliberately — it already renders exactly the audit half of the D5 contract, so they are keeping the answer rather than waiting for one, and consolidation churn would be change without a decision behind it. `Stamp`'s doc comment, which deferred human-friendly rendering to "the S15.12 sweep", is trued and dated: that decision arrived and was executed here.
- **`parts.tsx` imports `ui/Timestamp` DIRECTLY rather than through the kit barrel, and the reason is bundle rather than taste.** The barrel also exports the three primitives carrying `@base-ui/react`, and `parts.tsx` is reached from nearly every surface — pulling the dialog and toast machinery into that graph to render a park horizon would be a cost with no consumer. The resulting `parts ↔ ui/Timestamp` cycle is safe by construction: both modules export hoisted function declarations and neither calls the other at module-evaluation time, only at render. Recorded here because a cycle nobody wrote down is a cycle somebody later "fixes".
- **UTC-never-dropped is asserted per surface, clock-independently.** Each migrated site is checked for the served string in `dateTime`, the same string rendered as the `<time>`'s text, and a label BESIDE it — by asserting the rendered text ends with the instant and is longer than it, rather than naming a label that would depend on when the suite runs. **Probe: with the primitive's `<time>` deleted so it rendered relative-only, ELEVEN tests across seven suites fire** — including two landed ones this packet did not write. Both absence arms are covered on live surfaces: an empty instant renders `not recorded`, an unparseable one renders verbatim with no label, and `ParkedUntil`'s "parked, no horizon given" is byte-kept.
- **The `<time>` file pin stays exactly `['./parts.tsx', './ui/Timestamp.tsx']`**, "no view formats a date itself" passes unmodified, and both no-ticker scans pass unmodified — no `setInterval`/`setTimeout` currency source entered anywhere. `ui/Timestamp.tsx` itself is **byte-unchanged**: this packet applied the primitive, it did not touch it.
- **REPORTED, and left alone deliberately: the inbox expiry site now carries two readings.** The primitive's coarse label sits beside the landed countdown (`(in 10s)` / `(past)`). They do not disagree — both derive from the same device clock — and the countdown says two things the label does not: second precision, and whether the deadline has passed at all, which is its warn-flag. Removing a landed render to tidy a duplicate would have dropped a fact and an assertion, so the duplication is recorded rather than resolved by hand here.

#### The S13.9 follow-up spawn — the fourteenth D3 control, and the state-read gap that hid it

- **IT WAS IN NO QUEUE ROW, and that is the finding rather than the control.** B6-9's sweep counted 14 remaining routes, the gate's D3 prose named thirteen controls by name, and the operator ratified "all fourteen get built" — but the ratified six-group build order (cancel → pause → budget → opt-in → memory → history ask/search) never named the follow-up spawn, no UI row carried it, and `sweep.test.tsx`'s own comment assigned all three remaining routes to "UI-4's row" while STATE's UI-4 row scoped only the two history layers. A comment agreeing with a count is not a plan. The grounding named it instead of assuming either way, STATE outranked the comment, and the coordinator amended the row (OQ1(a)) so the pin had a home. **The lesson is the one worth keeping: a count and an order were reconciled by nobody, and the only reason it surfaced is that the sweep pins three numbers rather than one.**
- **It lands as packet B of the pre-authorized A/B seam** (A = history + C-1 + D5 + the amendments), and a clean stop at A was a stated success mode. It was not needed.
- **Gated on what the door SUPPLIES, never on a verb name.** `driveableFollowUpDoor` requires an open door, a POST, and a route that really is the spawn — the rule drain r1 D4 wrote after the opposite mistake shipped a form with an enabled submit whose handler could only report that the door named nothing. **TWO served doors reach this route and both are honoured:** the plain `follow-up` door, which carries no preset, and the `request-revision` door's FINISHED limb, which carries `revision` (deliverables.go:264–267 and :350). **The preset on the wire is whichever the door named** — `""` is a landed preset the verb admits (actions.go:102–108), so the plain limb sends the platform's own plain follow-up rather than an omission. **Probe: re-gating on the verb name fires two tests by name.**
- **NO REVISION PICKER, and that is the design.** The verb defaults to the CURRENT revision when the body names none (actions.go:170–174) — the honest reading of "follow up on this deliverable" — and the answer says which revision it linked to. A picker would be this surface inventing a choice in order to re-answer a question the platform already answers, and the lineage a successor links to is a fact rather than a preference. The body is therefore exactly `{preset, objective}`: the door's framing plus the person's own ask.
- **One api.ts member, `spawnFollowUp(deliverable, body)`, path-only subject**, with `FollowUpSpawned` transcribed field for field. There is no owner field to send: the successor belongs to the AUTHENTICATED requester (actions.go:206–210), which is why the operator's follow-up on somebody else's deliverable comes back as the OPERATOR's task — asserted from the served answer, because no client may decide whose work it is.
- **The §48 idiom, unchanged and not re-invented:** confirm-before-fire on the kit `Modal` through `ActConfirm`, `useAct`'s unconditional re-read (asserted by counting the detail reads), `[data-outcome]` with its honest arms, and §49's held-vs-busy separation — a follow-up with no ask states its reason at the field, opens no dialog and reaches nothing (fetch-log asserted). The confirm says what a follow-up IS (a new task of your own, entering intake on its own terms) and what it is not: no revision replaced, nothing re-opened, the accepted work still accepted. The words "deleted", "rolled back" and "undone" are asserted ABSENT.
- **Both authority directions are FIRED, not merely rendered.** The verb authorizes through `authorizeOwner` (reads.go:444–452) — owner or operator for any row, 404 before 403 so an unknown id cannot become an existence oracle. The owner's own spawn and the operator's spawn on alice's deliverable both fire; the 403's bare `forbidden` renders verbatim as `failed`, and is asserted NOT to be dressed as a no-op, as a 409's re-read, or as a task that was opened.

- **Bundle, measured at landing.** Against the UI-3 reference (JS **1108.76 kB** / gzip **334.02**, CSS **54.90** / **11.72**, 15 font assets / 417.30 kB): now **JS 1113.19 / gzip 335.21** (**+4.43 / +1.19**), **CSS 54.99 / 11.75** (+0.09 / +0.03), `index.html` and the fonts unchanged. The CSS delta is newly-compiled Tailwind utilities for the two forms. SPA stays un-split.

## 51. D8 pass I — the oversight surfaces: mission control (+ personal filters), the board, task detail (+ the timeline rail), the fleet (+ the session-read hoist) and the workforce map (P3-UI-5; S15.5, S15.10, S15.3, S15.12, proposal §1/§3/§5, §41-B, §42+§42-B, §45-B, §47, §48, §49, §50)

The fifth packet of the UI batch and the first of the three D8 passes. Its design authority is the operator-approved proposal, **subordinate to the spec on all behavior** — and no behavior moved except the one sanctioned hoist below. **Three walls were declared before the build started and all three held**, verified against the pre-packet commit `b45c280`: the byte-frozen set is byte-identical (`routes.ts` · `router.tsx` · `live.ts` · `events.ts` · `api.ts` (**AMENDED by the drain-r1 D1 sanction — see the round record**) · `controls.tsx` · `kanban.ts` · `Login.tsx` · `Inbox.tsx` · `Chat.tsx` · `Deliverable.tsx` · `Memory.tsx` · `Settings.tsx` · `settingsForm.tsx` · `PushDevices.tsx` · `ConnectionState.tsx` · every `web/src/ui/*` including `ui/Timestamp.tsx` · every production `.go` · `Spec/` · every fixture · `components.lock`/`go.mod`/`go.sum`/`package.json`/`package-lock.json` · and `shell.test.tsx`, so the C-1 pins passed **unmodified**); `App.tsx`'s diff is **exactly one hunk**, the Fleet route arm; and the workforce map's zero-mutation walk and source scan both still stand. It landed as the pre-authorized A/B pair (`3595fe1`, then this commit), which was a cut for reviewability rather than a shortfall — B was built in the same sitting.

- **THE SCOPE RECONCILIATION, disposed before the build (OQ1(a)) — BOTH filters and workforce rode this packet.** Three sources disagreed about the five-surface list: the STATE queue row (:150) named workforce, S15.5's own title named filters, and §47's migration ledger assigned filters here and the workforce map to UI-7. The file evidence settled it. **Filters is not a route — it is mission control's own route** (`FilterBar`/`FilterView` mount inside `MissionControl.tsx:105–106`; the four views are `/?view=<id>`), so restyling `/` without it would have restyled half a page. **Workforce is the binding queue row**, and no later row carries it: UI-6 is inbox/settings/login+push and UI-7 is chat/review/assistant/self-teaching/seeded-world, so deferring it would have left it row-less — the UI-4 fourteenth-control class of miss (§50: a count and a list reconciled by nobody). **DATED CROSS-NOTE on §47's migration ledger (2026-08-05): "the S15.10 workforce map" moved UI-7 → UI-5 by the STATE queue cut, which outranks the ledger's UI-1-time forecast; UI-7's row now covers the review surface, the assistant and the remaining shared blocks.** The ledger had already drifted elsewhere in the same way — it assigns "the assistant" to UI-6 while the queue puts chat in UI-7.
- **THE RAIL'S GRAIN IS A FINDING, NOT A PREFERENCE (OQ2).** The Odysseus idea is a TOOL-CALL timeline. **No landed read on the task detail serves one**: the run card carries the CURRENT tool name and args digest (api.ts:445) and a one-line `last_activity` (:461); `tool.called` is registered **DECLARE-ONLY with no producer at all** (`internal/eventlog/contract.go:626`); and `tool.completed` frames are triggers rather than data, because REST is the truth (§42). So the rail is **stage / lifecycle / decision** grain over the two reads this surface already makes, and every node class traces to a row or field of them: step/error/split ← `stage_progress[]` plus the CLOSED `stage.finished` outcome vocabulary (`internal/stage/stageevents.go:35–47`, registered at contract.go:431) · decision ← `decisions[]` · park ← `receipt.park_history[]` · terminal ← `runs[].state` verbatim · the live node region ← the run card's `last_activity`, stage, tool, counters, `wedged` and `waiting_on_human`. The node union is a closed TypeScript type and a test reads the classes off it, so a new one cannot arrive without that list being reconsidered. Tool-grain playback, if the operator wants it later, enters as its own sanctioned-read decision post-batch.
- **THE RAIL IS THE CHRONOLOGY; THE BLOCKS BELOW IT ARE THE RECORDS — a duplication recorded rather than resolved by hand.** Park intervals render on the rail AND byte-for-byte in the receipt; decisions render on the rail AND in full in the decisions list. That is deliberate and it is two readings of ONE served array, so they cannot disagree: the rail node is placement-and-plain-words (reason, horizon, the door), the record below carries every field including `(as operator)` and the whole receipt table. Removing either would have dropped a fact or an assertion, which is the §50 D-lesson applied.
- **THE ORDER IS THE SERVED INSTANTS' OWN, and the tie-break is served order.** Nodes sort ascending by the instant the platform recorded; equal instants, and any instant this client could not parse, keep their served position rather than being moved to one nobody recorded. The run-standing nodes close the rail in served order because a run's state carries **no instant of its own** on this read — placing them among the timed nodes would have put them at a moment the platform never wrote down.
- **NO TICKER ENTERED WITH THE RAIL, and it is the one place a timeline is tempted to.** Closed park intervals render the SERVED `duration_seconds`; the running node renders the SERVED `counters.elapsed_s`; no "running for…" clock derives against a device clock. Both tree-wide no-poll scans and the `<time>` file pin (`['./parts.tsx','./ui/Timestamp.tsx']`) pass **unmodified**, and `taskdetail.test.tsx` adds its own file-level negative because a rail is exactly where an inline `<time>` or a `toLocale*` would appear.
- **THE HOIST — the §48 recorded deviation is CLOSED (R20; DATED CROSS-NOTE on §48's "REPORTED DEVIATION — `Fleet.tsx` reads the session itself", 2026-08-05: closed here, by the packet that reopened the shell, exactly as that bullet said it would be).** `useMayAct` is gone; `App.tsx` hands Fleet `me` and `operator` as it hands Board, MissionControl and Deliverable — one read, one source (§41-B). **The predicate is byte-preserved, dev posture included** (`session.dev === true || session.user?.role === 'operator'`), because that is the predicate the server's own `isOperatorRead` used on the other side of these verbs; it is deliberately **NOT** Memory's users-row-role-only flag, which the S09 gate resolves its actor against and these two verbs do not. Both are asserted to still differ, in App's own source. **The "nothing actionable before the session lands" property did not move** — it is now the shell's `session === null` arm, which renders no surface at all rather than a surface with its controls withheld, so `MayAct` stopped being nullable and three null guards left with it. Every authority leg was **re-fired rather than re-rendered**, and it cost nothing to do so: `fleet.test.tsx` already mounts through `<App>` in every test, so every leg was already a composition leg. The new negative is asserted **two ways**, because a DOM walk cannot see a read a render happened not to trigger: the fetch log carries **exactly one** `/api/auth/session` call on the fleet route (it carried two), and `Fleet.tsx`'s source contains no `api.session(` at all.
- **THE CAPACITY RING IS ONE IDIOM WITH ONE MOUNT, and it renders a SERVED ratio.** `ThresholdRing` is a new export in `parts.tsx` — the §42 honesty home, beside `Money` and `ParkedUntil`, because the kit deliberately owns no figure primitives — mounted in `MetersPanel` **only**, which serves mission control and the fleet at once. Fill derives from `lane.pressure` under the two landed gates (`pressure_applicable && pressure !== null`, api.ts:182–199) and **nothing else**: re-deriving it from consumption and the declared ceiling would be a second implementation of the S10.4 gauge, free to disagree with the one that actually admits work (D4, §11). Otherwise the landed absence with its denominator reason renders **unchanged and no ring appears** — honest absence renders as absence. The served figure stays beside the ring in mono/tabular: the ring is glanceable redundancy, never a replacement. **No other capacity render exists on these surfaces** — run counters are monotonic with no denominator and the workforce serves no ratio, so neither gets one.

The fresh-context evaluation returned FAIL on 5 LOW findings, having first reproduced the battery, the bundle, the fixtures and the assertion counts **byte-exact**, verified all three walls and both OQ dispositions, and accepted all three recorded deviations on their merits. []`, so a read that had not answered yet rendered as a served empty: six "Nothing is …" teachings while `/api/runs` was still in flight, plus the board's own-queue and per-column empties and the fleet's no-lane-match. Filters, Workforce and TaskDetail already gated on `data && …`; the same gate now holds on all six, and `Freshness` owns the window as it always did. **The instrument was the worse half.** The three none-vs-not-loaded negatives written at landing installed `scriptedFetch({})`, which fails the SESSION read — so `App` mounted no surface at all and the assertions were looking at an empty `<main>`. They passed because there was nothing on screen, not because a gate held: a check that cannot observe the state it names. `Scripted` gained a `pending` route (one line of test wiring: the route returns a promise that never settles), so a test can land the session, mount the surface, leave the surface's OWN read in flight and look at exactly the window the rule is about. **Proved in both directions rather than argued: run against the pre-fix code the three new negatives FAIL, one per defective surface** (`Nothing of yours is queued.`, `No lane matches this filter.`, `Nothing is running.`), while the two already-correct surfaces pass — then the gate lands and all five go green. Each also drives the far side: once the read answers EMPTY, the teaching state is exactly what appears.
- **D2 — a present-tense alarm keyed to pure history, and the one banner site with no test.** The meters panel's stall banner fired on `meters.limit_events.answer.rows.length > 0`. #### The approval-row anatomy — five legs, and every one of them is a served field

- **The legs, mapped to the wire.** (1) **what's being approved** — `displayClass` over the served `kind` (byte-kept as the vocabulary) plus the served `tier`, `answerable` and `step_up_required` flags, now on the kit's `Chip` in the one chip formula; (2) **the mono provenance line** — card id, kind, owner and `observed_ts` in `font-mono tabular-nums`, which is exactly §47's "every number, id, timestamp and status token", with the expiry and the engine deadline riding it; (3) **what to check first** — class-grain teaching copy, below; (4) **the jump to the work** — the served `run_id` and nothing else; (5) **the verbs** — the landed served-actions row, state-computed exactly as landed. `.card-head` stays the leg-1 chip row, so the landed `flex-wrap: wrap` rule keeps doing the job `responsive.test.ts` asserts it does, and the other three legs are siblings beneath it.
- **"WHAT TO CHECK FIRST" IS CLASS-GRAIN, AND IT IS KEYED ONE LEVEL FINER THAN THE LABEL (OQ1 as disposed, with a recorded refinement).** The disposition is class-grain client-authored copy per R9, and that is what shipped: five lines, one per class, each true of every card in its class and naming no card fact whatsoever. **The refinement, recorded because it is a departure from the literal words "per display class":** `displayClass` has four labels and calls **every** `ask` a *question*, but R9 names distinct guidance for an S06.9 plan (read the assumptions and the will-NOT-do list) and for a decision card (the listed options are the whole answer). Keying the advice on the label would therefore have made one of those two lines FALSE. `checkClass` instead reads the served `kind` and, for an `ask`, the stored snapshot's own family through the landed `answerEnvelope` — the same declaration `CardContent` dispatches on. Nothing new is derived and no card fact is named; the grain is the card's own.
- **A class this file has never seen gets NO line, and that is the honest arm.** An unknown kind keeps its row, its provenance line and its served verbs (the §42 forward tolerance), and gets no guidance, because guidance nobody wrote for it could only be invented. Driven with a fabricated `quorum_vote` card and **bite-proven**. **The plant form matters, and it is recorded exactly (drain r1, D4c): `checkClass`'s fall-through must be made to return a NON-EMPTY class — `return 'question'` fires the named test.** The tempting plant, `return item.kind`, does **not** fire, and the reason is a second gate rather than a weak assertion: `checkFirst` looks the class up in its own five-arm table and returns `''` for anything it does not recognize, so a fabricated kind still renders no line. #### The CSS shed, consumer-verified rule by rule — and the cascade fact that bounded it

- **⚠ REPORTED, MEASURED, AND THE REASON THE SHED IS SMALLER THAN THE BRIEF ANTICIPATED: the owned stylesheet is UNLAYERED, so it beats every Tailwind utility.** `@import 'tailwindcss'` puts utilities in `@layer utilities`; every owned rule below the token block is unlayered, and in the CSS cascade an unlayered rule from an origin beats a layered one from that origin **regardless of specificity**. Verified in the SHIPPED artefact rather than argued. **DATED CORRECTION 2026-08-05 (drain r1, D4a): the offsets first recorded here — utilities 9571–28895, the owned rule at 32793 — were read off an INTERMEDIATE build and do not reproduce on the committed sources, which is the one thing a byte offset must do.** Re-measured on the FINAL committed build: the `@layer utilities{…}` block spans bytes **9620–30252** and contains `.m-0{`, while the owned `p,dl,dd,ul,ol,blockquote{margin:.6em 0}` sits at byte **34150** and the owned `input,select,button{…}` chrome at byte **39507** — both outside every layer. The evaluator's independent build reproduces these exactly; a figure that only reproduced on the machine that wrote it was a checkable claim that did not check out. **Consequences, stated so no later packet re-derives them:** (1) a utility can never override an owned ELEMENT rule — `label`'s flex-column, `ul,ol`'s list-style and padding, `h1..h4`'s and `p/dl/dd`'s margins, and the global `input,select,button` chrome; (2) so the kit `Button`'s variant colours (`border-transparent`, the identity gradient, `text-primary-foreground`) are currently suppressed by the unlayered `input,select,button { border; background; color; width:100% }` rule on **every** surface that has mounted one since §48 — the kit's layout, height, focus ring, disabled treatment and `motion-safe` gating do apply, its palette does not. **This packet did not fix it and deliberately did not work around it.** The fix is either the owned sheet moving into a cascade layer below `utilities`, or the global element rules leaving with the last raw form (§47's ledger puts that at UI-7) — and either one changes the rendering of every frozen surface at once, which is a STOP-and-flag rather than something to smuggle into a four-surface packet. What this packet DID do is refuse to ship class strings that provably do nothing: every utility added and then found inert was removed again, and the owned rules it could not replace were kept rather than shed with an inert utility left standing in their place.
- **KEPT, each with its named reason.** The phone-first LAYOUT contract stays in the sheet, rule for rule, unrenamed — the §51 recorded-deviation precedent applied unchanged, and the reason it is right here too: `responsive.test.ts` and `sweep.test.tsx`'s duty table are written against these rules, and re-pointing them onto utility-source reads is exactly the "selector updated, predicate gone vacuous" hazard the batch names first. Both suites therefore pass **byte-unmodified**. Kept: the sweep's duty containers `.cards` · `.card-row` · `.batch-bar` · `.push-device` · `.push-devices`; the no-fixed-width walk's `.panel` · `.pair` · `.pair-side` · `.settings-cats` · `.cat-panel` · `.setting` · `.setting-group`; the property-bearing `.card-head` (flex-wrap) · `.card-id` (overflow-wrap) · `.render` (overflow-x) · `.acts` + `.acts .buttons` (flex-wrap) · `.cat-tabs` (flex-wrap) · the `.setting-acts`/`.bounds-editor`/`.per-user-editor`/`.add-price-row` group (flex-column, plus its wide-query arm) · the `.setting-help`/`.setting-key`/`.audit-rows li`/`.deferred li` group (overflow-wrap). #### §52 drain round 1 (P3-UI-6 drain r1, D1–D4) — the jump leg becomes a real door, a login line that spoke for software it does not control, an untested honest absence, and three record truths

The fresh-context evaluation returned FAIL on 1 LOW + 4 nits, having first reproduced the battery byte-exact, **proved the addition-only claim by numstat**, re-proved both planted bites with its own plants, and **adjudicated BOTH reported findings TRUE with mechanism evidence** — the run→task 404 is structural (task ids are `t-<hex8>` and dotless, run ids are `<task_id>.<stage>[.gN]`, so overlap is impossible by construction), and the unlayered `input,select,button` rule beats every `@layer utilities` rule before specificity is consulted, suppressing the kit `Button`'s border, background gradient, colour, font and padding and imposing its width across 11 surfaces. **The refusal to smuggle either fix was upheld.** The cascade is dispositioned OUT of this round and is now a named UI-7 row requirement; it was not touched. Four items triaged, four applied, none refused.

- **D1 (the LOW) — SANCTIONED: the third narrow backend change of the batch, and the jump leg becomes a door that opens.** The §48-OQ1 class, dated. `ApprovalItem` gains an additive `task_id`, resolved **server-side from the run row the card already names** — `fillTaskRefs` in `internal/api/approvals.go` runs ONE `SELECT run_id, COALESCE(task_id,'') FROM runs WHERE run_id IN (…)` over the page's distinct run ids and fills the field. **The projector reads what the run row already stores and derives nothing**, which is the whole point: the mapping lives in exactly one place, and teaching the client to parse `<task_id>.<stage>` out of a run id would have been a second implementation of it, free to disagree. No new route, no new event, no store, no handler and **no scoping change** — the subject is a run this caller has already been served a card for, so re-filtering it here would have been a second authority model beside the one that decided the card was theirs.
- **THE SANCTIONED TOUCHED SET, exact, and every other wall held.** `internal/api/approvals.go` (**+62 / −1**: one struct field with its doc, one call site, one helper) · `internal/api/approvals_test.go` (test-only, +56) · `web/src/api.ts` (**+7**: the `task_id?` transcription and its doc) · `web/src/fixtures/api/approvals.json` and `approvals-mine.json` (regenerated). Verified against the landing commit `476f5c1`: **no other production `.go` file and no other fixture moved at all**, and every wall-1 path outside the sanction is still byte-identical to the pre-packet `0255668` — `App.tsx`, `parts.tsx`, `controls.tsx`, `push.ts`, `sw.js`, `shell.test.tsx`, `sw.test.ts`, `sweep.test.tsx`, `responsive.test.ts` included.
- **THE FIXTURES REGENERATED THROUGH THE REAL PROJECTOR, AND THE CURSOR CHECK IS STATED: `cursor` stayed 89.** No event is minted by a read, so the head could not move, and it did not — checked across **every** committed body, not only the two that changed: no body carries a cursor other than 89. The diff is **purely additive** — 10 and 11 insertions, **zero deletions** — and every card that names a run resolved a task (11/11 in the operator's body, 10/10 in alice's). Cards that name no run — the blind pair, the memory conflict — gained nothing, which is the design.
- **THE NON-VACUITY THE OLD LINK NEVER HAD.** A href test asserts the shape of a string and would have passed against the broken link for a year. ### The cascade record — the fix, what it un-suppresses, and the proof jsdom cannot give

- **THE FIX CLASS (OQ3 as disposed, the row amendment's first arm).** Everything below the token / `@theme` / kill-switch blocks — the preflight-compat block, the content and shared sections, and every per-surface section — is wrapped in **`@layer base { … }`**. `base` is Tailwind's own second layer (`theme, base, components, utilities`), so no order statement is needed, and the owned rules still beat Tailwind's preflight because they sit later in source order **inside the same layer**. The scoping alternative was not available as a whole fix: the `form`/`label`/`input,select,button` chrome still serves every frozen surface's raw forms (§52 :1778), and those surfaces do not open here.
- **THE DIFF IS PURELY ADDITIVE — `index.css` +38 / −0 at the fix commit.** No owned rule was deleted, renamed, re-ordered or re-indented by the fix itself; deletion is the restyle's separate consumer-verified business, which is A2's.
- **THE CONTENTS ARE DELIBERATELY NOT RE-INDENTED, and that is a finding rather than a style choice.** `design.test.ts:17`, `responsive.test.ts:17` and `sweep.test.tsx:798` all locate a rule with `css.indexOf('\n<selector> {')` — **line-start anchored**. Indenting the block by two spaces would have made every one of those locators **FAIL LOUDLY** — `indexOf` returns −1 and the suite reports "<selector> is not styled at all" — on a commit whose whole claim is that it changes no behavior. **DATED CORRECTION 2026-08-05 (A1 evaluation, N1): this said "silently re-pointed", which names the wrong failure mode; these locators do not degrade quietly, they cannot find the rule and say so.** The decision stands unchanged and for the same reason — the fix must not move a landed test — so the wrapper adds two lines and touches no other byte. The reason is written at the block, because the next reader's instinct will be to tidy it.
- **THE REDUCED-MOTION KILL SWITCH STAYS UNLAYERED, on purpose.** For `!important` declarations the layer order is **REVERSED** — unlayered important is the WEAKEST — so moving it into `base` would have strengthened a backstop nobody asked to strengthen. It clamps motion and competes with no utility, so it was left exactly as it was. R1's own words ("the `@keyframes`/media machinery move only as the mechanism requires") are what this follows.
- **THE SENTENCE THIS PACKET OWES, recorded verbatim-equivalent: SOURCE stays byte-frozen; the RENDERED LOOK of every surface changes by design.** That is what a tree-wide cascade change means, and it is why the frozen-surface walls and the visual record are not in tension.
- **⚠ THE DIST-CSS GUARD, AND ITS PRE-FIX BITE.** `internal/webui/cascade_test.go` (**test-only Go; the production `.go` counter is still zero**) reads the **real embedded stylesheet** and asserts the **RELATIONSHIP, never a byte offset** — §52 D4a's lesson, that offsets read off an intermediate build did not reproduce, which is the one thing a byte offset must do. It asserts: the sheet declares a `utilities` layer; that layer really carries a compiled utility (`.m-0{`) so the ordinal comparison cannot hold over a sheet that compiled nothing; and each owned marker (`input,select,button{`, `p,dl,dd,`) sits inside a layer block whose name the sheet's own layer order places **before** `utilities`. **Bite recorded in both directions: run against the pre-packet build it FAILS, naming both markers UNLAYERED; it passes against the post-fix build.**
- **IT IS HOMED IN GO FOR A MEASURED REASON, not a preference.** The battery order is `typecheck → test → build`, so a vitest reading `dist/` would read the **previous** build and could pass over a sheet that no longer exists. The Go suite runs after the web build, over the real embedded bytes.
- **⚠ THE SCANNER FOUND ITS OWN DEFECT FIRST, and it is worth keeping.** The first version skipped quoted strings so a brace inside `content:"{"` could not desync the depth count — and it reported "the sheet declares no `utilities` layer". The real sheet carries a Tailwind-generated selector of the form `.\"\]:before`, an **escaped quote outside a string**, which the skipper read as a string opener; it swallowed ~20 kB and lost the utilities layer entirely. **An instrument that silently loses the layer it is measuring reports "no defect" for the wrong reason.** CSS backslash escapes apply outside strings, the scanner now handles them, and that exact shape is one of its five planted probes.
- **WHAT THE FIX UN-SUPPRESSES, MEASURED IN A REAL BROWSER over the real served dist — because jsdom computes no cascade and §52-B is the proven cost of that blind spot.** The same probe ran against the pre-fix and post-fix builds on a throwaway control plane (dev posture, empty database, production untouched), over ten routes, reading `getComputedStyle`:
  - **primary**: `background-image` **none → the identity gradient**, border → transparent, colour → `--primary-foreground`, padding `8px → 12/16px` — on Fleet, Settings, Memory and Login.
  - **secondary**: background `rgb(7,7,13)` → `--secondary`, padding `8px → 12px` — on Mission control, Filters, Fleet and Inbox.
  - **ghost**: border and background → transparent, colour → `--muted-foreground`.
  - **THE TWO NEGATIVE LEGS, which are what prove the change is bounded: 48 native, utility-less controls — 0 changed. 15 bare-element type-rhythm samples (h1/h2/h3/p/ul/ol/dd) — 0 changed.** An unlayered→layered move only changes winners where a utility competes, and the measurement says exactly that.
  - Screenshots of the built artifact confirm it by eye: the "Create operator" primary really carries the violet→cyan gradient, and the native inputs beside it really keep the owned chrome.
  - **NOT COVERED HERE, honestly: `/tasks/:id` and `/deliverables/:id`.** Both need rows an empty database does not have, so the TaskDetail and Deliverable Button consumers were not visually walked. That is precisely the gap the seeded world (R17, seam C) exists to close, and the check belongs to the packet that lands it.
- **ALL 668 LANDED TESTS PASSED THE FIX COMMIT UNMODIFIED.** jsdom computes no cascade, so a landed test that had moved on that commit would itself have been a finding. None did.

### The A-2 assistant card, in operator words

- **ONE RENDERER, TWO CONSUMERS, and both stayed green.** The rework is `AnswerView`'s disambiguation branch in `History.tsx`, consumed by the History panel (`MissionControl.tsx`, its view-answer arm) and by Chat (**the `<AnswerView` mount inside `AnswerOutcome`, `Chat.tsx`** — CORRECTED at the A2 landing 2026-08-05, re-check N1: this said `ChatAnswer`, a component that does not exist; the misnaming was the cite-accuracy class recurring inside its own correction, caught because the structural form fails loudly). Both surfaces' landed pins pass. **DATED CORRECTION 2026-08-05 (A1 evaluation N2, then A2 drain r1 D4): this first cited `Chat.tsx:594`, the pre-packet line, because the head rework moved the mount in the same commit that wrote the cite. It was corrected to `:600` — and the A2 restyle immediately moved it again, to `:637`, so the correction re-broke on the very next commit and repeated the exact defect class it describes. Both cites are therefore now LINE-INDEPENDENT and name the enclosing structure instead, which is what a cite into a file under active restyle has to be to survive one.**
- **GROUPING IS PRESENTATION, and it is the shell's own algorithm.** `choiceRuns` cuts the served choices into the **consecutive runs** that share a served `category` — deliberately the `navSections()` class (App.tsx) — so order in is order out, every choice renders exactly once, and a choice whose category is empty gets its own **unlabelled** run rather than being folded under its neighbour's heading. The property is asserted directly: the flattened rendered list equals the served list **in order and in count**.
- **⚠ A LANDED ASSERTION WAS PASSING FOR THE WRONG REASON, and it was strengthened rather than left alone.** `mission.test.tsx:429` asserted the served `category` by checking `li.textContent`. In the golden body **every choice's category is `cost` and every query starts with `cost.`**, so that predicate contained the category whether or not the category ever rendered — and it would have kept passing after the rework moved the category to a group heading. It now asserts the category on the element that carries it (`[data-choice-group]` and its heading), and **the coincidence is asserted to still be a coincidence** so the next reader knows why the obvious check is not the one used. Bite-proven: dropping the heading fires this test *and* the grouping test.
- **THE DEGRADED-MODE SENTENCE, narrowed to what the wire allows (proposal §7 amendment A1.1).** The wire carries **no machine cause code** — a `Disambiguation` is `{question, reason, choices[]}` (api.ts:202–206) — and the store serves this card for at least **seven** distinct reason classes (internal/history/layer1.go :155/:178/:190/:202/:210/:232/:256/:264). Classifying served prose is banned (§38). So the proposal's illustrative *"no local model is wired, so I can't read sentences yet"* **cannot ship as unconditional client copy**, and it does not. What ships is client words true of every class — this is a list rather than an answer, **nothing was run**, and picking one selects that question for you to ask — beside the platform's **own served `reason`, rendered verbatim and alone as the SOLE statement of cause**.
- **THE OVERCLAIM NEGATIVES ARE FIRED AGAINST THE CLIENT'S WORDS ALONE, which is the only way they can bite.** The served reason legitimately contains "not wired"; if the negatives ran over the whole card they would be unfalsifiable. They run over `[data-card-words]`: no "not wired", no "local model", no "local tier", no free-generation promise, and no claim that anything ran — with the control that the served reason really does carry those cause words, so the negatives are discriminating. **Bite-proven**: restoring the proposal's illustrative sentence fires the test.
- **WHAT DID NOT CHANGE, because the landed pins are the contract.** The served `question`, `reason` and every choice's `query`/`category`/`description` render **verbatim**; a choice **SELECTS and never fires** (§50's contract — the picker fills, its slots render empty, the person asks deliberately, and the card is not cleared because it is the context the choice was made in); the card renders as an **ANSWER** and never through the error banner; the escalation act and its `layer < 2` gate are untouched.

### The three-verb head

- **The landed line named two verbs of three.** It said ask and start-a-task, and left out **file exchange** — a verb this surface really has. The head now takes the landed `SurfaceHead` treatment (no new `parts.tsx` export was needed) and states the A-2 contract in operator words: ask about the platform and the work it is doing · hand something over as a task for intake to shape · exchange files with it — plus the fact that makes the conversation rail worth having, that conversations live on the platform.
- **Its overclaims are asserted absent:** no free-form generation is promised, because by S15.7 / S14.10 design none exists, and nothing claims the assistant edits anything. **Bite-proven**: restoring the landed two-verb line fires the test.

- **THE WALLS HELD, byte-proven against `8595174`.** Every wall-1 path is byte-identical, `Deliverable.tsx` · `Memory.tsx`'s frozen neighbours · `Inbox.tsx` · `MissionControl.tsx` · `parts.tsx` · every `web/src/ui/*` (including `ui/Toast.tsx`, which this seam MOUNTS and does not touch) · `api.ts` · `controls.tsx` · `chatFacts.ts` · `chatRuntime.ts` · every production `.go` · `Spec/` · all **52** fixtures · the package files · **`shell.test.tsx` unopened** (so the C-1/login pins pass unmodified and the :401–402 comment stays on the standing list) · **`sweep.test.tsx`, `responsive.test.ts`, `design.test.ts`, `scans.test.ts` byte-unchanged**.

The session machinery, `useConnection`, `navGroupOf`/`navIcons`, every route arm and the C-1 arms are byte-region untouched.

##### ⚠ The finding: a second stream subscriber inside the shell tree makes EVERY surface read twice

- **The etiquette's first shape mounted its own subscriber as a component inside the shell.** The full battery caught it immediately: `workforce.test.tsx` failed with **two** `GET /api/workforce` calls where its landed assertion pins exactly one. The mechanism is the landed rule that test's own comment states — **the FIRST subscriber OPENS the source and reads once; every later one JOINS and is handed an immediate synchronous `connected` resnapshot, so it reads twice** (§44-B drain r1 D7, restated at §45). React commits child effects before the parent's, so a subscriber rendered inside the shell tree commits BEFORE the surfaces' hooks and becomes the opener — inverting the ordering the whole tree is built on and costing every surface an extra read of its own snapshot.
- **The fix is structural rather than positional.** There is now exactly **ONE** etiquette subscription, and it lives in `useEtiquette`, which runs in App's OWN effect — the same place `useConnection` subscribes, which React commits after its children's. The toast sink is still a component inside the provider, because `useToast` reads the provider's manager, but it **subscribes to nothing**: it drains a bounded queue the hook fills. Asserted directly — the sink's source contains no `.subscribe(`, and the module holds exactly one subscription tree-wide.
- **Recorded because the tempting fix is the wrong one:** moving the component later in the JSX would also have made the tests pass, and would have left the invariant depending on render order. It is worth the extra queue to have the ordering be a property of where the hook is called.

##### The etiquette, on the ratified sets only

- **DOTS: chat ← `chat.turn_settled`/`chat.turn_abandoned`; inbox ← the six card-OPENING types.** Every one is asserted to be a type `live.ts` already declares, and the six **closing** types (`decision.recorded`, `run.state_changed`, `watchdog.suppressed`, `watchdog.annotated`, `benchmark.pair_recorded`, `eval.score_recorded`) are asserted ABSENT — a dot says "something is waiting for you", and a card LEAVING the queue is not that. Lighting one on a removal would send somebody to look at nothing, which teaches people to ignore dots. **Bite-proven**: adding `decision.recorded` to the set fires two tests.
- **NO COUNTS, and the dot clears on route entry.** The rendered link is asserted to carry no digit at all: frames are triggers and REST is the truth (§42), so a count derived from frames could disagree with the queue the person then opens, and a figure that can be wrong is worse than a dot that cannot be.
- **NO MEMORY DOT, for a structural reason rather than a display preference.** Knowledge frames are owner-scoped to the WRITER, so an open memory conflict reaches its addressee through no frame at all (`live.ts` records this for the inbox's ninth kind). A memory dot would light for your own writes and stay dark for exactly the case that needs you — wrong in the direction that matters. **Bite-proven**: adding a memory entry to the route map fires the test.
- **TOASTS: the chat turn lifecycle ONLY, suppressed on-route** (proposal §7 amendment A1.3). The copy states only what the TYPE NAME carries, and the door rides the kit's own frozen `Toast.Action` slot handing the route change to the ROUTER (§48 OQ2: cross-link, never re-implement). **NO run or deliverable toast**: a frame carries `seq/run_id/user_id/type/topics/ts` and an OPAQUE payload, so "your run finished" would invent the one word that matters, and a deliverable toast has no honest link target without reading a payload the shell may not interpret. **Bite-proven**: removing the on-route suppression fires the test.
- **NO NEW READ AND NO CONNECTION CHANGE.** Asserted with a type no mounted surface declares, because the obvious choice would have measured the wrong thing: `engine.gate_ask` is in `boardEventTypes`, so mission control re-reads on it **by design**, and a naive assertion there would have reported a defect that is landed behaviour. `chat.turn_settled` is in no oversight set, so any read after it would be the etiquette's own — there is none. Structurally: the module imports no API client and contains no `fetch(`. The connection URL is asserted to carry no `topics=`.

##### The tour

- **OWNED JSX, NO LIBRARY, and it NEVER auto-starts.** Nothing in this client persists, so a tour that started itself would ambush every load with no way to remember it had. One visible shell-header affordance starts it and nothing else can — asserted to be exactly one. Escape ends it from any step, and so does the visible End tour control. No timer, no storage, no ⚙ key; the ring's motion is a `motion-safe:` utility, and every import is this tree's own or React.
- **THE VERB WALL, structurally, with its planted bite.** Two classes only — `nav` (a real route-changing anchor) and `disclosure` (fires nothing, or a GET). The registry is checked against that list and **a planted verb-class step fires the check**. Beyond the declared class, what the selectors really SELECT is checked on live pages: a `nav` step must resolve to an `<a href>`, and no step may resolve to a submit, to anything inside a `<form>`, to an act-outcome region or to a verb button.
- **THE ZERO-NON-GET WALK.** A walk over every registered step fires no non-GET request at all, with the fetch log as the evidence and a non-vacuity check that the walk reached something.
- **REAL CLICKS, OVER AN EMPTY DATABASE.** One route's walk advances by clicking the spotlit controls themselves — the listener only ever OBSERVES the target, never calls it, never `preventDefault()`s it and never synthesizes a second activation — and the third click really navigates. Every mission-control step's target is asserted present with every list emptied, because **the tour ships to production where the seeded world never exists**: it spotlights chrome, never data rows.
- **TWO REGISTRY CORRECTIONS the tests forced, both honest.** The connection step first targeted `[data-connection]`, an attribute `ConnectionState` does not render — a step that could never point at anything. It targets the real `p.conn`. And the rail step was classed `nav` while resolving to a `<nav>` CONTAINER; it fires nothing, so it is `disclosure`, and only a real anchor is `nav`.
- **ONE MECHANISM FOR "NOTHING TO POINT AT".** The first shape gated the overlay on the step's route matching the current one, which meant a cross-route step rendered **nothing at all** — the silent case a teaching layer must not have, and it also made the visible-skip path unreachable. The gate is gone: the overlay renders whenever the tour runs, and a target that is not on the page — whether because it belongs to another surface or because an empty database has not produced it — takes the ONE honest path, a card that says there is nothing to point at and a button that says *Skip this step*. The chat-head step is scoped to `.chat-head` for the same reason: a bare `[data-surface-what]` matches whatever surface the reader is on, so it could never be absent and the skip path would never be exercised.

The fresh evaluation returned FAIL on **1 HIGH + 4 LOW + 3 nits**, having first verified the structural subscriber fix by planting its own child-tree subscriber and watching the workforce one-read pin fire, checked the signal sets byte-exact in both directions, and reproduced the bundle split with its own `ToastProvider`-stub build. So hit-testing landed **every click outside the tour card on the root**: the spotlit control could never be pressed, click-to-advance could never fire, a nav step could never navigate, and every cross-route step degraded into the skip card. **All eight tour tests passed over it because jsdom does no hit-testing** — it dispatches straight at the target — which is the §52-B hazard class landing on the very seam whose own record claimed "REAL CLICKS". The root now carries `pointer-events-none` and the card `pointer-events-auto`; the aurora field is this tree's own precedent for pass-through chrome. **PROVEN THREE WAYS, as the disposition required:** (i) a structural pin on both elements with its probe; (ii) the jsdom walk still green; (iii) **a REAL-Chrome click-through over the served dist** — `document.elementFromPoint` at the spotlit control's centre returns `topElement: "a"`, `topIsOverlayRoot: false`, `targetContainsHit: true`, and a coordinate-dispatched `Input.dispatchMouseEvent` advanced the tour `nav → connection`. **The bite was measured the same way against a deliberately reverted build: the top element is the covering div, `targetContainsHit: false`, and the real click does NOT advance (`nav → nav`).** (Recorded precisely: the revert restored the root's default only, so the element on top in the bite build is the scrim rather than the root — the mechanism and the outcome are identical, and claiming it reproduced the exact original element would be a claim nobody checked.) The in-code comment and the §53 bullet now say what is proven rather than what was assumed.

- **⚠ D4 — the queue overflow was a SILENT DROP, and fixing it exposed a second problem.** `slice(-keptRequests)` discarded the oldest undrained requests with no marker — a silent cap, which is the one thing the no-silent-caps invariant forbids, and the kit's own stack models the right answer one layer down (`data-limited`: hidden, never dropped). The overflow now **collapses into the oldest surviving entry**, which carries the count and says so: *"N earlier completions are not shown separately."* **The second problem, found while driving it:** the sink never removed what it had shown, so the queue kept every request forever and the overflow would have "absorbed" entries that had **already been on screen** — a figure that over-reports is worse than none. The sink now drains what it fires, so the queue holds only what has NOT been shown and the figure is exactly the number of completions nobody ever saw. Driven as a real BURST (twelve frames inside one `act`, so React batches and the sink cannot drain between them): twelve driven, eight kept, `4 earlier completions` reported.

##### §53 C-1 drain round 1 (D1–D5) — bytes that did not outlive the process that minted them

The fresh evaluation returned FAIL on **1 HIGH + 2 LOW + 2 nits**, having first verified both wall mutations fire naming the file, the shipped binary strings-clean, all three refusal locks driven, the 15th skip, the split's zero-drift regeneration, and the script twice with production untouched. Five items triaged, five applied, none refused.

- **⚠ D1 (HIGH) — the seeded review surface could not serve its diff or its anchored comments, and the metadata endpoint hid it.** `GET /api/deliverables/d-site/comments` and `/compare` both answered **500** on the real binary — `review: object 7a2204ee…: open <STATE>/review/objects/…: no such file or directory` — with no `$STATE/review/` on disk at all. **The cause is exactly the hazard this file's own B6-8 note already warns about, one process further out.** The C-1 split threaded `root` into the knowledge store and nothing else, so `fixtureReview` still rooted the content-addressed object store at `t.TempDir()`, as did the project root, the portpool, the preview scratch and the chat exchange. `t.TempDir()` is removed when the test binary exits, which is invisible and harmless while the same process both mints and serves — every committed fixture is produced that way — and **fatal the moment a world is seeded for a DIFFERENT process to serve: the database keeps the rows and the bytes are gone.** The throwaway DB held 13 revisions and 7 anchored comments, seeded and unservable.
- **THE FIX IS THE ROOT-THROUGH DISCIPLINE EXTENDED TO EVERY FILE-BACKED STORE.** `backend` gains a `root`; `fixtureWorldOn` records it; one helper, `fixtureRoot(t, b, name)`, names each store's directory beneath it and falls back to a per-store `t.TempDir()` when no world is composed. Review objects, projects, portpool, preview scratch, exchange, push state and workers all route through it. **Behaviour-preserving in both directions, and proven rather than argued: the 52 golden fixtures regenerate with ZERO drift at `cursor` 89 again.**
- **RE-VERIFIED THROUGH THE REAL BINARY, endpoint by endpoint** — the check the first pass should have been: `/api/deliverables/d-site` 200 · `/comments` **200 with 7 rows, every one anchored** · `/compare` **200** · `/compare?old=1&new=2` **200**, serving a real unified diff over two files with real hunks. The directories now exist on disk beside the database (`review/ projects/ exchange/ portpool/ workers/ push-state/ knowledge/`).
- **A MEASUREMENT LESSON WORTH KEEPING:** the first verification asked the one endpoint that needs no file. Every read that *did* need one was 500, and a green on the cheapest endpoint was taken for a green on the surface. When a claim is "this surface is reachable", the check has to be the reads the surface actually makes.
- **D2 — the owner-scoping record described an intention, and the claim was half-false.** §53 said the walk doc "names the owner-scoping the walk will meet"; the edit never landed in the script, so it named nothing. And the claim was wrong on one of its two halves: `/api/chat/sessions` really is empty for the dev fallback, but `/api/memory` serves it **7 house-scope entries** — house defaults address everyone, which is the API's own visibility sentence. The walk doc now states each surface's real answer separately, and the seed leg's line no longer claims "every surface below has rows to show".
