##### ⚠ Two findings the restyle surfaced, both fixed, both recorded

- **⚠ THE ACCEPT CARD WAS BORROWING THE WORKFORCE MAP'S `.provenance` GRID.** `.provenance` is the S15.10 workforce rule — `display: grid` with a grid column template and its own margin, written for a `<dl>` — and `AcceptCardView` rendered `<p className="muted provenance">`, a paragraph of prose, under the same class. So a cross-section selector had been silently laying out the accept card's provenance line since B6-8. `Workforce.tsx` is byte-frozen, so **the rule stays for its real owner and the class was DROPPED from Deliverable**, which now carries its own mono/tabular utilities on `[data-provenance="accept-card"]`. A test pins both halves: the class is gone from the card, and Workforce still renders it.
- **⚠ `diff-widget` IS ALSO react-diff-view's OWN CLASS.** The adopted widget mounts its rows as `<tr class="diff-widget">`, and our own inner `<div className="diff-widget">` sits inside one — so the owned `.diff-widget` rule (a .35rem/.5rem padding and a 3px left rail in `currentColor`) MATCHED both. The rule is shed and the presentation now lands once, on our element, leaving the adopted stylesheet to style its own DOM (adopt-don't-fork). The class name is unchanged, because the landed pins select `.diff-widget [data-comment]` and reach ours either way — the new test selects `[data-widget-key]` instead, with the reason written at it.

  **DATED CORRECTION 2026-08-05 (C-2 drain r1, D4): this bullet said the rule was "painting BOTH, applying one rail and one padding twice", which overstates the defect by one property — only the RAIL ever doubled.** react-diff-view's `.diff` table collapses its borders (its own stylesheet sets that border model to `collapse`), and under the collapsed model a border set on a table **row** box IS painted — so the 3px rail really was drawn on the adopted `<tr>` and again on our div inside it. But **padding does not apply to a table row box at all**, so the row's padding was never painted and only our div's ever was. Matching a rule and painting it are not the same thing, and the record claimed painting. The mechanism, the shed and the fix are unchanged; the count of doubled properties is **one, not two**. The in-code comment at `deliverable.test.tsx` carried the same overstatement and is trued there too, dated.

  **⚠ And writing that correction found a live gotcha worth its own line, because it bit this drain first.** Tailwind's source scan reaches **prose**, not just class attributes — the first draft of the two corrections above spelled the hyphenated CSS property and display-value literals out in ordinary sentences, and the rebuild compiled **two new and permanently dead rules into the production sheet** (`.border-collapse{…}` and `.table-row{…}`, +71 bytes) out of the SCANNED TEST FILE'S comment alone (CORRECTED at the C-2 landing 2026-08-05, re-check R1: the first record said "and a Markdown paragraph", which the re-check DISPROVED BY PLANT — `P3/CONVENTIONS.md` is not a Tailwind-scanned source, planting the same tokens there compiles nothing and the sheet stays byte-identical; this note's own backticked literals sitting here with zero sheet effect are the standing counterexample; the error direction was overcaution about .md files, but a mechanism fact in a teaching note must be plant-verified, this note's own standard). Both notes are now written without bare literals in the scanned file, and the built sheet is byte-identical to C-2's again — same `sha256`, same `index-kiCmlWw5.css` / `index-8ixY4gSm.js` content hashes — verified by rebuilding rather than by reasoning. (Two rules already in the sheet look like the same mechanism from an earlier packet — `.table` and `.hidden` are compiled while no production `.tsx` puts either in a `className` — but this drain did not trace their origin and does not claim it; `.grid` and `.block`, which look similar, have 7 and 3 real markup consumers and are not examples of anything.) **The rule for later packets: a hyphenated utility-shaped token left bare in any scanned file — a test comment included — ships a rule.** Rebuild and diff the built `@layer utilities` block before believing that a doc-only or test-only change moved nothing.

##### The teaching layer (R11/R12), and two more §51-D1 gates that were real

- **R11 — the head.** `SurfaceHead` (no new `parts.tsx` export needed) states the five verbs this surface really has and the one thing worth warning about: *"Review one deliverable end to end: read the revisions the platform minted, compare one round against another, comment on a line or on the whole file, try the built thing in a frame, and accept a revision when it is right. An accept pushes a commit under your own credentials, and nothing on this page takes one back."* **Overclaims asserted ABSENT over the client's own line:** *approved*, *signed off*, *sign-off*, *reversible*, *undo*, *revert*, *roll back* — because approval state is served PER ARTIFACT (§38 ruling (a)) and no verb at any shape un-accepts a revision. A length floor keeps the negatives from passing over an empty line.
- **⚠ R12 — TWO §51-D1 GATES, and both were live defects.** `CommentsBlock` read `feed.data?.comments ?? []` and `LiveSessions` read `feed.data?.sessions ?? []`, so a read still in flight rendered as a served empty: the surface taught *"Nobody has commented on this revision yet."* and *"No preview session is running."* about questions the platform had not answered — and the strip additionally asserted that *every* comment had a live position over a list nobody had been sent. Both are now gated on `feed.data !== null`, with `Freshness` owning the window. **Bite-proven through `doubles.ts`'s `pending` route in both directions**: restoring either `?? []` shape fires its negative by name, and each test additionally proves the surface really mounted and really asked (the instrument §51 D1 had to fix).
- **FOUR sites migrate to the kit's `EmptyState`, and two deliberately do NOT.** Migrated with a `why` that teaches what makes a row appear: the revision list, the comment list, the door list, the preview-session list. Kept `Empty`-grade per R12's own "only where a teaching `why` is true and useful": *"The platform served no diff text for this pair"* is a mid-form absence whose reason is already in its own sentence, and *"Every comment on this revision has a live position in the diff above"* is a POSITIVE statement about the comments that do exist rather than an empty list. The try-it and accept absences stay `Absent` — they render the SERVER's own reason for a closed door, which is not an empty list and would lose that reason in an `EmptyState`. `Empty` therefore keeps live consumers and is NOT retired.

##### ⚠ The carried hazard, answered the other way round — and a standing guard for it

- **THE MECHANISM, restated because this seam is where it was most likely to bite:** since the cascade fix the owned sheet sits in `@layer base`, so an owned rule — **media-gated or not** — LOSES to `@layer utilities`. A2's `.chat-verbs` is the instance that shipped: a `flex-col` utility killed the owned wide-screen arm and **no jsdom test in the tree could see it.** The review surface has **seven** elements of exactly that shape (`.deliverable .rev-picker`, `.diff-controls`, `.image-modes`, `.port-picker`, `.frame-path`, `.two-up`, `.frames`), each with a live `flex-direction: row` arm at 48rem.
- **THE ANSWER HERE IS THE OPPOSITE OF A2's, and deliberately so.** A2 shed the owned rule and gave the breakpoint to a `md:` utility. That was not available here: `responsive.test.ts` is byte-frozen and reads these very rules, so **the rules stay and the elements carry no competing utility at all.** One source for the breakpoint either way; which one it is follows from which suite owns the pin.
- **The guard is PROPERTY-AWARE, and it had to be.** A first cut banned every layout utility on a kept element and immediately fired on `.merge-options`' own `mt-2 list-none ps-0` — utilities for properties that rule never declares. Banning them would have taught the next reader the wrong rule. The guard now **reads the banned property families off the sheet's own declarations** (base arm and wide arm), so it cannot drift from the rules it guards, and `.merge-options` is kept in the walk as the CONTROL that proves it discriminates rather than banning everything. It also re-asserts all nine `responsive.test.ts` selector/declaration pairs, so the shed carries its own tripwire against a byte-frozen suite. **Bite-proven**: planting `flex flex-col` on `.frames` fires it by name, on the `display` family.
- **AND IT WAS MEASURED IN A REAL BROWSER, which is the only place the answer exists.** At 1280px `.rev-picker` and `.diff-controls` compute `flex-direction: row; flex-wrap: wrap; align-items: center`; at 375px both compute `column`. **The arms are ALIVE. The `.chat-verbs` regression did not recur.**

##### ⚠ A legibility defect found by eye, proven LANDED, and fixed here

The three radio pickers were unreadable at desktop width. The sheet's global chrome makes every `label` a flex COLUMN and every `input` `width: 100%`; inside `.diff-controls`/`.image-modes`/`.port-picker` — flex ROWS at the breakpoint — that stacked a stretched radio ABOVE its own text and let the text overflow its column, so the shipped page read **"(o) (o) / Side by side  Inline"**: two radios adjacent, two labels adjacent, and nothing saying which belonged to which. **Proven LANDED rather than introduced here** — the label markup is byte-identical to the pre-packet file and the numstat shows no `+`/`-` line touching it. Fixed with `flex-row items-center gap-2` on the label and `w-auto` on the input, which after the cascade fix is the only shape the fix can take: an owned rule can no longer override a utility, so the winner has to be the utility. It competes with the GLOBAL chrome and with nothing this section keeps. **Re-measured in Chrome:** at 1280 the two labels sit on one line at 102px and 56px with the radio beside its own text, and `document.elementFromPoint` at the radio's centre returns that radio; at 375 they stack, still radio-beside-text.

##### Deviations, recorded under scrutiny

1. **The kit `Chip` is mounted for single-WORD statuses only** — the doors' open/closed. Every other status slot on this surface renders the platform's own MEANING SENTENCE (*"blocker — this triggers another round"*, *"drifted — the quote was found near, not at, the mapped position"*), and a sentence given the uppercase mono status-token treatment stops reading as a sentence. Those take a local `toneToken` string on the ONE chip formula (§47) over `--tone` instead. This is §53 A2's content-vs-status-token judgement applied the other way round, and it is a taste judgement a later packet may overrule without overruling a fact.
2. **Every tone map hands back `null` for a value this build has never seen**, and `null` renders the neutral treatment with no hue claimed — the §51 D5b rule (a status colour that disagrees with its own word is the one thing a status colour must not do). The deliverable STATE token claims no hue at all, because this build owns no map of that vocabulary.
3. **`reviewPanel` is a local string, not `parts.tsx`.** It carries the same resting look as A2's `chatPanel` — border, radius, `--panel-grad`, `--density-pad`, no motion, no hover — but the two files are the only consumers and hoisting a two-consumer string into the shared module would be a new export for no structural guarantee (§51's three-export deviation bought one; this would not). Recorded so a third consumer is the trigger to hoist it.
4. **Native, utility-less form controls keep the owned chrome on purpose** — the negative leg the A1 cascade record measured (48 native controls, 0 changed). The radio fix above is the ONE deliberate exception, and it is recorded as one.
5. **`textarea` gained chrome it never had.** It is the one form element the global `input, select, button` rule never covered, so every free-text box on this surface rendered the user agent's default beside inputs that carried the owned chrome. `reviewTextarea` gives it the same border, radius, surface and padding, plus the 4rem floor and `min-width: 0` the shed rule carried.

##### Measurements

- **Bundle, against the C-1 reference** (JS **1167.53** / gzip **352.48**, CSS **57.88** / **12.12**, `index.html` **1.80**, **15** fonts / 417.30): now **JS 1174.07 / gzip 354.02** (**+6.54 raw / +1.54 gzip**), **CSS 57.61 / 11.99** (**−0.27 raw / −0.13 gzip**), `index.html` **1.80** and the fonts **unchanged** (same 15 files). The JS step is copy-scale — the head line, four teaching `why` sentences, the tone maps, the utility class strings and the restyle's own comments — with **no new package** and no new primitive reaching the chunk (`Button`, `Chip` and `EmptyState` were already in it).
- **THE CSS MOVED BOTH WAYS and is itemized rather than netted:** the owned SOURCE sheet **SHED −989 bytes** (22,636 → 21,647 with comments stripped; **193 → 180 selector blocks**), and in the BUILT sheet Tailwind compiled **+510 bytes / +11 rules** of new utilities for the same markup with **zero rules vanished** — so the built sheet's −268 byte net is a shed and a compile, not a shrink. 6. **Run-grain completion toasts**, post-batch — they need a served state fact the frame does not carry today.
7. **A served cause code for the disambiguation card**, post-batch — the honest fix for A-2's degraded-mode sentence, and a backend change with its own sanction.
8. **The seed's lineage edge**, as an optional exit-walk nicety — it would make the one jsdom-only region walkable, and it is a seed change rather than a restyle one.

**The build stands where S19.5 put it: B6's frontend is built, and the batch that built it is closed.**

## 54. Recovery-lease liveness — the DEAD conjunction, the renewal duty & the fence (P3-RW-5; S02.5, S02.3, S02.2, S10.7/S10.8, S14.4)

The defect this settles, in one line: a live, human-paced interview run was reaped as DEAD by the recovery sweep while it was demonstrably advancing — it died 11 s after its lease expired, holding a checkpoint written 14 s earlier — because the lease was written ONCE at claim time and never renewed, and classification let that dead lease outrank fresh event-cursor evidence.

- **Two observations, two questions (the settled reading).** The **lease** is *holder liveness*: is a platform component driving this run right now? The **event cursor** is *progress evidence*: has this run appended anything lately? They are not substitutes, and the ladder now reads both. A long quiet engine call has a beating holder and no progress; a renewal gap on some path still leaves the cursor. Each mechanism alone would have fixed the incident; together each backstops the other's blind spot, and both ratified artifacts (⚙ `recovery.heartbeat`, S02.2's heartbeat cursor) stop being dead letters.
- **DEAD is a CONJUNCTION under an unknowable body** — refining §8's compressed "DEAD needs proof (corpse-failed) or a dead/absent lease" sentence; its *live-lease-is-always-honored* half is unchanged and strengthened. Under `UnitGone`/`UnitUnknown` a scanned run is DEAD only when the lease is dead-or-absent (suspend-aware, ⚙ `recovery.wake_grace` exactly as before) **AND** the newest `run_events` append is older than ⚙ `recovery.dead_after` (+ that pass's grace) **AND** there is nothing terminal to harvest. That is S02.5 step 2's own text — "unit gone/failed **with nothing newer to harvest**" — finally read whole; a checkpoint 14 s old is something newer. `UnitCorpseFailed` remains sufficient **on its own**, cursor recency notwithstanding: the body is conclusive, and P-T07-2's mandatory wrapper exit-record append means a corpse case can show a very recent event that is *death* evidence. Cursor freshness therefore gates DEAD **only** under an unknowable body. The reap bound is explicit and swept by test: not dead before `max(lease deadline, last event + dead_after) + grace`, dead on the first pass after.
- **The renewal duty belongs to whoever is DRIVING the advance** (the spec *gap* S02.2/G2 Def.2/S18 all presumed and no S-section ever assigned; recorded here per S00.9 rather than amended, since no ratified sentence contradicts it). The four driving layers hold: the **scheduler dispatch leg**, the **intake post-answer advance**, the **stage answer/resume drains**, and the **adapter driver's pump** (`Drive`/`DriveResume`/`DriveStage` — the one holder that covers a paid engine turn whose stream goes quiet for minutes). Each renews `runs.lease_deadline_ts = now + ⚙ recovery.dead_after` every ⚙ `recovery.heartbeat` — **this packet is that key's first consumer**, which is what makes the registry cross-check `dead_after ≥ 2× heartbeat` load-bearing: a holder survives at least one missed beat. The mechanics live in ONE helper, `run.LeaseKeeper` (start/stop, owns the ticker, `Hold` for an advance and `Beat` for a single-shot), in `internal/run` because all four layers already import it — the scheduler ↔ engine seam (§11) stays intact.
- **Renewal is fenced, and silence is the refusal.** `run.Store.RenewLeaseTx` applies only `WHERE generation = ?` **and** `state IN (claimed, running, draining)`; anything else is a silent no-op (`false, nil`) — never an error, because refusing a zombie holder must not fail the healthy path that superseded it. `Hold` pins the generation when it is taken, so **take a hold AFTER the transition that takes the run** (the parked→running resume bumps the generation) and a takeover underneath a running hold stops mattering by itself. `SetLeaseTx`'s claim-time semantics (S10.7) are byte-identical and `claimOne` is untouched.
- **A heartbeat is not progress.** Renewal is a lease-column update, appends NO `run_events` row (the `SetLeaseTx` property, kept and pinned by test), and stamps `heartbeat_event_seq` with the run's newest `event_seq` — S02.2's "last event_seq the holder asserted", giving that column its first honest writer and making the lease row self-describing for forensics. Classification keeps reading `run_events` directly. If a beat appended an event, every idle holder would forge its own aliveness.
- **No fake Units seam, ever.** An in-memory map of live advance goroutines offered to the ladder as `UnitActive` is *supervisor memory*, and S02.5's kubelet rule ("re-list actual state, never trust supervisor memory") forbids exactly that. The DB lease row and the event cursor ARE the re-listable actuals — which is why the beat is a durable write and not a variable. `recovery.UnitLiveness`/`HarvestSource` stay the B0 no-ops (rejected alternative, recorded).
- **The in-process WEDGED analog never dies.** With no unit to be "active", S02.5's WEDGED translates to *live lease (a beating holder) + stale cursor*: flagged `run.wedged` once per stall episode through the existing `flagWedged` discipline, counted in `Report.Wedged`, **never** auto-killed (D1.3, S10.8). Between the two lives the wake grace: a lease that has expired but sits inside ⚙ `recovery.wake_grace` decides nothing at all and stays `Pending` — the platform cannot yet honestly say whether the holder is gone (P-T07-4). Containment stays the watchdog's silence rule (park + card, S14.4); `internal/watchdog` is untouched and the §31 importwall holds. The two liveness observers now read the SAME evidence, so they can no longer disagree fatally about the same run in the same minute.
- **Parked stays unscanned.** The pass still scans exactly {claimed, running, draining}, so an open-ask pause is structurally safe for hours or days — that is why arbitrary pauses at ask cards need no lease at all, and why the kill window was only ever the post-answer advance. Every parked→running resume must leave a live lease behind it, whether by the driving hold's immediate first beat or, for a resume that hands the run onward instead of driving it inline (an approved plan; a person's "resume — I was wrong"), by one explicit `Beat`.
- **Fixture note for future packets:** a run whose events were written moments ago is now ALIVE for one `dead_after` even with no lease. Recovery fixtures asserting a reap must place the pass past the bound (a fake clock past `max(lease, lastEvent+dead_after)`), which is what four pre-existing ladder tests were adjusted to do at this packet — preconditions only, assertions untouched.

## 55. Recovery-fork integrity — supersession, run identity & the dispatch surface (P3-RW-6; S02.5, S02.3, S10.7, S13.7, S14.4)

The defect this settles, in one line: an intake-class crash-fork could never resume, because the fork's identity never crossed into the pipeline — every generation's dispatch died with "run is not running: run `<task>.intake` is crashed", the ladder re-forked, and a lineage holding 8 state events, 3 answered asks and 2 checkpoints burned to a tombstone as a "repeat offender".

- **A run id is composed exactly ONCE, at birth.** Every later consumer reads the run's CURRENT identity from state; nobody re-derives it from the task id. This extends §16's last bullet (which stated it for the verify judge) into the general house rule, because the same mistake was made independently at six intake sites. The two sanctioned mechanisms: where the pipeline owns the seam's input struct it PASSES the id through (`intake.DraftInput.RunID`, `ReviseInput.RunID`, `RouteQuery.RunID`); where the seam signature deliberately admits only artifacts (the S06.8 Critic, the S12.4 utility/spot-check duties) the stage implementation READS the current identity from pipeline state (`Skeleton.currentIntakeRun`, the `engineRevise` LoadState precedent), bound for the local seams inside `stage.New` where the pipeline is born. The ONE site that legitimately composes is `localClassifier.Classify`: it runs inside `Pipeline.Start`, where the composed id IS the birth identity, and it says so in a comment.
- **The rebind is the supersession, and it is guarded by LINEAGE, never by an id's shape.** `Pipeline.AdvanceDispatched(ctx, taskID, runID)` is the dispatch leg's entry: it walks the dispatched run's `runs.parent_run_id` chain (migration 0002) to the state's current run, requires the same task, and only then moves `st.RunID` — as ONE `intake.state` event on the FORK at the FORK's generation, in one WriteTx with the open ask row's re-point and (when a gate is open) the fork's park on it. Multi-hop is the normal case, not an edge: a fork that crashed before its own rebind committed leaves the state naming an ancestor. A same-id dispatch performs no write at all, so the ordinary path is byte-equivalent. A failed guard refuses with `intake.ErrLineage` onto the dispatch crash path — a rebind MOVES an identity, and the platform grants that only along a real chain.
- **The rebind runs before every early return.** Terminal-phase and open-gate returns included: a fork dispatched over an already-approved state must complete ITSELF (`finishIntake` then completes and settles the fork, never the parent), and a fork dispatched over an open gate parks on it rather than standing running-idle for the next sweep to reap. Downstream needed no changes — the lease `Hold`, `SessionVerbs`, ask ids, approval, claims and `finishIntake` all already read `st.RunID`.
- **ONE fork-aware suffix matcher, exported.** `metering.StripForkSuffix` is the platform's single reading of `<parent>.g<newGen>` (S02.5 step 3). Four implementations had existed and they disagreed: the shell's raw `HasSuffix` refused `<task>.execute.g1`, so a recovery fork of a project-backed execution silently lost its worktree and snapshot lane. `stage.runRole`, the shell's workspace gate, `metering.derivePurpose` and `internal/watchdog`'s reader all delegate to it now (metering is inside the §31 forward allowlist, so the watchdog wall is untouched). A fifth private copy is a defect; the property test sweeps the shapes (every base × role × chain, plus `.g`, `.gx`, `.g1x`, `.g1.foo`, `.gadget`, a task literally named `t-g1`).
- **A dispatch that cannot proceed leaves a CORPSE.** An unroutable run id used to return its error before any transition, leaving the run `claimed` and holding its cap-1 (user, lane) slot until a sweep noticed it up to ⚙ `recovery.dead_after` later. It now takes the ratified `claimed→crashed` edge with the cause in the detail. This is not a kill: the run was just claimed by us and is provably undispatchable (NO-AUTO-KILL, S14.4 / G1 D1.3, stated in a comment at the site).
- **No production run class is fork-bait by its id shape.** `stage.Routable` (the same question `Dispatch` asks) is exported and the shell composes `NoFork = IsDirectArmRun(id) || !Routable(id)`, so a crashed ROLELESS run finalizes-with-card instead of forking into a successor no dispatcher can route. This covers `platform.deadman.*` canaries (roleless by construction, S14.4), any future platform probe id, and dirty pre-RW-4 worlds' seeded rows. The watchdog's probe semantics are untouched and its importwall holds — fork policy stays where fork policy lives, as a shell-composed predicate, and `internal/recovery` still names no run class of its own (its finalize detail now states both grounds honestly).
- **Queue settlement is level-triggered and scheduler-owned.** `IsTerminal(crashed)` is deliberately false, so the dispatch-path settle skips a crashed run — and when the ladder LATER tombstoned, finalized or harvested it, or forked it and left the parent behind, nobody settled the row (recovery never touches the queue; `SettleRun` refuses non-terminals). The claim pass now runs `settleEndedRows` beside `reconcileQueueRows`: any queued/claimed row whose run is in {completed, crashed, finalized, tombstoned, died-at-gate} settles to `done` in a bounded per-row WriteTx. Being level-triggered heals rows that PREDATE the fix (the live world's 16). `crashed` settles QUEUE-ONLY — its admission is over but its lineage is not, and each successor ends with its own receipt (D4); the four `IsTerminal` states materialize theirs through the existing idempotent `MaterializeTx`. `parked` is excluded on purpose: an open-gate park keeps its claimed row by documented design and its resume continues under it. Queue rows remain non-event-minting (the `SetLeaseTx` doctrine).
- **Declared not taken (OQ3's optional half):** the lease `Beat` at dead-man canary creation. It would add a keeper dependency and shell wiring to the one package whose import wall is the point, for a $0 momentary probe that the mid-probe-sweep test now proves is already safe under the §54 conjunction (fresh appends outrank an absent lease).

## 56. The detached crash posture — endings outlive their request, and dead-holder runs go to the ladder (P3-RW-10; S02.3, S02.5, S06.1, S07.7, S14.4, S01.3)

The defect this settles, in one line: a requester answered an interview card, the plan-draft sessions started inside the answer POST, their page navigated away — and because the crash posture rode the same request context that had just died, the state read failed, the corpse was never written, and the run sat `running`, driver-less and unscannable, until the watchdog silence-parked it into a state only another human could release.

- **THE RECORD OF THE ENDING OUTLIVES THE REQUEST.** This is the stage layer's law, and it is the chat-API doctrine (§37-C) generalized: any write that RECORDS how a beat ended rides `context.WithoutCancel` — values kept (identity, log attribution), cancellation dropped. Three writes are endings: `Skeleton.crash` (the corpse the ladder forks from), `verifyTerminal` (the paid drain's outcome), and the state READ that decides between them (`Surface.mapDriveErr`). The detach lives at each seam's own boundary, never at the call sites: `crash` detaches INSIDE, so every caller — the dispatch legs, both intake beats via `mapDriveErr`, both verify-answer sites — is covered in one move, and no future caller can forget. The cancel-suppression consult runs on the detached context too, so a leg unwound by a human cancel still stays corpse-free (drain D1).
- **The drive itself stays attached, and abort-mid-drive is a CRASH.** Weighed and decided: no background drive, no detached engine sessions, no early return from the answer POST. S02.5's fork-from-last-checkpoint IS the ratified recovery for a dead driver and RW-6's rebind makes the fork re-drive it; D7 bounds the re-spend and S02.5's harvest step covers a call that completed server-side after the abort. A drive that survived its caller would also need the "still composing" face the SPA does not have. So the posture, not the work, is what outlives the request — the caller dies, the drive dies with it, and what is left behind is classifiable.
- **The cut line is the run's STATE, and it now holds under cancellation in both directions.** Past the resume commit (`running`) → corpse + 500 `advance_crashed_recovering`, whatever the error looks like — a canceled context no more outranks the state than a wrapped sentinel does (RW-9 R4, unchanged). Before it (parked, terminal) → the existing 4xx, and a beat that died because its CALLER died answers 409/`conflict`: nothing about the platform is broken, the gate is standing, and re-reading is the whole remedy. A raw 500 for an aborted request was a lie about the platform (S01.3).
- **Verify parity: finished work lands, residue crashes.** A drain that finished its rounds has already been paid for, so its verdict lands whatever became of the requester's connection (D7, S07.7 — no finding dies silently). And a `verifyTerminal` that fails REGARDLESS now takes the crash posture at both call sites, closing the stage layer's last uncorpsed path: a run holding a paid outcome nobody landed is a strand exactly like a dead drive's.
- **The silence rule reads the lease, and stops hiding dead-holder runs.** A `running`/`draining` silence candidate whose LEASE deadline has passed (or that holds no lease at all) AND whose event cursor is older than ⚙ `recovery.dead_after` gets its flag card and is LEFT WHERE IT IS. Parking it contained nothing — there is no live work to hold back and no next paid call for the scheduler to refuse — while hiding it from the one component ratified to classify a driver-less run (S02.5 step 2), whose heal is machine-only and bounded; a park with no resume-time waits on a person forever. The watchdog mints no corpse and takes no new edge: park remains the only transition the suite makes (§31 intact), it is simply not made for this class. A LIVE lease is untouched — beating holder + stalled cursor is WEDGED, and S14.4 parks it. **That rule is the recovery pass's own DEAD arithmetic in steady state, to the second** (§54), and matching it exactly is the point: at the instant the watchdog abstains, the pass would already reap the run, so there is no window where it is neither contained nor collected. **No wake grace is applied, deliberately and against the first reading of §54**: the pass's grace is level-triggered, applied only on its first pass after a wake or a clock jump, so steady state — which is what a 30 s sweep meets — is zero. A grace-padded bound was implemented first and was PROVEN NEVER TO FIRE at v0 defaults (drain r1, F1): the default silence budget IS `dead_after`, so a freshly dead holder trips silence at ~300–330 s, strictly inside a 420 s abstain bound — still parked, still hidden, the ratified wedge intact. Abstaining INSIDE a wake-grace window is also the right answer: the pass collects the run when its own grace expires, whereas a park there would re-hide it. The cursor conjunct is what preserves containment — a run silent past a SHORT per-run-type ⚙ `watchdog.silence_budget` but still appending inside `dead_after` is not the pass's candidate yet, so it parks exactly as before.
- **Fixture note for future packets:** the intake nudge refuses an ask-less parked run (`pipe.Advance` demands `running`) but is a benign no-op on a gate-parked one (gates wait, S06.1) — a test that wants the refusal must build the ask-less park, which is the live wedge's own shape.
- **Fixture note, watchdog half:** a silence fixture must be REACHABLE at the 30 s sweep cadence and the effective budget (default: the `dead_after` seed). A test that only trips at multiples of the bound proves nothing about the arm it claims to cover — that is precisely how the F1 defect above stayed green through a full battery.

## 57. Deep-Plan interview depth — per-family question sets, the phrase-and-summarize seat & the understanding block (P3-RW-12; S06.4–S06.6, S06.10, S09.4/S09.8/S09.10, S12.4, S15.2)

The defect this settles, in one line: the operator asked for a webshop and the platform asked eight generic questions — nothing about what to build it with, where the pictures come from, or what it should look like — so the interview knew the shape of a task and not the task.

- **Six seeded question sets, not two (extends §14's seed bullet).** `SeedTaxonomies()` now returns one set per value in `Families()`: software at v2 (the ten ClarifyCodeBench slots verbatim plus `technology_stack`/`assets_media`/`look_feel`), research, content, data, chore at v1, generic unchanged at v1. S06.2's "v0 ships software plus a generic fallback" is a FLOOR the 2026-08-12 operator directive raises — operator-directed, additive (S15.2), no S00.9 amendment. The DISCLOSED-fallback machinery (`applyFamilyTaxonomy`/`recordTaxonomyFallback`) is retained and now fires only for an operator override map or a family seeded later; the test that guarded it moved onto a custom `Pipeline.Taxonomies` map, which is the case it actually exists for.
- **Two drafting rules bind every set.** (1) Every requester-facing string is written for someone who is not a programmer — the person answering is describing what they want, not specifying a system. (2) Every question asking for a technical or aesthetic DECISION leads with `plannerChoosesValue` ("You choose for me and show me what you picked"), so nobody must have an opinion to get a result; the choice comes back on the S06.9 approval card's restatement and steps, where Re-plan contests it — no new machinery, because an answered slot is an answered slot.
- **Evidence is named where it exists and disclaimed where it does not.** ClarifyCodeBench (arXiv:2607.00711) covers the software family only, so its ten weights stay measured and the three added software slots sit strictly BELOW the benchmark-failed 12 — reasoning does not outrank measurement. The four new families' weights are REASONED, and each set's `Source` states the ordering rationale in full rather than borrowing an authority it does not have. Every taxonomy's `Source` carries drafting model + date + packet id (S06.5 "drafted at implementation time with the strongest available frontier model").
- **Depth scales through the ⚙ floors alone, and the weight distribution is therefore a REQUIREMENT.** `TestSeedWeightsMeetTierFloorShape` pins it: for every seeded set, highest-weight-first questioning crosses 60 within 2 cards and 75 within 3 at the ratified defaults. No per-tier question caps (G1 P8 rejected them), no new ⚙. A future set that is flat enough to need four cards to clear the low floor fails this test, which is the point.
- **`intake.Phraser` is a SEPARATE optional seam (extends §14's seam list), and the containment is structural.** The taxonomy decides what must be asked; the pipeline decides which slots fit this card; only then is the finished selection offered to the seat, and only the WORDING comes back. `buildInterviewCard` folds the result BY SLOT ID in platform code — an id that was not asked is dropped, an id the seat skipped keeps the taxonomy's words, and count/order/ids/`Options` are untouchable by construction. Never a prompt-level lockout (R03 §2.1: a prompt is something a model can be argued out of, a fold is not); the engine-enforced one-property-per-asked-id schema is a belt, not the authority. `Question.Text` stays canonical and `Question.Phrased` is additive, so the ask-row snapshot records both.
- **`Card.Understood` / `ApprovalLayer1.Understood` are DETERMINISTIC.** Items are composed from `State.Resolutions` at card build — no new state field, because the resolutions already ride every state event and the rendered block already rides the ask snapshot. Interview and clarification cards carry it; escalation and family cards do not (a single mid-planning question and a pre-round nothing-is-known question have nothing to summarize). The approval card carries the FULL recap beside `Restatement` — complement, never replacement — and adds **no card and no click**: approval is the confirmation (S06.1), and a pre-draft recap gate would be one more click (S06.4). The recap is resolutions **plus answered 1.7 escalations** (`understoodRecap`): an escalation changed what gets built exactly as much as an interview answer did, so omitting it would under-report what the approval is approving. Escalation items carry `UnderstoodEscalation` as their origin label rather than a fourth `SlotResolution` kind — they settle a consequential ambiguity, not a must-know slot, so Clearance must keep ignoring them.
- **Honest absence, still.** Nil or erroring seat → verbatim taxonomy questions, items-only block, zero added asks, no invented prose. `Understood.Text` is empty unless a seat actually answered: the deterministic items are never dressed up as model output (§26).
- **The local seat holds the whole S06.10 utility row.** `stage.UtilitySeat` = `intake.Utility` + `intake.Phraser` on one object, one `utility` alias, bound once at the composition root. ONE duty call per card carries wordings and summary together (one $0 D7 row, one degrade point, one shared context). `local.PhraseSchema` owns the SHAPE (reason-first, then summary, then one property per asked id, `additionalProperties:false`), stage supplies the ids — the §26 wall, both directions. **`phraseMaxTokens = 4000`, and the number is MEASURED, not reasoned: a drafting duty keeps its think phase (`NoThink = Classification`), the think phase is emitted before the constrained region, and at the first cut's 1000 it consumed the entire budget — content length 0 on every card, every time. At 4000 the output is schema-exact with good phrasings.** A length cap for a thinking seat budgets the thinking, not just the JSON. Structural constant beside `helpMaxTokens`, under the standing settings-tab flag; **no new ⚙**.
- **A live seam is a seam that runs in CI-by-default, not one behind an env var.** The first cut gated its live leg behind `SINET_LIVE_SMOKE`, so it never ran and the seat above was dead on the ratified stack while every fake-backed test stayed green. `TestLivePhraseAndSummarize` follows the RW-11 T11 pattern instead: it self-starts llama-swap on an ephemeral port from a config generated from today's manifest, AUTO-RUNS wherever the stack is installed, and sanctioned-skips where it is not. Its load-bearing assertion is the tripwire the drain needed — a NON-EMPTY `Phrased` for every asked id — because the honest degrade (verbatim questions, zero clicks) makes total seat failure invisible to every other test. **Measured cost, operator-facing: ~53 s cold and ~50 s warm per card on the ratified stack, synchronous inside the interview card build.** Warm ≈ cold means the cost is generation, not model load; a three-card interview adds ~2.5 minutes of wall time before the requester sees anything. Nothing in this packet spends that budget differently — it is recorded here because the number belongs to whoever decides whether the seat stays on by default. `PhraseInput.RunID` is explicit on the seam (the `DraftInput.RunID` precedent) because the duty runs before any pair exists and the pipeline already knows which run it is driving — after a recovery-fork rebind, the fork.
- **Governance content is a SNAPSHOT of what was ratified, never a live pointer (new rule, extends §17).** `b2Seeds()` used to marshal today's `SeedTaxonomies()`, which made the B2 entries pointers rather than records: a fresh world's first boot would have written v2 content under the B2 gate's provenance while an existing world's governed v1 file quietly diverged from the runtime seed. Closed on every side. (1) `b2SoftwareTaxonomyV1()` and `b2GenericTaxonomyV1()` freeze what B2 actually approved — generic too, though P3-RW-12 did not change it, because the trap is the live POINTER and the moment two things agree is the only cheap moment to pin them. (2) `EnsureRW12TaxonomyGovernance` brings governed content current by SUPERSESSION under its own provenance (S09.8: new version, old retired, chained by `supersedes_id`); it creates the four new families, re-checks software and generic by content, never resurrects a removed entry, and defers with a log until an operator account exists (D10). (3) **The rule binds this packet too**: `rw12ContentDigest` pins the sha256 of the exact content the RW-12 originRef attests to, checked at runtime before anything is written (divergence ⇒ `ErrSeedDiverged`, a loud skip and never a boot failure) and at build time by `TestRW12DigestsMatchTheShippedSeeds`. Digests, not a second copy of ~550 lines that would then be two things needing to agree. **For the next packet that edits a question set: do not update the digests, and do not extend this Ensure — mint your own, with your own provenance, exactly as this packet did to B2's.** `TestB2GovernedTaxonomiesAreTheRatifiedSnapshot` pins both frozen fixtures. Boot order is fixed: B2 seeding first (it puts the entries there), then this.
- **A governed object's content is what its ROW was committed with — never what is on disk.** `writeEntry` places the knowledge file BEFORE its transaction, deliberately (a crash leaves an orphan file, never a row without content). The cost is a window where new bytes sit on disk under a still-active old row, and a boot that compared FILES would find them already equal to the in-code seed, skip the supersession, and keep skipping it at every future boot — the active row attesting content it does not have, permanently and silently. So the equality check reads the content hash from the `knowledge.write` event, which commits inside the row's own transaction and therefore cannot be torn. Divergence is counted (`TaxonomyGovernanceResult.Repaired`), logged loudly at boot in NEUTRAL words — "crash-torn write or out-of-band edit; repaired from the row", because an operator editing the file by hand produces the same state as a crash and the log should not accuse the wrong cause — and repaired: by completing the supersession, or, when the row is already right and only the disk is wrong, by rewriting the file to what the row attests, which mints no version because nothing about the record changed. `TestGovernanceDecidesFromTheRowNotTheFile` simulates the torn state and fails against the file-based check.
- **An unreadable record is UNVERIFIABLE, not permission to trust the file.** The provenance event is not guaranteed to be there forever: knowledge events are `keep:false` (`retention/keepforever.go`), so past ⚙ `retention.compaction_horizon` the S14.9 pass may strip payload bodies, and a compacted body carries no `entry_id` either. Reading a SQL NULL into a string would have failed EVERY boot of an otherwise healthy old world, and a missing row would have quietly returned the check to the file — the exact posture the bullet above removes. So: NULL, elided, or no row ⇒ the entry is skipped, counted (`Unverifiable`), and named at boot ("provenance hash unavailable — compacted or pruned; supersession not attempted; divergence check limited this boot"). Never a file fallback, never a boot failure. **Measured while pinning this**: a `knowledge.write` payload is ~240 bytes against retention's 1024-byte `BulkPayloadFloorBytes`, so the compaction pass does not select these rows today — and `run_events.ts` is an identity column, so no test can backdate a row past the trigger's one-month floor to prove otherwise. The posture is implemented regardless: that floor is an interim structural constant, and the no-record branch is reachable without compaction at all (a restored database, an imported world). `TestGovernanceSkipsWhenProvenanceIsUnverifiable` covers both reachable shapes and fails against the old code with exactly the two symptoms — a NULL scan error and a file-trusting supersession.
- **Non-goals, restated so they stay non-goals.** The band gains ZERO asks — `familyGate`'s band guard and the interview's band skip are byte-identical, pinned by the existing `TestBandNeverAsksFamily*` staying green by name. Option LABELS are not phrased at v0 (authored plain-language content, canonical values; free text is always available regardless). No `web/` edits — rendering `Phrased`/`Understood` is the SPA builder's FRONTEND.md pass. No migration, no new dependency, no new ⚙, and `Start`/`familyGate`/`applyFamilyTaxonomy`/`advanceLoaded` untouched.

## 58. No terminal without a door — ladder-terminal cards, the verification-infrastructure card & the per-project check pack (P3-RW-14 Cut A; S02.3, S02.5, S07.2, S07.3, S07.7, S13.7, S15.5/S15.6)

The defect this settles, in one line: a software task reached verify, the drain refused because no check pack existed, the refusal took the crash path, the S02.5 ladder forked that deterministic refusal three times and tombstoned the lineage — and the task then sat at kanban "verifying" forever with ZERO open asks, because the "card" every terminal claims to write was a STRING inside an event payload.

- **The rule, and it is a rule: a lineage ENDING writes its open ask in the SAME transaction as the transition.** All three ladder terminals owe it — repeat-offender tombstone (S02.5 step 7 "tombstone-review cards"), stale-interruption finalize and the shell-composed NoFork finalize (S02.3 "finalized (finalize-with-card)"). The branch that does NOT end a lineage — the ordinary fork — owes nothing, and writing a card there would be an inbox item for something nobody has to decide. `TestRW14EveryLadderTerminalLeavesADoor` is the property over all four branches; the payload string is REPLACED by the row, never duplicated alongside it (the payload now carries `ask_id`, a reference to the durable record).
- **The task leaves its stage column in that same transaction.** `kanban_status → "attention"` when the ended lineage was the last non-terminal run of the task (S15.5 blocked-on-a-human; the landed `verifyTerminal` vocabulary). One SQL statement carries both conditions, so the read and the write cannot race. **A task already `done` or `cancelled` is never touched**: it did not become "blocked on a human" because a leftover run ended, and rewriting the column would falsify how it finished. The landed `deriveKanban` view overlay (a tombstoned run reads "attention") is left exactly as it was — it has its own landed test, and the STORED column is what this rule governs.
- **The card lives with its minter; the choreography lives with the FSM.** `internal/recovery` shapes `LadderCard` and gains NO new import (its JSON field names mirror the S07.7 card — kind/task_id/run_id/issued_ts/sla/summary/detail/choices/ask_id — so ONE inbox renderer reads both kinds); `internal/stage` owns retry/cancel exactly as `answer.go` owns the S07.7 verbs. The ask id is DERIVED (`ask-ladder-<run id>`), not random: a lineage terminates once, so a second card for the same terminal is a primary-key violation rather than a silent duplicate in an operator's inbox. **The card carries no S07.7 route-table category** — a ladder terminal is not a verification finding, and minting one would invent ratified vocabulary this packet was not given; it carries the ratified SINK type and the S02 name of the terminal that raised it.
- **Both card kinds answer `{retry, cancel}` and nothing else (coordinator-ratified OQ2).** `retry` = an explicit human grant of a FRESH bounded budget (the §16 / S06.7(a) precedent): on a ladder card a generation-bumped successor of the ended lineage with `recovery_attempts` RESET, admitted through the one ingress (S16.6); on the infrastructure card a re-entry of the drain on the same run (parked→running, generation bumped). `cancel` = the ratified S02.3 mapping (§14 reading 9). Every other verb is `verify.ErrUnsupportedAnswer`. **There is deliberately no `accept_best_effort` on the infrastructure card**: V1 never ran, and `SetVerified` stays the only path to verified (S05.1/S07.11). The ladder card reuses verify's sentinels on purpose — one answer surface, one refusal vocabulary, one transport mapping.
- **A ladder terminal on a run with NO task still gets its door** (the dead-man canary, the BENCH-REG §2 direct arm): the ask row is written, the kanban step is skipped because there is no board column, and the ledger decision is skipped because there is no ledger — logged, never fatal to the answer. An ending is recorded and answerable even when nothing owns it.
- **Only the DETERMINISTIC preamble refusal converts to a card; a mechanical mid-drain failure still crashes for the ladder.** The class is marked at its source (`verify.PreambleRefusal`, wrapping the refusal so `errors.Is` still sees the sentinel) rather than classified from an error's text (§38's ban): `validateInput`'s three infrastructure absences, plus the two stage-side refusals that happen before a Verifier exists — the P-T06-5 unsupervised-judging gate and the check-pack seam. A judge transport dying, a DB error, a malformed deliverable: all still corpses, because a fork of those may well succeed (§21). Both directions are tested at both layers.
- **Exactly ONE place a verification outcome reaches the run FSM, per leg.** `drainOrCard` RETURNS the escalate-with-card outcome instead of landing it itself, so the dispatch leg still has a single `verifyTerminal` call site under the landed crash-posture rule (`TestVerifyTerminalErrorsTakeTheCrashPostureAtEverySite`, which counts sites in source). A future site owes the same posture — or, better, the same shape: produce the outcome, let the one site land it.
- **The check pack is per (domain, project), built from the S13.7 registry capture.** `stage.Config.CheckPacks map[domain]` — empty since B2-4, which is why the whole software family crashed — becomes `CheckPackFor(ctx, domain, taskID)`, wired at the composition root over `internal/project` (stage never imports project, §23). Captured `lint`/`build` are the S07.3 static rung, `test` the unit rung; `run`/`preview` are NOT checks (they start something and wait — that is S13.8's preview, not a verdict). The pack's rule-7 verified-on stamp is the CAPTURE's own date — a suite is exactly as fresh as the scan it came from — which gives ⚙ `verification.check_audit_interval_days` its first real consumer. **No commands captured, or no project at all ⇒ a refusal that NAMES what to capture, and that sentence becomes the card's summary** (ratified OQ3(i)): the platform invents no pack content and never silently degrades a launch domain. Non-launch domains keep the ratified V1-empty degraded mode (S07.8) and see no card.
- **Carried hazard, stated because Cut A creates it and Cut B closes it.** With packs now wired, V1 actually runs for project-backed software tasks — against `RunRoot/<executeRunID>/cwd`, which for a project-backed task is the empty scratch dir, not the revision (the real work is in the worktree). That is exactly RW-14 R6, scoped to Cut B: until it lands, a project WITH commands will fail its own checks in an empty tree and drain into rework rounds. The command-less shape this cut was cut for (the live `shop`) never reaches V1 at all, so the wedge is closed either way — but B is not optional.
- **Non-goals held.** No new ⚙ (the 118-key tally stays green — the R1 cards consume the existing `verification.card_remind_hours`/`card_push_hours` at issue, approval class, ratified OQ5), no migration (asks/tasks/runs rows all existed), nothing under `web/`, the watchdog untouched (§31/§56), `internal/local` untouched, and the quality gate is still never the effects gate (S07.1: no card here releases anything outward).

### §58 drain round 1 — the card's own answers had to agree with the board and with the cancel mapping (P3-RW-14A D1–D3)

- **A derived overlay must yield to a decision already made (D1).** `deriveKanban`'s tombstone→"attention" overlay was successor-blind and task-state-blind, and R1's new verbs broke it: a task CANCELLED at the card served "attention" forever against a stored `cancelled`, and a RETRIED lineage served "attention" while its successor worked and after it finished. The overlay now speaks only while the door is genuinely open — the task itself has not ended (`done`/`cancelled` are decisions a dead run may not re-open) and the tombstone has no successor still being driven (a `crashed` successor counts as driven: it is terminal-but-SUPERSEDABLE, S02.3, and the ladder owns its disposition). The general rule: **a derived view may correct a stale column, never contradict an answered card.** The landed signature is kept so the landed `TestDeriveKanban` still binds it.
- **One cancel mapping, one implementation, and the ladder card rides it (D2a).** `ladderCancel` wrote `cancelled` on the task row in isolation, which left live sibling runs BILLING under a cancelled column and let a sibling's later verdict flip the task to `done`. It now goes through the cancel machinery, which ends every non-terminal run under the ratified S02.3 mapping and closes the asks parked on them. The call is made from `cancel.go` (`CancelTaskAtCard`) rather than from the answer path, because the NO-AUTO-KILL wall is FILE-SCOPED (`TestCancelIsReachableFromTheHTTPVerbsOnly`): the card answer is a fourth link in the same HUMAN chain — authenticated actor, reachable only through the HTTP answer verb — and putting the entry point inside the sanctioned file keeps the wall byte-meaningful instead of widening its allowlist.
- **A card outlives its lineage, so it must refuse what the task no longer wants (D2b).** A second ladder card left open when the first was cancelled at could RESURRECT the task: a fresh run enqueued and billed, the board dragged back out of `cancelled`. `retry` now refuses with `ErrNotResumable` when the task's stored column is `done`/`cancelled`, consumes nothing, and leaves the door there to cancel.
- **A refusal class is defined by WHAT it is, not by where it was caught (D3).** The invalid-pack error surfacing from inside `RunV1` is now marked `PreambleRefusal` too. Today the composition root validates before handing a pack over, so this is latent — but a future pack source that skips resolve-time validation would otherwise hand the ladder a deterministic refusal to fork into a tombstone, the exact wedge this packet closed.

### §58 drain round 2 — a wall that cannot see a caller is not a wall, and a recovered lineage is not an open door (P3-RW-14A R-1, R-2)

- **A new entry point into a walled machinery must be ENUMERATED in the wall (R-1).** `CancelTaskAtCard` was added inside the sanctioned file, which satisfied the NO-AUTO-KILL wall's file scope — while being invisible to its `targets` set, so a machine caller of it from ANY file would have passed green, and the method's own doc credited the wall with coverage it did not have. The wall now names it (`targets`) and names the answer path as its sanctioned caller (`sanctioned`), with the coordinator's by-name sanction for editing that landed test; the edit is strictly STRICTER (one target added, one caller file added, its own comment kept truthful about the count) and was probe-proven both ways — a call added from an unsanctioned file is now flagged by name. **The rule this leaves behind: widening a walled surface means widening its wall in the same commit, and the doc comment may only claim what the wall actually enumerates.**
- **`completed` is the one thing a tombstone can stop being (R-2).** The D1 overlay treated a COMPLETED successor as "ended for good, decides nothing", so a retried lineage that RECOVERED still shouted "attention" over the stored column for the whole next phase. A successor exists only because a human answered the card, so completion means the answer worked: it suppresses. Only `finalized` / `tombstoned` / `died-at-gate` leave the parent's tombstone speaking — and a tombstoned successor speaks through its own card, which is the overlay's one remaining job (kept live by the same test).

## 59. Billed work lands, or dies at $0 — the stripped verification workspace, the wrote-nothing gate, write-aware routing & plain assumption prose (P3-RW-14 Cut B; S07.2, S07.3, S08.8, S13.1, S02.8, S06.5)

The defect this settles, in one line: an execute leg ran 7 engine sessions against the right worktree, reported every one "completed", billed $1.11 — and wrote nothing at all, because a read-only specialist had been handed a plan whose every step declared a write_set, and no layer that could have noticed was reachable.

- **A completed session is not evidence that work happened.** `stage.finished` derives from session completion (end_turn) by design, and that is honest — but it implies nothing about the tree. The honesty layers are V1 step contracts and V0's diff-empty family, and BOTH were unreachable: V1 crashed for want of a pack (Cut A), and V0's ratified diff-empty gate compares revision N to N−1 **by bytes**, so revision 1 of a repo-backed task — the exact live shape — was invisible to it. The rule this leaves: when a layer reports what a MODEL did, some other layer must report what the WORLD did.
- **The wrote-nothing gate runs on platform facts only.** A repo-backed revision whose snapshot commit equals the attempt's base ref, while the plan holds an active W claim or any non-empty step write_set, is a V0 malformed verdict — hard kill at $0, one regeneration, never a judge call (S07.2; S13.1 revision 1 is presented against the pre-task state; S02.8 the claim is the durable knowledge that the task writes). All three terms are durable platform knowledge — the snapshot ledger, the recorded base, the approved plan — and **nothing the engine said about its own work is admissible**, which is the entire reason the gate can be trusted about a session that claimed success. Each term is guarded separately: no snapshot pin means not repo-backed, no base means the basis is unknown and the gate NEVER guesses one, no write claim means a read-only plan may legitimately move nothing.
- **Reading a fact must not create it.** `project.SnapshotAndBase` is read-only and deliberately not `Snapshot()`, which stages and commits: asking the question at verification time would have the platform manufacturing the evidence it is about to judge. It is safe to read because the execute leg already took its stage-close snapshot commit before verify was ever launched — so HEAD is the tree the work landed on. Pinned by test: repeat reads are stable, create no commits, and an uncommitted file does not move the answer.
- **The verification workspace is the revision, stripped.** V1 stops running in `RunRoot/<executeRunID>/cwd` — for a project-backed task the EMPTY scratch dir, while the real work sat in the worktree. It now receives a locked utility checkout at the revision's snapshot pin, copied WITHOUT `.git` (S07.3 rule 1, P-T06-2: with history present a pass measures lookup ability, not work — the §25 substrate). A worktree's `.git` is a FILE pointer, not a directory, and the test binds that against a checkout git actually made. The executable bit survives (or a captured `./script` check fails for a reason unrelated to the work) and symlinks are dropped (a link out of the tree is the escape the strip exists to prevent).
- **An honest absence is not a failure, and a wired seam must still be able to say "nothing here".** The materializer answers `""` for a task with no project or no snapshot pin, and verify falls back to the caller-prepared cwd rather than starving the checks — so the non-project arm is byte-unchanged. `verify.Verifier.Workspace` previously ignored `VerifyInput.Workspace` entirely once wired; a seam that can only answer "here it is" forces every caller into a lie.
- **A writing plan is a REQUIREMENT, and equipment that cannot write cannot take it.** `routeQueryFor` derives the write posture; the S08.8 step-1 filter refuses a candidate whose granted class is not workspace-writable OR whose granted tools hold no write instrument. **Both halves, because they fail independently**: the live culprit had neither, but write tools under a read-only class is equally useless — the compile takes `TighterClass(step, worker)`, so a C1 worker on a C2 write step runs `ro` and writes nothing. `sandbox.Class.WorkspaceWritable` derives from the class Profile rather than re-hardcoding the table, and is NOT a rank threshold: the ladder orders by tightness, and C0 (rank 0) has no filesystem at all while C1 (rank 1) has a read-only one. The refusal is NAMED on the no-fit card — "nobody could" and "nobody matched" are different facts, and only the first is actionable.
- **A ~0 bm25 rank is the opposite of a match.** The flat +0.5 for any FTS hit becomes a bounded magnitude-scaled fold. Measured on the shipped driver: a term appearing in EVERY indexed description ranks ~-0.000001 **regardless of corpus size** — its idf is ~0, which says it distinguishes nobody — while a genuinely discriminating term ranks -1.2 at 5 templates and -3.4 at 30. The floor sits three orders of magnitude above the noise and two below the weakest real signal; below it the contribution is exactly 0, so a candidate with no other signal keeps score 0 and takes the existing skip. The contribution stays under the family selector's +2 by construction: **what a worker DECLARES it is for outranks what its prose happens to echo**, and `plain_reason` still prints the rank it was earned on.
- **Requester-facing prose is for the person.** `"(force_proceed) Comparison Rules — assumed: proceeding without an answer"` baked an internal token into a sentence an operator reads on the approval card. The structural origin already rides the artifact's `Assumption.Origin`; the two arms now say why nobody was asked, and they say different things because they ARE different reasons (a force-proceed is the requester's instruction; the band is the platform's own rule that a trivial task is not worth an interview).
- **R10 was NOT implemented** (spec-tension OQ4): no ratified intake check catches a non-empty write_set under a read-only class, S06.7's spine list is closed at (a)–(d), and widening confinement at compile is forbidden (S06.6, P-T05-1). R8 closes the routing half and R7 the outcome half without touching ratified text; the S00.9 amendment is the operator's.
- **A paid test needs its own explicit opt-in, and must reap what it spawns.** Gating a billed leg on ambient environment let ordinary battery runs start engine sessions — 204 stray worlds and five orphaned sessions before an operator caught it. The pre-registered-paid-leg discipline applies to TESTS: one dedicated flag, nothing inherited, plus cancel-and-reap on every exit path (by process GROUP — the engine spawns its own children, so killing the parent alone re-orphans them one level down). **A test that can bill must be unable to start by accident, and unable to leave anything billing behind.**
- **Non-goals held.** No new ⚙ (118-key tally green; the R9 fold and the R8 write-instrument set are structural constants, settings-tab-flagged), no migration (0001–0024 byte-untouched), nothing under `web/`, `internal/local` untouched, and the quality gate is still never the effects gate.

## 60. The completion doctrine — delimiters may be completed, content never; and the adapter stays verbatim (P3-RW-16; S03.1, S06.6/S06.10, S02.5, S01.11)

The defect this settles, in one line: `planner session: stage: session output is not the contracted JSON object: unexpected end of JSON input` crashed ~30% of plan advances on the drain-r1 walk — and the missing byte was never ours to lose. The engine's OWN transcripts (copy-asides and the live `~/.claude/projects` originals, byte-identical) end 6 of 11 plan/critique sessions exactly one closing brace short at `stop_reason:"end_turn"`, ~7 KB against a 10 MiB cap, envelope parsed, `result` field non-empty. The platform was crashing on damage done upstream of it.

- **Where a repair may live is decided by who can tell the truth about the bytes.** The adapter's job is testimony: the envelope `result` field wins, streamed text substitutes only when it is empty, and what the engine said is handed on VERBATIM (S03.1, RW-9 R1–R3). An adapter that completed a truncated reply would be editing the record it exists to keep — so the completion lives at the stage's JSON-contract choke point (`parseJSONOutput`), where the platform is already the one judging, and where one seam covers every JSON-contract duty at once (plan draft/revise, critique, both judge axes, composer, dry-run). Trust stays in the platform validation, never in the seam (S06.6).
- **The completion appends closing delimiters and NOTHING else.** Eligible iff, after the fence/prose trim, the text is a valid JSON prefix whose cut lies OUTSIDE any string, immediately after a complete value or a closed container, with every open container closable from the bracket stack alone — bounded at 8 closers (plain constant, the `sseBatchSize`/`cancelGrace` precedent; S03 ratifies no parse-repair key, so no ⚙). Ineligible input keeps today's error verbatim, and the completed document is re-validated before it is used at all.
- **Four walls, each for a different lie the completion could tell.** It never closes a QUOTE (a string's content is model-authored and its end is unknowable). It never fires after a dangling `,` or `:`, nor on an object key awaiting its colon (both would require inventing a value). It never finishes a NUMBER: `12345` cut to `1` completes to perfectly valid JSON carrying a different number — fabrication wearing a syntax check's clothes, and the only wall whose violation produces no error at all. And it never closes a container that was opened and holds nothing yet: that recovers zero content while spending the bounded re-ask the seam would otherwise get, trading a crisp parse error for a worse semantic one.
- **The property that governs it: a completion may never change a value that was present.** Pinned by sweeping every byte cut of a corpus document — nested containers, escaped quotes, bare braces and brackets inside a string value, multi-digit and exponent numbers, `true`/`null` — and asserting for every firing cut that what parses out is contained, leaf for leaf, in the original. This property, not the syntax check, is what the number wall exists to satisfy.
- **A completion is never silent, and never quotable by the model.** Each one logs a Warn through the Skeleton logger with run, stage, session kind and closer count — counts and platform-authored names only (S01.11); the kind comes from `sessionKind`, which reads the caller's own declaration or the platform-authored marker line, so no model-written brief content can name the record. No new run_events type: the S14.2 event contract (§29) is untouched.
- **The retry posture does not move.** `jsonRetryLimit` stays 1 — the bounce recovers a malformed envelope, it is not a refine loop — and the S02.5 ladder remains the SOLE owner of crashed-advance recovery. With the completion the proven class heals in-session at $0, which makes the ~5-minute ladder fork the rare fallback it was designed to be rather than the routine cure.
- **A ``` inside a JSON string value is content.** Fence-stripping applies only when the first fence PRECEDES the first `{` — i.e. only when it really is a block's opening fence. Stripping unconditionally cut valid replies apart at a fence a step's `done_when` happened to mention, producing the same crash signature through a different door. **Both ends of the block need the rule** (drain r1 D1): taking the LAST fence as the closer re-opened the same wound from the other side — a TRUNCATED fenced reply carrying an in-string fence was cut mid-string and could never complete, so R2 and R4 could not compose. The closer is the last fence that either starts its own line — JSON forbids a raw newline inside a string, so a line-anchored fence is PROVABLY outside the document — or has nothing but whitespace after it; a block with no such fence was never closed, and its true tail goes to the prefix analysis intact. The four working reply forms (bare / fenced / prose-then-fenced / prose-then-bare) stay pinned, and prose after the closing fence still parses.
- **An oversized stream line is a skipped line, not a wedge (S03.1 forward tolerance).** `bufio.Scanner` stopped the pump cold on `ErrTooLong`: the tail including the terminal envelope was never read, the child blocked on its unread stdout, and `cmd.Wait` never returned — a hang, from a line the contract says to log and skip. The pump now discards the oversized line through its newline, logs it with its byte length, and CONTINUES to EOF; `scanBufCap` stays a plain constant, because an unbounded reader only trades a wedge for unbounded memory. If the discarded line was the envelope itself, the session ends honestly on the existing "exited without a result envelope" crashed path.
- **What the completion CANNOT guarantee — the absorb residue, stated plainly (drain r1 D2).** Syntactic completeness is not semantic completeness: the truncation eats the document's TAIL, and in the pair schema the tail is `coverage`, `risks` and `est`. `Plan.Validate` requires at least one well-formed step, so a reply cut before its steps still dies loudly — but coverage is only checked for DANGLING references, and risks/est are not checked at all, so a completed pair can be structurally valid with an empty coverage map and a zeroed estimate. Those are not silently absorbed, but they are caught later and at a price: `coverageCheck` (spine (a), which runs after every revision) turns an empty map into uncovered ACs and the bounded `coverage_autofix` revise round — one more engine round instead of one re-ask — and the D7 human approval gate sees the pair itself, estimate included. The critic path has the analogous residue: `{"kind":"revise"}` completed from a truncated verdict passes the kind switch with zero findings and spends a revise round saying nothing, though a model can emit exactly that untruncated, so it is not a completion-specific hole. **The honest summary: the completion converts a crash into a cheaper, louder, later check — it does not promise the document means anything.** A semantic-minimum guard for completed pair/critic documents (est/coverage present, revise carries findings) is a DEFERRED-LEDGER candidate, deliberately not built here: new semantic guards belong to the ratified validators, not to a parse-repair packet.
- **Scope held.** Production changes in exactly two files (`internal/stage/engines.go`, `internal/adapters/claudecli/claudecli.go` — the pump reader alone); no new ⚙ (118-key tally green); no migration; `web/` and `internal/local` untouched; the adapter's retention suites pass UNMODIFIED. The upstream question — whether a CLI release above pin 2.1.218 or a model revision stops emitting the short brace — is the coordinator's live-research item and an S03.3 deliberate-bump decision; the completion stays as the belt regardless, because any lane can truncate.

## 61. The opencode substrate — a per-USER server behind a per-RUN contract (P3-LN-1; S03.1–S03.7, S02.3–S02.4, S11.1, S16.2–S16.4)

`internal/adapters/opencode` is the second D3 substrate, behind the EXISTING `adapters.Adapter`/`Session`/`Driver` seam (§10 package map): `opencode.go` (Adapter, session, outcome assembly, the answer decisions), `serve.go` (the per-user instance manager + health watch), `client.go` (the measured HTTP surface), `lower.go` (S03.5 lowering + the S02.4e fingerprint), `parse.go` (v1 SSE → the closed platform kind set). Substrate name `opencode` (already fixed in `adapters.go`); imports are `internal/adapters` + stdlib only, and **never** `internal/sandbox` (§12: sandbox → adapters is the only direction). **Substrate only at LN-1** — no provider entry, no credential, no lane: Z.AI/GLM commissions at LN-2 and Kimi K3 at LN-3, both as config DATA atop this substrate (S03.6: adding a lane is never a new substrate).

- **The shape mismatch this packet had to hold, stated plainly.** The D3 contract is per-RUN; `opencode serve` is a per-USER standing HTTP server (S03.2). Three consequences bind the code. (a) **Config is startup-bound**: 1.18.3 resolves agents, the permission map and the provider block when the server boots, and `prompt_async` accepts an agent only BY NAME — there is no inline per-request agent definition [SPIKE P2-S5 Probe 3]. So a change to any STARTUP-BOUND part of the invocation RESTARTS the user's instance. `Manager.Acquire` keys on a sha256 digest over the compiled config JSON **plus the per-user root, the run cwd, and the CredInject-transformed serve env** *(corrected 2026-08-23 at drain r1: D8 excluded the S02.4e invocation fingerprint — and with it the per-message model, which rides `prompt_async` and must never restart the serve; D3 folded the injected env in as a digest so a rotated credential reaches a fresh instance, never a stale one; no raw env or secret ever appears in the key)* — the cwd because 1.18.3's stable `POST /session` carries no per-session directory member, so the serve's own cwd is what a session reports as its `directory`, and reusing an instance across cwds would silently run a run inside a PREVIOUS run's workspace. The honest consequence: with per-run isolated workspaces, "one instance per user" holds per WORKSPACE in practice — the same per-user-server-vs-per-run-workspace tension S11.3's per-session workspaces resolve, and resolving it is LN-2/D6 scope. Any ask the restarted instance held dies with it, which is exactly the S03.4 restart-ask-loss the containment path already covers. (b) **Confinement is per-user, not per-run**: S11.1 places the jail around the whole server and calls opencode's own `permission` config an inner soft layer only, so a non-nil per-run `Confiner` is `ErrConfinementUnsupported` — the permanently correct semantics, not an interim guard, and composing the per-user jail is LN-2/D6 scope. (c) **The cancel ladder's group rung ends the user's whole instance**, because that is what the process group IS here; it fires only after the cooperative `POST /session/{id}/abort` failed, and per-(user,lane) concurrency is 1 at v0 (§11), so the instance being reaped serves this run and no other.
- **The endpoint hand-off is a seam, not a spawner.** `Instances{Acquire,Stop}` is what the Adapter consumes (`Instance{BaseURL,Password,Root}`); `Manager` is this packet's dev-posture implementation — the platform spawning per-user subprocesses itself, each `Setpgid` into its own group, reaped by GROUP on every exit path. The D6 `sinet-engine@<user>` unit replaces the provider, not the adapter, which is why that unit's `ExecStart` stays a DRAFT (§7) here on purpose.
- **Ports are ALLOCATED, never fixed.** `--port 0` means the engine's own default **4096** at this pin (measured), which would collide across users and with anything on the host. The Manager allocates an ephemeral loopback port, and the engine's own printed `http://127.0.0.1:<port>` line is the authoritative URL (it reports what was actually bound). Boot is bounded (`BootTimeout` → `ErrBootTimeout`), so a battery can never hang.
- **Basic auth: the USERNAME is part of the credential.** `OPENCODE_SERVER_PASSWORD` is minted per instance from `crypto/rand` and enforced as HTTP Basic on EVERY endpoint including `/api/health`. **Live-recorded delta from SPIKE P2-S1 at the pin on this host (2026-08-23): the username must be `opencode`** — `-u <anyuser>:<pw>` is refused 401, where the spike recorded 200. The measurement wins and `BasicAuthUser` encodes it; the tier-R suite asserts both directions. The password lives in process memory and the child env only — never logs, run_events, the DB, fixtures, park records, or test output (§10 credential hygiene, extended).
- **The tools channel is the permission map, and the default-deny is structural.** `permission` compiles to `{"*":"deny", "task":"deny", <allowlisted>:"allow", <gated>:"ask"}` on the agent, plus a blanket `{"task":"deny"}` at top level. Blanket deny STRIPS a tool from the model's toolset PRE-inference [SPIKE P2-S5 Probe 5] — **verified live 2026-08-23**: with that map the offered toolset was exactly `[bash read]`, with `task` absent, and the gated `bash` produced a real `permission.asked`. An input that tries to re-admit `task` — an allowlist naming it (any case), a wildcard allowlist, a gated-tools entry, or an agent fragment supplying `permission.task` other than `deny` — is REFUSED with `ErrNativeSpawnTool`, never silently overwritten (the §12 fail-closed precedent).
- **`always` is unsendable by construction.** The client's `reply` accepts only `once`/`reject`; v1 `always` rules are in-memory AND server-wide, so they leak approvals across a person's sessions and vanish on restart [SPIKE P2-S1 Probe 6-A]. The suite pins it as a PROPERTY over random answers, not one example. The engine's own `always`-class fan-out (one reply → N `permission.replied`) is still parsed tolerantly and resolved by `requestID`.
- **The reject decision has no field on the shared `adapters.Answer`, and inventing one was out of scope.** On the Claude lane an answer is always an allow, so rejection never needed a member. This substrate's `permission.reply` takes `{reply, message}` and has NO input-substitution channel, which makes `UpdatedInput` unusable for its Claude-lane meaning here and free to carry the decision: `ApproveAnswer` / `RejectAnswer` build a documented `sinet.decision` envelope. A RAW replacement input is refused (`ErrUpdatedInputUnsupported`) — dropping a human's edit silently would execute the parked call unreviewed, the exact S03.4 failure the park exists to prevent. **A first-class approve/reject member on `adapters.Answer` is the honest fix and is flagged to LN-2** (it touches the shared package, which §5 put outside this packet's file set).
- **Resume DIFFS, it never assumes.** Shutdown rejection is SILENT — no bus event announces a dead park [SPIKE P2-S1 Probe 5] — so `Resume` enumerates `GET /permission` and branches: ask still held ⇒ reply (a defer-style unpark at no further cost, and the parser is told the turn is already in flight because no fresh `busy` will be emitted for a turn that never stopped); ask gone but the session listed ⇒ the park died, the orphaned call is marked **cancelled in the platform's OWN record** (opencode leaves its transcript part cosmetically `running`, which is never trusted) and recovery is a re-prompt of the surviving session id — a normal PAID turn; session gone too ⇒ a named error, because recovery is then the S02.5 fork ladder's, not the adapter's.
- **A reconnect reconciles by STATE; nothing ever claims replay.** opencode ignores `Last-Event-ID` (fix declined upstream) and its SSE frames carry no `id:` field at all — there is literally nothing to resume from. A dropped stream is re-opened a bounded number of times (`streamReconnects = 1`) with no such header, and the turn's state is re-derived from `GET /permission` + `GET /session/status`. The platform `/events` resume stays reconstructed from `run_events` ALONE (§30 line, S14.5); the standing hermetic test in `internal/api` is untouched and this substrate adds its own assertion.
