- **Two orderings that only live traffic reveals, both now handled.** (1) A completed assistant message is re-emitted several times, so one paid call is grouped by MESSAGE ID and emits exactly one `Usage` — never one per frame. (2) A `text` part can arrive AFTER its own message's completion frame; a late part still updates the retained answer (only for the message that completed last, so an older frame can never overwrite a newer answer). Losing the engine's whole answer to a frame ordering is precisely the failure §60/R19 exists to end.
- **`session.idle` is honored only after `busy`.** A freshly created session reports idle BEFORE any prompt (recorded live), so an ungated idle would end the turn before it began.
- **Two contract shapes are structurally unreachable here, and neither is faked.** `OutcomeDiedAtGate` exists for the S03.4 ceiling-ordering race, and 1.18.3 exposes **no per-turn engine budget belt** — there is no engine ceiling to order against, the platform ledger is the only ceiling, and the ordering obligation is trivially satisfied. `Outcome.GateFallback` reports the Claude lane's single-tool-call defer trap, which has no analogue: `permission.asked` parks without that bound and a parallel turn parks every call at once. Both stay unset, with the reason in code.
- **No transcript, so the copy-aside is inert rather than disabled.** opencode's store is SQLite (`event`/`event_sequence`), not JSONL: `Cursor.TranscriptPath` stays empty and `Driver.CopyAsideDir` therefore does nothing on this substrate — no branch was added anywhere to make that happen.
- **⚙: NONE consumed, and that is a finding.** `adapter.claude.cleanup_period_days` is Claude-lane retention; `adapter.parallel_gate_fallback` selects behavior for a defer trap that does not exist here; `adapter.engine_ceiling_backstop_mult` has no engine belt to scale. Each rationale is a doc comment in `lower.go`, not a fake consumer. **No new ⚙ key** — the S18 tally stays 118/33. Structural constants, flagged to the gate under the `sseBatchSize`/`cancelGrace` precedent (§7/§9/§11): `cancelGrace` 5 s, `streamReconnects` 1, `requestTimeout` 30 s, `scanBufCap` 10 MiB, `defaultBootTimeout` 90 s, `defaultStopGrace` 5 s, `defaultHealthInterval` 15 s, `bootPollInterval` 50 ms, `passwordBytes` 32, `serveLogCap` 8 KiB. Making any of them operator-tunable is an S00.9 amendment adding S18 rows.
- **Conformance tiers, and what tier R actually costs.** Tier F is fixtures plus a fake serve speaking the recorded surface on an ephemeral loopback port. **Tier R runs for REAL and costs $0**: a real `opencode serve` drives a real turn whose model call terminates on a loopback fake OpenAI-compatible provider — a live `permission.asked` → `reply:"once"` → completion round trip, with the live toolset proving `task` was stripped. Tier L is defined and structurally unreachable (`SINET_LIVE_SMOKE=1` per §10 — no second env name minted — plus a lane that is not commissioned until LN-2); both gates print named skips. The per-user provider dependency install (~62 MB, network once, SPIKE G1-S3 F1) is CONDITIONAL — reproduced in a shell probe at this pin, absent from the hermetic battery — so the bind/auth/isolation probe stays off provider-touching paths and every provider-touching probe is bounded with a named skip.
- **Registry (§32) and the rail (§4).** The `adapter-opencode` seed row lands with its adapter, discharging registry.go's own "Its row lands with its adapter"; its Notes are honest that it proves the SUBSTRATE, not a lane, and the zai LANE stays omitted until LN-2. The row-set-pinning tests moved 12 → 13 rows and the engine_bump set 6 → 7. The `opencode-ai (engine)` lock entry materializes in the same commit as the package, pin `1.18.3` EXACT (never `latest`, never `@1`), MIT **path-scoped and read verbatim at the pinned ref** with the `packages/enterprise/` carve-out scanned and cleared, no `modules` and no `npm_packages` claim (an external CLI, not a Go module and not an SPA dependency), and `opencode.Pin` coupled by `TestPinMatchesLock`.
- **`POST /global/upgrade` is not reachable from the client at all** — not guarded, absent (S03.3 rule 2).
- **What `-race` found, and why it is worth recording.** `assembleOutcome` mutated the very `*adapters.Ask` that had already ridden the `gate_ask` event, while the Driver was concurrently marshalling it into the durable ask row. The Outcome now carries a COPY. An event-carried pointer belongs to its consumer the moment it is sent; a later "just filling in one field" is a data race wearing a bookkeeping disguise.

## 62. The Z.AI/GLM lane — a provider entry per person, and the second adapter that makes it dispatchable (P3-LN-2A; S03.6, S03.7, S10.5, S10.6, S11.5, S03.4)

LN-1 built the substrate; LN-2A commissions the first lane on it. S03.6's governing sentence held: **adding a lane was a provider entry per user plus billing flags, and no substrate changed.** What did change is the one thing S03.6 does not mention, because it is not about lanes at all — `internal/shell` now registers **two** adapters.

- **The lane is a DOCUMENT, and the document is the unit of honesty.** `internal/adapters/opencode/lanedata/zai.json` (embedded, the `internal/watchlist/pricedata` precedent) carries the endpoint, the model ids, the per-model attributes (`billing` / `overflow_mode` / `region_model_gate`), the credential REFERENCE, the Eco lever's shape and the provider's wire signal set — each with its own `verified_on` date. `LoadLaneConfig` validates on load, which is what makes onboarding a gate rather than a copy: a model declaring `overflow_mode: auto-metered` without a proven metered disable is REFUSED there (S03.6 3.10), because accepting it makes an unbounded bill reachable by default from a flat-rate plan. **No endpoint and no model id is a Go constant in a non-test file**, pinned by a source scan over the package — three of this seed's rows moved inside five weeks, and a constant goes stale invisibly where a dated row goes stale visibly. The seed is seed data, never the authority; the account's own observed list is (P-T17-3), and its canary is 2B's.
- **`ProvidersFor(userID)` is the per-user seam; `Providers` stays the default.** The credential and the model set are per-PERSON facts (D2), so one value serving everybody was never the shape. The existing single value is the single-user/default case, so nothing that predates the seam changed. The consequence §61(a) already recorded now has a lane attached to it: a person's provider entry is startup-bound, so **editing it restarts that person's serve and nobody else's** — asserted in both directions.
- **A lane is CONFIGURED by a document and COMMISSIONED by a credential, and the two are different states.** The adapter refuses by name (`ErrLaneNotCommissioned`) when a model names a lane whose provider entry this user does not hold, and again — after `CredInject`, before any process exists — when the variable the document names did not arrive. A missing credential is therefore a surfaced state, never a panic, never an unauthenticated call the provider answers with an auth error somebody then has to disentangle, and never a fabricated success. **No key exists at this packet**; key placement is the operator's ceremony, and the empty `Commissioned` map in `engineadapters.go` is the seam it fills.
- **The credential's whole path is the broker's, and its containment is a property, not a review.** The document names an `engine-cred` auth PROFILE and the env var the existing `broker.EnvInjector` fills at spawn (`laneCredInject` composes the two, in `internal/shell`, the only place both halves are in scope). The compiled config names the VARIABLE (`{env:…}`), never the value — a config body is a thing that gets hashed, logged and inspected. Containment is tested by scanning every emitted event payload, every `run_events` row, the park record, the instance identity key, the ops log and **the whole SQLite file** for a sentinel.
- **The endpoint self-check is an INPUT to the classifier, never a lookup inside it.** `LimitSignal.EndpointVerified` is established at lowering, where the config is, and forwarded as data, because `Classify` is pure and total and must stay so. It exists because one code carries two unrelated meanings: on the subscription endpoint `1113` means the plan is spent (Class 3, probe-park, unchanged); on the general endpoint the subscription does not apply at all, the pay-as-you-go balance answers instead, and the same code means the LANE IS MISCONFIGURED. Probe-parking that waits forever for a top-up nobody is going to make — P-T08-2's failure class exactly. The verdict is `ClassNone` plus a new `Action.Surface` (`endpoint-misconfigured`), which schedules nothing; `1211` (unknown model) surfaces the same way as `model-drift`, because parking a run because the provider renamed a model hides the one fact worth acting on.
- **Unknown codes classify on their SIGNAL, never on a guess** (the coordinator's OQ-3 disposition, sanctioned by S10.5's own class definitions). The provider publishes `1311`–`1321` as one collapsed row, so their individual meanings are UNVERIFIED and the signal table records the band by status rather than pretending otherwise. A zai `429` the set does not name is Class 2 when it carries a parseable `next_flush_time` and Class 3 when it does not — **never Class 1** (a retry storm against a depleted plan) and **never Class 4** (freezing a healthy lane), pinned as a property over 1300–1399 in both signal states rather than as an example. Class 4 is still checked FIRST, pinned as its own property over the code space.
- **The wire body is searched for, not assumed.** The provider's shape is `{"error":{"code":"1308","message":"…"}}` with `code` a JSON **string** — the exact shape a numeric decode rejects — and engines wrap it in their own error prose, so the extractor scans for an embedded JSON value (bounded), tolerates a numeric code, and yields NOTHING rather than a guess when nothing parses. An unparseable `next_flush_time` yields no resume time, which classifies in the safe direction (a probe-park rather than a wait on a time nobody can read). An unnamed code is logged and forwarded with its facts intact — never dropped, never fatal, never minted as a new platform kind.
- **The Eco lever is startup-bound, and that cost is paid openly.** 1.18.3 exposes provider options only through the compiled config, so `thinking:{"type":"disabled"}` rides `provider.<id>.models.<id>.options` and an effort change therefore RESTARTS that user's serve like any other config change (§61(a)). The alternative was inventing a per-request field this engine does not have. `reasoning_effort` is real, newly verified and **deliberately unwired** (OQ-4): recorded as a dated fact in the document, with no behavior invented around it. The active mode rides the durable terminal event, because S10.6 makes a mode change a **visible state, not a log line**.
- **`adapters.Answer` has a first-class decision, and its zero value APPROVES.** That is not a convenience: it is what let every construction site predating the member keep its exact meaning with no edit, on a type whose misreading executes a call a human refused. A value that is neither approve nor reject is not a default — it is a verdict the substrate cannot express, and **both** substrates refuse it loudly, because the only default available is consent. The Claude lane gained a real `deny` path (its answered hook branch could previously only ever say "allow", which made refusal unrepresentable on that lane); opencode's `sinet.decision` envelope is RETIRED, and with it the marshal failure its fail-closed sentinel existed to survive — a typed member cannot fail to encode. The four LN-1 guarantees survive verbatim: `always` unsendable (property), a raw replacement input refused (`ErrUpdatedInputUnsupported` — this substrate has no input-substitution channel and dropping a human's edit would execute the parked call unreviewed), an inexpressible decision refused (`ErrUnsupportedDecision`), and an approve staged byte-identically on the Claude lane.
- **Registering the second adapter IS the change of posture, so it is stated rather than implied.** "One agentic lane" was never code — its only occurrence in the Go tree is a comment — it was the single entry in `shell.go`'s adapter map. `engineadapters.go` now holds that map with both substrates, plus the shutdown reap: the opencode substrate runs per-user server PROCESSES, and a control plane that exits without reaping them leaves engines holding a person's ports and XDG tree. **Precisely (corrected at drain r1):** the second substrate is now REGISTERED, which is the precondition for a second paid agentic lane and not yet the thing itself — `stage/skeleton.go:87-92` still defaults every stage to `SubstrateClaudeCLI`/`LaneAnthropic`, so a zai run becomes reachable only when 2B's routing seat lands. S08.8's flat-lane pressure rule becomes reachable on the same event. **No lane is commissioned by this either**, and with none commissioned the second adapter is present and selected by nothing.
- **Two vocabularies are the SPEC's, not this lane's** (corrected at drain r1): `overflow_mode` is the ratified `{hard-stop, opt-in-credits, auto-metered}` enum verbatim (S03.6; S18.3's per-model row) — an invented value would validate against Sinet and mean nothing to anyone reading the spec — and `region_model_gate` is required per model, because a model with no gate state cannot be diffed against what the account actually serves (P-T17-3). The document also refuses to load without a credential reference or an endpoint marker: both gates fail OPEN if left optional (no credential ⇒ the spawn-time check is skipped and the engine authenticates as nobody; no marker ⇒ every endpoint self-check answers "unverified" and masks real depletion behind a permanent false alarm).
- **Coded signals are classified before any text heuristic** (corrected at drain r1). The provider ships the word "violations" inside the documented message of its own usage-limit band, so a keyword scan running first would read an ordinary depletion as a revocation and freeze a healthy lane — the mirror image of P-T08-2 and just as wrong. `classifyZAICode` therefore owns every coded zai verdict and runs ahead of `looksLikePolicyBan`, which keeps its narrow role for the codeless case. Auth codes classify by CODE as well as by status, because the engine may never surface a status at all — and an unnamed code with no status parks on the bounded probe schedule rather than falling out as "not a limit event", with the P-T17-1 auth canary as the standing revocation detector for the genuinely indistinguishable case.
- **Absent means absent on the wire** (corrected at drain r1). `omitempty` is inert on a `time.Time`, so a signal with no resume time would have serialized `"reset_at":"0001-01-01T00:00:00Z"` and a consumer reading a park horizon out of it — `internal/api`'s string-fallback read does exactly this — would show a person a wait until the year 1. `LaneSignal.MarshalJSON` omits the member entirely. The payload↔`scheduler.LimitSignal` contract is an EXPLICIT typed conversion (`scheduler.SignalFromPayload`) rather than shared tags, because the two are not the same thing: the signal also carries facts no adapter can know, and a decode that filled the whole struct would zero `EndpointVerified` and turn a genuine depletion into an "endpoint misconfigured" verdict. Normalizing also never costs the raw facts — the engine's own retry context rides alongside.
- **Left to 2B, deliberately, so the record does not go stale quietly:** the `routing.go` / `local.go` / `gpubroker.go` / **§26** "no second adapter exists in this cut" clause is now FALSE and its dated correction is R23's, in the next cut — as is the local lane's own truth (still no v0 consumer, for the different reason that no local provider entry is commissioned). Metering tiers, the multiplier/quota rows, price-row semantics, the three canary legs, the routing seat and the `zai` conformance row are all 2B's.
- **Structural constants flagged to the gate** (the §61 list, extended): `dateLayout` (the `verified_on` shape), `maxErrorScanStarts` (8 — how many embedded JSON starts a wrapped engine message is probed for, so a hostile blob cannot turn parsing into work), and `resetLayouts` (the accepted resume-stamp time shapes). All three are parsing MECHANICS rather than provider facts or operator choices, which is why they are code and not lane data; making any of them tunable is an S00.9 amendment adding S18 rows.
- **The S11.5 injection-proxy handoff is recorded where the packet that builds it will look** (OQ-1, brief §5): the wire facts live on `opencode.CredentialInjectionFacts` — inject ONLY on the coding endpoint's `/chat/completions`, `Authorization: Bearer`, per-process CA trust via `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS` with the system store untouched, the P-T01-2 pin-regression canary asserting 200 through a terminating proxy per engine version, and ⚙ `sandbox.model_egress_tls_terminate = false` as the per-lane pattern-2 fallback on regression. Z.AI publishes no `x-ratelimit-*` headers, so the proxy's Anthropic-lane second purpose has no analogue here and this lane's limit state rides error-code BODIES.
- **`{env:VAR}` resolution is MEASURED, not assumed** (drain r1): the credential design rests on the compiled config naming a variable and never a value, which only works if the engine resolves the reference. A tier-R probe now proves it at the pin and at $0 — a real serve, `options.apiKey: "{env:…}"`, a sentinel in the serve environment, and a loopback fake provider that records the `Authorization` header it received (sentinel present, `{env:` absent, `Bearer` presentation). Had it failed, the fallback would have been material in the config body, which the containment property forbids — so this is the assumption that had to be measured rather than argued.
- **⚙: none added.** The S18 index stays 118 keys / 33 domains, all five pin assertions untouched. The lane's own numbers live on the S18.3 data surfaces (the document above; the price table and budget rows are 2B's), which is exactly why they need no dotted key. `limit.probe_interval_max` / `limit.retry_cap` / `limit.retry_budget_ratio` are read by dotted key as before.
- **$0 held absolutely.** No live provider call, no credential material anywhere, tier L still structurally unreachable behind `SINET_LIVE_SMOKE=1` with its named skip. Every turn in the suite terminates on the loopback fake serve or the loopback fake provider.

## 63. The Z.AI/GLM lane, accounted for and watched — two readings that share a run and share nothing else (P3-LN-2B; S10.1, S10.3, S10.4, S08.8, S14.6, S03.7, S14.5)

2A made the lane run. 2B makes it **legible**: what it consumed, what that cost, which lane a run should take when two are covered, and how the platform learns the provider moved. The through-line is that every one of those answers is either MEASURED or DERIVED, and the two are never allowed to look alike.

- **A subscription lane has two consumption stories, and folding them produces one confident number wrong in both units.** The tokens a call consumed are measured per-call and land on the ledger row at **tier 1**. What the PLAN charged for that call is a different quantity in a different unit — published as an allowance with a charging multiplier and **no per-request counter** — so it is derived from the requests actually made, at **tier 3**, and labeled "assumed" with its reason. They are therefore two types, not two fields: `Gauge` (tokens, `Tier` stamped `TierMeasured`) and `PlanReading` (plan units, `Tier` stamped `TierDerived`), and `Gauge.Tier` exists precisely so a reading cannot be mistaken for the other kind by a caller who reads them side by side. A test pins both on the SAME run and fails if the two numbers are ever equal.
- **The plan's commercial shape is a DATED DOCUMENT, because it moved.** `internal/metering/plandata/zai.json` (the `lanedata`/`pricedata` precedent) carries the unit, the multipliers with their window and timezone, and the allowance rows — each with a `verified_on`. Three of these moved inside five weeks of the spec being written, which is the whole argument: a constant goes stale invisibly, a dated row goes stale visibly. A source scan pins that no quota number, no multiplier and no window hour is a Go constant in this package, and the acceptance test changes the DATA and asserts the gauge output moves with no code edit.
- **The unit changed, so the platform says the new one.** S10.4 seeded the denominator as "~1,600 prompts/5 h"; the plan is denominated in **credits** as of 2026-08-23 (Max 28,000/5 h + 140,000/week, peak 1.0× / off-peak 0.5×, the peak window Mon–Fri 14:00–18:00 UTC+8, the weekly cycle order-anchored per account). The coordinator's C-1/C-2 disposition binds: those sections mandate the numbers be applied *as data*, so the live values bind and the stale parentheticals are provenance notes. Receipts and gauges say **credits** — reporting a credit as a prompt would be a quiet lie about what was counted. **One cosmetic S00.9 changelog entry is owed to the gate**, and the packet does not block on it.
- **Exactly one multiplier row is the DEFAULT, and validation enforces it.** With none, an instant no named window claims would be charged at no rate and the gauge would under-report the plan; with two, which applied would depend on row order. Each request is charged at the rate in force **when it was made**, not the rate in force now, because a window that closed mid-run charged what it charged; an unreadable timestamp charges at the standard rate, because the safe direction for a consumption gauge is to over-report.
- **Nothing in this packet prices a zai row, and that is the point.** With no metered `zai` row loaded, zai usage renders **UNPRICED (tier 5)** — and a coding-plan row at $0 does not rescue it, because the S10.3 flat-lane guard refuses to price a flat lane from an all-zero row. Both guards were already there and both stay UNTOUCHED; 2B's contribution is the test that pins them for this lane plus a source scan proving no `zai` price row is constructed in code anywhere. UNPRICED is a **pricing** verdict and never a downgrade of a measured row: the line still stamps tier 1.
- **`request_id` is a reconciliation key and deliberately NOT a LINE-ITEM member** *(corrected at drain r1: it rides the RECEIPT — `Receipt.RequestIDs` — so the key is visible where a person reads their run, not merely queryable from the ledger).* S03.7 names it as the key to the operator's provider dashboard, so it rides the usage block and is read back per call by `Ledger.RequestIDs`. It is not on `LineItem` because a receipt line aggregates every call for a {model, lane, purpose} — one id out of eleven invites exactly the wrong reconciliation. A run whose blocks carry none returns none: an absent key is absent, never invented. *(The WRITE side rides the adapter's usage block and is the ceremony's; the read path and its contract land here so the calibration recipe has something to run against.)*
- **The flat-lane rule became reachable, and the seam it needed was DEAD.** S08.8 has always said selection between flat lanes uses consumption pressure, never dollars — and `Router.Pressure` was wired end to end from the composition root and **read by nothing**, which was harmless while one lane existed and would have been a silent lie the moment two did. `chooseFlatLane` now consumes it. D5 is pinned as a **property**, not an example: a reflective scan asserts no selection input type carries a money-shaped member, and a source scan asserts `routing.go` names no price, cost or metering symbol. There is nothing to *resist* pricing with, structurally.
- **A seat is DATA and it activates under coverage, not under registration.** `AlternateSeatsFor` seats a commissioned lane on **execution only** *(corrected at drain r1: the seat is composed at the composition root FROM the lane document, so no model id is a constant in `internal/worker` or `internal/shell` — pinned by the no-lane-constants source scan, extended across both packages).* Planning and judge keep their anthropic-only seats deliberately: the B3 gate ratified that mix from measured research, the judge seat additionally carries S07.5's capability-≥-executor bar AND the different-model-than-the-executor rule, and **nobody has measured a zai model against either** — seating one would be inventing a ratification. An owner holding only zai therefore gets the unchanged 2.7 subscription-gap advice for those duties, which is the honest answer.
- **Dispatchable, selectable and DISPATCHED-TO are three different things** *(corrected at drain r1, D4)*. Registering the second adapter (2A) made a SUBSTRATE dispatchable; a commissioned provider entry makes a LANE selectable; and a lane→substrate MAPPING is what actually sends the work to the right engine — that third thing existed nowhere in the tree, so a decision seating a zai model would have executed on the Anthropic CLI and metered as anthropic with nothing anywhere contradicting it. The lane document now declares its own `substrate`, the composition root maps the commissioned lanes, and the session resolves the LANE ahead of the run row — the row is stamped at creation, which happens before routing has run. So coverage grows from `Config.CommissionedLanes`, derived from what an operator has actually placed — empty at v0, which means Coverage is byte-identical to the pre-LN-2 single-lane world and the whole flat-lane path is inert until the ceremony. A pinned model skips alternates entirely: offering a different lane's model would not be honoring the pin.
- **The zai seat window is the platform floor, and that is a recorded absence rather than a number.** The provider publishes **no input-context figure** for these models on either primary page (checked 2026-08-24; both state a 128K maximum OUTPUT and no input window). Understating a window only splits stages earlier, which is safe; minting an unverified one would disarm overflow protection entirely. The observed-list canary is where model facts will arrive from. `modelCovered` stays untightened per the coordinator's OQ-5 disposition.
- **An endpoint that serves no model list is not a failed probe, and not an empty catalogue.** `ErrModelListUnavailable` exists because those three states share a code path and must not share a verdict: failing would raise a card every cycle for a condition nobody can act on, and an empty list would report **every configured model as REMOVED** — the fabricated drift the canary exists to catch. A 404 is reported honestly, dated, diffing nothing; every other non-2xx stays an error. The Z.AI coding endpoint is the live case: `/models` is undocumented there.
- **The canary legs were structurally in scope and hollow; what they were missing was named wrongly.** `PaidLanes()` already returned zai, so the auth, behavioral and model-list legs already scheduled it. The **config side** of the P-T17-3 diff was empty, and it is now composed from the lane documents — the only written record of which models a lane is configured for, dates included, and emphatically **not** the authority. The disarm reason narrowed with the truth: it used to say no per-lane endpoint exists, and half of that stopped being true when the lane document landed. What is missing is a **credential** — no lane is commissioned, and a probe dialling with none would report an auth failure that says nothing about the lane's standing. Real-request legs stay DISARMED behind `SINET_CANARY_ARM`; arming is LN-CEREMONY's.
- **No logprob canary for zai, said out loud.** The coding endpoint exposes none (S03.7), so the lane is behavioral-eval-only and the logprob canary refuses a non-local lane by name. The absence is asserted rather than assumed — an accidental omission and a reasoned one look identical in a diff.
- **The watch rows were re-verified rather than trusted.** `t1-zai-devpack` and `t1-zai-release-notes` were both fetched at commissioning (2026-08-23/24) and both are live; the release-notes row is CORRECT as seeded, and the sibling `devpack/release-notes` path that 404s is **recorded on the row** rather than quietly retargeted, because a dead watch must announce itself. All three zai rows now carry their re-verification date in their notes. The URLs are asserted by host and path **as parts**, never as a whole URL literal, because the package's own tripwire bars a routable literal from a test file — and structural comparison is stricter anyway.
- **The conformance row says what it does NOT prove, and the wall that used to bar it was INVERTED, not relaxed.** `adapter-zai` carries tier-prefixed handles across five packages. Its Notes split honestly: what it proves is the lane as **configuration** (dated provider entry, broker-only credential, signals through the five-class taxonomy, tiered consumption, UNPRICED receipts, watched drift); what it does not prove is that a paid call works, because no credential exists — every leg terminates on fixtures or a loopback fake provider at $0 and tier L stays structurally unreachable. The old test asserted a zai row must NOT exist (correct while no lane was commissioned); the new one asserts exactly one exists and that its notes name `LN-CEREMONY` and `$0`. Same honesty rule, pointed the other way. A green substrate row is still not a working lane, which is why `adapter-opencode` now stays silent about lanes and the conformance canary's lane map sends only `adapter-zai` to lane zai.
- **⚙: none added.** The S18 index stays **118 keys / 33 domains**, all five pin assertions and every owner/domain tally untouched. `budget.background_window_fraction`, `pressure.cache_read_weight`, `canary.auth_interval`, `canary.behavioral_interval` and `watchlist.fetch_fail_streak` are read by dotted key as before. The lane's own numbers live on the S18.3 data surfaces — which is exactly why they need no dotted key.
- **Row-count pins moved to exact numbers, never to inequalities:** conformance seed rows 13 → **14**, the engine_bump set 7 → **8** (a substrate that still passes can carry a lane that no longer does), and the watchlist conformance-canary's weekly lane-affecting adapter rows 3 → **4**.
- **$0 held absolutely.** No live provider call in any test or code path; no credential material committed; every canary probe terminates on a loopback `httptest` stub; tier L unreachable behind `SINET_LIVE_SMOKE=1`. The only network this packet touched was the operator-facing doc verification behind §1's dated rows.
- **The wire delta is ADDITIVE, and the golden fixture is the CONTRACT** *(corrected at drain r2, R3)*. `web/src` application source is untouched; `web/src/fixtures/api/` is not application source but a backend-owned contract snapshot, and leaving the new members out of it meant neither language was held to them — a member no fixture exercises is a contract nobody has agreed to. The meters payload gained `tier` and a `plan` object (`MeterLanePlan`), the receipt gained `request_ids`; all are `omitempty`, so a lane with no flat plan and a run with no provider ids serve exactly the bytes they served before. The fixture meter now populates a tier-3 `plan` for one lane and the goldens were regenerated through the sanctioned `SINET_WRITE_API_FIXTURES=1` path — the diff is purely additive, no existing member changed value. One CONTENT change worth naming: `routing.decided`'s `plain_reason` now names the absent local provider entry and, when two flat lanes are covered, either the pressure comparison or why the order was deterministic.

### §63 drain round 1 — the denominator was the provider's, the ratio was a raw count, and no lane knew its engine (P3-LN-2B D1–D10)

Three findings were blocking, and all three were the same mistake in different clothes: a number that looked comparable and was not.

- **D1 · The provider's allowance is a SEED, never a denominator.** `ReadPlanUnits` divided consumption by the published 28,000-credit window and reported the result as pressure — an inferred provider window, which S10.4 forbids **by name** ("the denominator is ALWAYS the operator budget, never an inferred provider window (D4)"), and which the token gauge one file over documents that invariant against itself. The allowance now seeds a PROPOSAL (`ProposePlanBudget`, a conservative ⚙ `budget.background_window_fraction` of it) that an operator declares; `ReadPlanUnits` takes a `PlanBudget` and reports `Applicable=false` with pressure 0 when none exists, mirroring the token gauge exactly. The allowance rides the reading as `SeedAllowance`/`SeedQuota` **provenance**, and a test asserts pressure is not equal to consumption÷allowance — the specific arithmetic that was wrong. Dividing by the vendor's number would have let a pressure figure move when the vendor changed its marketing, and re-imported the provider's own opinion of how much a person may work.
- **D3 · A raw count is not a ratio, and a fresh lane would have won forever.** `chooseFlatLane` ordered by `WeightedConsumption` — with no budget that is a person's unbounded LIFETIME token total, so a newly commissioned lane holds the smaller number permanently and takes every dispatch regardless of how hard it is being worked. Worse, across lanes it compares a token against a credit. `PressureReader` now returns a typed `LanePressure{Ratio, Applicable, Unit}`; production reads the right gauge per lane (plan document ⇒ tier-3 credits, otherwise tier-1 tokens) and against the DECLARED budget. The no-budget case is now explicit and pinned: deterministic duty-map order with a reason that says why, never a raw count. The gap that let this through was that the D5 test used a fake — there is now a test through the production `routePressure` with a real gauge, real checkpoints and a real declared budget.
- **D4 · No lane knew which engine ran it.** There was no lane→substrate mapping anywhere in the tree, in code or data. The run row is stamped with the process-default substrate at CREATION — before routing runs — and `runPlannedStage` forwarded only the decision's model and window, dropping its lane; so the moment a lane was commissioned, routing would seat `glm-5.3`/`zai` and the run would execute on claudecli and meter as anthropic. The lane document declares its own `substrate` (validated non-empty, and validated at `stage.New` against the registered adapter set — an unregistered substrate is a refusal, never a fallback), `SessionInput` carries the decision's lane, and `substrateFor` resolves lane → run row → ceremony default in that order.
- **D2 · The tier-3 reading had no production consumer**, which is the "wired and read by nothing" class this section was written to celebrate fixing. It now rides the meters read (`MeterLanePlan`, with its unit, tier, assumed label, multiplier and seed provenance) and `request_ids` rides the receipt. Both are `omitempty`, so the golden SPA fixtures are byte-identical and `web/src` stayed untouched.
- **D5 · `glm-5.3` was a Go constant in `routing.go`.** Seats compose from the lane document at the composition root now; the no-lane-constants scan the opencode package runs on itself is extended over `internal/worker` and `internal/shell`.
- **D6 · The "over-report on an unreadable stamp" claim was FALSE**, and the probe proved it: the SQL `created_ts` string comparison filtered a malformed stamp out **before** the fallback could run, so the call vanished entirely — an under-report, the one direction a consumption gauge must never fail in. The period filter moved into Go; an unparseable stamp is counted at the plan's `StandardMultiplier()` (derived from the rows, not assumed to be 1.0), because the discount covers most of the week and "whatever rate is in force now" was the wrong default too.
- **D7** `commissionedLanes` / `laneConfiguredModels` / `laneSubstrates` / `laneAlternateSeats` are tested through the composition root, in both the nothing-commissioned and commissioned states. **D8** two stale comments corrected, dated: the model-list canary's "empty at v0" (the documents fill it now) and the conformance row's tier-L handle ("until a credential is placed", matching its own Notes). **D9** the watch row's keyword and points threshold are asserted as parsed query parts; the logprob refusal is asserted over every paid lane with the local lane as the control, replacing a file-content check the file trivially satisfied; a parked zai run is driven to a receipt and its park history asserted. **D10** the D5 reflective scan follows maps, slices and pointers to the struct beneath — as bare map kinds `DutyMap` and `AlternateSeats` returned nothing, a scan that passed because it looked nowhere.

### §63 drain round 2 — the resolver was right and two callers never called it (P3-LN-2B R1–R5)

- **R1 · A correct function reached through a dropped argument is a broken feature.** `substrateFor` was right, and tested, and 2 of the 8 `SessionInput` construction sites never passed it a lane — the HELPER spawn (`helpers.go`) and REVISE (`engines.go`), which are precisely the two fed by an EXECUTION-seat decision, the only duty that ever seats a second lane. So the planned path dispatched a commissioned zai run to opencode while a helper on that same decision went to claude-cli. Revise had the lane in hand the whole time: it read `st.Routing.Model` and `.WindowTokens` out of the recorded S08.8 selection and left `.Lane` sitting in the same struct. **The lesson is where the guard goes.** A test of the resolver in isolation cannot see a dropped argument — the same blind spot as the `fixedPressure` fake one round earlier — so both guards drive the real call sites through recording adapters and assert which engine was reached, and both were mutation-verified: revert either fix and the guard fails. The ceremony, planner, critic and judge sites are anthropic-only by design and stay as they are.
- **R2 · Moving a filter can drop a bound nobody was looking at.** Pulling the period filter into Go for the unreadable-stamp case (r1 D6) silently retired the upper bound SQL had been enforcing, so a future-dated row — clock skew, a restored backup, a bad import — would have counted into the current period and inflated the reading. The bound is explicit now, and the test asserts the row is excluded by DATE rather than discarded: it returns to the total once the reading catches up to it.
- **R3 · A wire member no fixture exercises is a contract nobody agreed to.** The new meters members were `omitempty` and the fixture meter returned zero values, so they never reached the committed body and the SPA side had nothing to build against. `web/src/fixtures/api/` is a backend-owned contract snapshot rather than application source: the fixture meter now serves a populated tier-3 `plan` for one lane and the goldens were regenerated through the sanctioned `SINET_WRITE_API_FIXTURES=1` path. Purely additive — no existing member changed value.
- **R4 · Both new gates refuse by name, proven negatively.** A document with no `substrate` and one whose `default_model` is not in its own model list are refused at load, each naming what is wrong. Two controls keep the gates honest: the unedited seed must load, and an ABSENT default model must be ACCEPTED — a lane may ship without an execution seat, and refusing that would make the gate about something other than correctness.
- **R5** the no-lane-constants scan now covers `internal/stage` as well, which consumes lane data since D4.

## 64. The Kimi (Moonshot) lane — a wire that does not sort by status, and the first lane that can spill (P3-LN-3; R02 §5, S03.6, S10.5, S10.1/S10.4, S00.9, S16)

LN-2 commissioned a lane by copying a shape. LN-3 was supposed to be the same shape with different strings, and two findings broke that assumption before a line was written. Both are recorded here because both are the kind of thing that composes fine in one place and not another.

- **HTTP status is not a classifier on this wire, and wiring it as one would have paged the operator every week.** Kimi publishes quota exhaustion on **403 as well as 429**, and membership-tier entitlement failures on **401**. `Classify`'s opening rule freezes any lane on a bare 401/402/403, unconditionally and first — correct for Z.AI, whose auth codes genuinely arrive there while every depletion code arrives on 429. Wired naively this lane hard-freezes itself and raises a suspected-policy-revocation alert **every time its weekly window empties**: routine, recurring, and indistinguishable at the alert from the real thing. It is the exact failure CONVENTIONS §62 records the zai branch was written to prevent, arriving through a different door. And the fall-through was worse than it looked: with no numeric code `ExtractSignal` produced **no signal at all**, so only a bare status ever reached the classifier.
- **The fix is an EXEMPTION LIST, never a re-ordering, and its vocabulary is closed for a reason.** A lane document may mark a `(http_status, message_contains)` row with a `documented_class`, and the pre-Class-4 guard fires **only** on a row naming `depletion` or `model-drift` on an auth-shaped status. Everything else about the ladder is byte-identical: an unmatched bare 401/402/403 still freezes, and both directions are pinned. The vocabulary is `{transient, depletion, model-drift, endpoint-defect}` and has **no `auth` and no `balance` member** — a FORGED class is refused at load and a value outside the set is **inert**, classifying exactly as no class at all, pinned as a property, so no document can mint a verdict the classifier does not already define. *(Corrected at drain r1 F2: the closed vocabulary forbids forged classes and nothing more. It does NOT stop an IN-vocabulary re-class — somebody stamping `depletion` on the revocation row — and the original wording implied the shape of the type did. What actually catches that is the **belt** below, plus the round-trip test that drives the shipped document's own revocation strings and asserts they freeze. The type keeps the vocabulary honest; the belt is the structural net.)* `403 "Access terminated"` and the genuine-auth 401s therefore carry **no** documented class in the shipped seed, and freeze on the unchanged status rule.
- **A real body is not one phrase, and the first cut of the guard did not survive that** *(drain r1 F1, probe-executed against the shipped document)*. A provider that suspends an account can say so in a sentence that ALSO carries an ordinary depletion or entitlement phrase. `Access terminated. Your account was suspended; you have also reached your usage limit for this billing cycle.` on a 403 matched the depletion row — listed first — and **parked instead of freezing**; `Your account has been suspended for a policy violation and does not have access to this service.` on a 401 matched five generic words (`does not have access to`) and classified as model drift, which simply **continues**. Two fixes, at two layers, because either alone is thin. (1) At the DOCUMENT layer, an ambiguous body resolves to the row carrying **no** documented class — the row that classifies on its status, which on 401/403 means it freezes — so the verdict is never decided by where somebody put a line in a JSON file. (2) At the CLASSIFIER, revocation- or policy-ban-shaped text **defeats the exemption outright, whatever row matched**: the belt sits on `exemptsAuthStatusFreeze` itself rather than on one branch, which is the difference between a net and a patch. The belt has **no `OnValidCredentials` precondition** — it only DECLINES an exemption, handing the signal back to the ratified Class-4 rule, and requiring the canary to have run first would leave the hole open exactly when nothing else is watching. Its false-positive direction is a freeze on a merely-depleted lane: recoverable, operator-visible, the safe half of P-T08-2. Both halves are mutation-verified, and the inverse controls (a pure depletion phrase still parks, a pure tier-gate phrase still surfaces drift) are pinned beside the probes so "freeze on everything" cannot pass as a fix. The belt is pinned in the SCHEDULER's own suite as well as through shell's round-trip *(drain r2 C4)* — deleting it used to leave that package green, and a guard whose deletion its own package cannot see is a guard nobody is holding.
- **The same word is limit vocabulary on one wire and revocation vocabulary on another, and that is why it cannot be a global rule** *(drain r2 C2)*. Kimi publishes `Access terminated` as its literal account-suspension string, so `Your access was terminated. You have reached your usage limit…` on a 403 must freeze — and it parked. Adding the stem to the SHARED `looksLikeRevocation` fixed it and immediately broke a **pre-existing ratified pin**: `TestZAINamedCodesAgainstBanAndLimitText` holds `"The upstream connection was terminated due to overload; retry shortly."` as a zai 1302/1305 that must RETRY, and both turned into lane freezes. So the stem lives on the DOCUMENTED path (`looksLikeDocumentedRevocation`) instead, where the message table already establishes what a phrase means on a particular wire; `looksLikeRevocation` is byte-identical and zai is untouched, with a control pinning that. This is the message-keyed taxonomy's own premise applied to its own heuristics — the thing the packet exists to say, discovered a second time from the other end. `Classify` stays pure and total: the document's verdict arrives as DATA on the signal, exactly as `EndpointVerified` does. (OQ1(a). The fuller ratified `semantics` member replacing `classifyZAICode` is (b), pre-registered as an S00.9 amendment for when a THIRD coded lane arrives — it re-opens the zai path, which is a larger blast radius than one lane addition should carry.)
- **DOCUMENTED-NOT-OBSERVED is a label the code wears, not a caveat in a report.** Every message row is quoted from the vendor's published error reference as captured 2026-08-24; none is a body this platform has seen. The audit could not verify the JSON shape of a Kimi error body, whether it carries a `code` field, or whether any reset header exists (U3/U4/U5). The lane document says so in `signals_note`, the conformance row's Notes say so, and the ceremony owes a live single-request probe — one real 401, one real 429, one real 403 body if reachable — before the table is treated as final. The P-T17-1 auth canary is the authoritative revocation detector for whatever the message grammar misses. Ship the fixtures; do not ship the belief that they are complete.
- **The substrate difference really was data.** This lane rides opencode on `@ai-sdk/anthropic` where zai rides it on `@ai-sdk/openai-compatible`, and the `npm` field already existed precisely so that is a document row. **No code changed for it** — but that was asserted through the REAL dispatch and the REAL call sites (helper spawn and revise, the two that dropped the lane at §63 drain r2), never through the resolver alone, because "composes fine" is a claim and not an observation.
- **`reset_marker` is DELIBERATELY empty, and empty is the honest seed.** No reset-time signal is documented anywhere: the error reference publishes none and states reset times live in the Console (U4). Leaving the marker empty routes depletion to the Class-3 probe park rather than fabricating a Class-2 wait on a time nobody published. A live header probe at bring-up may fill it.
- **A lane's windows can be denominated differently, and one scalar cannot describe that.** The rolling **5-hour** window counts **requests**; the **7-day** subscription-anchored window counts **credits**. `PlanQuota` gained its own `unit` (empty inherits the document's, so the zai plan is expressible **unchanged**), the reading's unit follows the window it was DERIVED from, and every declared window rides the reading and the meters payload with its own unit. Rendering both gauges in one unit would have been a quiet lie about what was counted.
- **A window whose SHAPE is published and whose ALLOWANCE is not says exactly that.** No primary page carries a per-tier 7-day credit figure — the plan-price pages are JavaScript shells and the aggregators' 1×/5×/15×/30× multipliers are secondary repetition this audit refuses to promote. So the weekly row carries `allowance_unverified` with `units: 0`, meaning **"nobody published one"** and never "the allowance is nothing"; declaring both a figure and the flag is refused at load, and `ProposePlanBudget` refuses to propose from such a row because there is nothing to take a fraction of. Seeding a number this platform cannot source would have minted the denominator D4 forbids by name — and worse, an operator would have accepted it because it looked sourced. The monthly membership pool is recorded as prose for the same reason: its reset is a billing cycle, not a fixed number of hours.
- **Sinet's own count is a LOWER BOUND on this lane, not the pool state.** The vendor states verbatim that "All signed-in devices and API Key share the same quota", so the operator's interactive Kimi use and Sinet's runs draw on one pool. That is a sharper reason for the `assumed` label than the zai lane's, it rides the plan document's `assumed_note`, and consumption-pressure routing must never present the reading as anything else.
- **"Config-only" was FALSE until this packet, in exactly two places.** Both seed loaders embedded one named file and returned a one-element slice, so dropping a document in added nothing. They are directory embeds now (the `internal/storage/migrate.go` precedent), walked and returned **sorted by lane name** — and the sort is why every positional `lanes[0]` was rewritten to select by name in the same commit, rather than "fixed" by appending the new lane second and leaving a test asserting things about whichever lane the alphabet put first while claiming to test zai. **Two gates ride the edit and neither existed before:** a duplicate `lane` name or a duplicate `provider_id` is refused BY NAME at seed time, because `laneFor` takes the first provider-id match and `laneConfiguredModels` overwrites by lane — a config-only lane system whose failure mode is silent shadowing is not one.
- **The C5 routing rider is RECORDED, not enforced, and the packet says so in the code.** The lane is PRC-adjacent under either governing-law reading (Beijing operating entity, mainland-China residency, training-on-inputs by default with only a contact-based opt-out, no GDPR/EEA language; and the two applicable agreements name different governing law with no page stating which binds a membership). The rider — no household personal data, personal correspondence or identity-bearing content — rides `lanedata/kimi.json` as a `data_policy` row with its citation and `enforced: false`, because a grep found **no per-lane data-policy enforcement point anywhere in the tree**. The word "applied" appears nowhere in the rider's own enforcement note, and a test asserts that of **that note** — the scan is the lane document's `enforcement_note`, not the whole tree. Inventing an enforcement seam was out of scope; giving the routing-policy seam one place to read when it lands was not. **It needs an affirmative operator yes at the gate, not merely an absence of objection.**
- **First non-`hard-stop` lane, so 3.10 stops being theoretical — and the honest half is what shipped.** `overflow_mode: opt-in-credits` is carried end to end and a lane carrying it is distinguishable from a `hard-stop` lane at every surface that reads it. The catch, stated rather than papered over: **no surface reads billing regime yet**, so "end to end" ends at the validated document, and the currency-changing receipt path is a `TBD-S10.2` naming its consumer (the `ProposePlanBudget`/13.4 precedent — build the honest half, name the consumer, do not invent the surface). The flip is an operator act through the rehearsed kill-switch, never automatic and never silent. Recommended posture, recorded on the document: **Extra Usage OFF**, under which the lane behaves as a true hard stop and the ¥-denominated top-up rails are moot.
- **The tier gate is not a region gate, and no attribute was invented for it.** Kimi's model gate is by MEMBERSHIP TIER; `region_model_gate` stays `"none"` on every row. The gate is real and enforced on the wire (401 *"Your current subscription does not have access to k3"*), and the thing that handles it is the **model-list-diff canary** (P-T17-3) — asserted by driving an observed list that has lost `k3` and pinning that it produces a model-drift finding naming the model, **not** a lane freeze.
- **The credential variable was READ, not guessed** — and *which* record it was read from turned out to matter more than the reading. `KIMI_API_KEY` comes from the record **EMBEDDED in the npm-shipped opencode 1.18.3 binary** (`grep -ac "kimi-for-coding"` = 3 on all five shipped binaries; `~/.cache/opencode/bin` is empty), read at **$0 with no live provider call**, and the document's note records that provenance with its date — because a name with no provenance is a guess wearing a date.
- **Two records of the same provider disagree on this machine, and the packet says so instead of picking a winner** *(drain r1/r2, the packet's most instructive mistake)*. The first cut of the catalogue record was written from a 4.3 MB **models.dev cache belonging to a different tool entirely** — `/home/sinep/.hermes/models_dev_cache.json`, written by the Hermes Agent, mtime 2026-08-23 22:06:56 *(attribution itself corrected at the cap re-check; the r2 text had blamed a nonexistent opencode-written XDG cache — the third provenance error on one record)* — and called it "the installed engine's record". It is not: the pinned engine embeds its OWN record in its npm-shipped binaries, and the two differ. The embedded record lists **six** model ids — `k2p5, k2p7, kimi-k2-thinking, kimi-for-coding-highspeed, k3, k2p6` — where the fetched snapshot lists `k3, k3-256k, kimi-for-coding, kimi-for-coding-highspeed`. So `k3-256k` occurs **zero** times across all five shipped binaries, `kimi-for-coding` is the **provider key and never a model id**, `Kimi For Coding` is the **provider's** display name while `Kimi K2.7 Code` belongs to model `k2p7` — and the first cut had conflated the last pair and attributed real 262,144 context limits to two ids the engine does not carry. **Three false dated claims shipped in a document whose entire value is that its claims are dated.** Both absent ids are now flagged `seed-only-pending-observation` rather than dropped: the vendor's own docs support the 256K variant, the fetched snapshot lists both, and the ACCOUNT's observed list is what settles it (P-T17-3) — which is the whole reason that canary exists. The lesson is narrower than "check your sources": a record fetched *by* a tool is not the record *of* that tool, and only the verbatim listing pasted into the document makes the difference checkable.
- **The engine record contradicted a brief-sourced claim, and the claim was graded rather than defended.** `k3` declares `reasoning_options: [{type:"toggle"},{type:"effort",values:["max"]}]`. The effort vocabulary is `["max"]` alone, which corroborates the `unverified-primary` grade already on the brief's `["low","high","max"]`; and a `toggle` type **exists**, which contradicts this document's own "Kimi publishes no thinking disable" line. That line is now graded too, and the lever stays unwired — a contradiction between two seeds is a reason to build on neither. Had it been undeterminable, the field would have landed empty with the named-missing-credential state carrying it, which the load-time gate makes impossible to sail past.
- **The watch rows are the onboarding, not an afterthought.** `t1-kimi-coding` was a watch-only `moonshot` **candidate**; re-stamping it to the kimi LANE is what makes `severityFor` route its hits to flag-now instead of the daily digest, and `classify.go`'s lane enum is a **constrained-decoding grammar** — until `kimi` was in it the local classifier literally could not emit the lane, so no hit could ever be attributed to it. **Twelve rows** now carry the lane, all dated — ten tier-1 pages (the re-stamped `t1-kimi-coding` included), the tier-2 models.dev provider record, and the feed; the count is pinned by test so this sentence cannot drift from the seed: the **error reference** (the classifier's source of truth — a diff there can silently invalidate the signal table), the changelog, the benefits page (which carries *"A new membership system is coming soon"*, the highest-value early warning in the audit), the Extra Usage page, the K3 price row, **both** ToS pages (two, because the membership is bought on one property and consumed through the other and no page says which governs), and a points-thresholded HN feed. `kimi.com/coding` and `kimi.com/membership/pricing` were **re-confirmed JS shells on 2026-08-24**, so the row's own notes say that **a near-empty diff here is not "no change"** — a low-signal row that reads as reassurance is worse than no row.
- **The include-filter map is unchanged, and the new rows carry no filter for a DIFFERENT reason than the old ones.** `pageIncludeFilters` and its pinned `held != 14` both stand. The existing no-filter rows served **no landmark** to a live fetch; the new kimi rows were fetched for their CONTENT and nobody checked their DOM. A filter that matches nothing fails LOUD on every poll, so an unverified `main` is a guess with a recurring cost — those rows are diffed whole until somebody looks, and the test's set says which reason applies to which row.
- **⚙: none added.** The S18 tally stays **118 keys / 33 domains** and the S18.3 data-surface count stays **3** — a second lane document is another ROW of an existing surface, never a new surface. Both are asserted against the spec text rather than assumed. The lane reads only pre-existing keys (`limit.*`, `budget.background_window_fraction`, `canary.auth_interval`, `canary.behavioral_interval`, `pressure.cache_read_weight`, `watchlist.fetch_fail_streak`).
- **Row-count pins moved to exact numbers, never to inequalities:** conformance seed rows 14 → **15**, the engine_bump set 8 → **9**, the conformance-canary's weekly lane-affecting adapter cards 4 → **5**, and the canary sweep's disarmed legs 6 → **9** (3 legs × 3 paid lanes) at **four** sites — two in `internal/watchlist/canary_test.go` and two in `internal/shell/watchlist_seams_test.go`, which the brief's own exhaustive table missed. `sweep.Reasons` stays **3**: reasons dedupe by leg kind, so a third lane adds legs and never reasons.
- **The wire delta is ADDITIVE and the golden fixture is the contract** (the §63 R3 rule, applied again). The meters payload gained a `windows` array on the plan block, `omitempty`, and the fixture meter populates it so both languages are held to it. `web/src` application source is untouched and the snapshot was regenerated through the sanctioned `SINET_WRITE_API_FIXTURES=1` path. *(Corrected at drain r1 F7: the first cut shipped `allowance_unverified` UNEXERCISED — the §63-R3 rule this very bullet cites, broken in the same commit that cites it. The fixture world now carries a run on the kimi lane, so the committed body serves the shape only this lane has: a requests window beside a credits window whose allowance nobody published. Rendering that 0 as "none" instead of "unknown" is the mistake the snapshot now exists to catch.)* The delta spans four fixtures — one meters lane with its plan block, and one run row in three listings. *(Corrected at drain r2 C3: "no existing member changed value" was inaccurate. Bob's aggregate lane row went 2 → 3 and two `row_count`s moved 9 → 10 and 10 → 11 — mechanically forced by the new run, and additive in shape but not literally value-preserving. A fixture claim that overstates its own innocence is the kind a reviewer stops checking.)*
- **The S00.9 amendment is the ONE Spec/ edit, and the assembly was re-proven byte-for-byte.** A11 records the lane's early addition on the operator's 2026-08-23 order — the rider-3 mechanism **followed, not bypassed**: the Gate A–C audit ran live against primary sources and is committed. Marker sites annotated at the S03.6 lane roadmap, the S03.6 deferred "Post-v0 lanes" row (Kimi has LEFT it, as the worked example of the re-entry path the row still describes) and a new S16 lane-onboarding manifest record. No ⚙ default or clamp moves → **no S18 re-sweep**. `Spec/core-architecture-v1.md` was regenerated with the verified awk concat and re-verified byte-identical to a fresh concat (sha256 `8b4b0ef4…`), and a standing test now reproduces that check so nobody can edit one copy alone.
- **$0 held absolutely.** No live provider call in any test or code path; no credential material committed; the audit was the packet's only source of provider facts and it was not re-fetched. The only local read was the provider catalogue embedded in the installed engine's npm-shipped binaries (plus, at the first cut in error, a different tool's models.dev cache — see the two-records bullet). Tier L stays structurally unreachable behind `SINET_LIVE_SMOKE=1`, the real-request canary legs stay disarmed behind `SINET_CANARY_ARM`, and no new dependency was added (`components.lock` untouched).

## 65. Commissioned-lane activation — a placed key becomes a routable lane (P3-LN-4; S03.6, S11.5, S08.8, S03.2, S14.1, §61–§64)

LN-2 made a lane runnable and LN-3 added a second one, and both ended with the same sentence: no lane is commissioned, because `internal/shell` constructed `engineCommissioned` EMPTY. That one line of Go was the whole gap. A credential could be placed in a real broker store, `lanekey verify` could print COMMISSIONED and the tier-L smoke could make a real paid call, and the control plane would still route nothing to that lane — coverage, the lane→substrate map and the alternate seats are all derived from that map. This packet fills it from what is actually placed, and changes nothing else about how a credential travels.

- **The map is composed from PLACEMENT, and placement is a question about a KIND.** At startup the control plane lists the people who have a broker store, asks each store which auth profiles hold an `engine-cred`, and gives that person the provider entry of every shipped lane document whose profile is among them. The read is `broker.PlacedEngineCreds` (+ `StorePeople`, `StoreRoot`, `internal/broker/placed.go`): it reads the record's **plaintext `kind`** — the field the store's own `kindOf` reads — and never decrypts, never writes, and **never calls `OpenStore`**, which `MkdirAll`s, `Chmod`s and GENERATES `master.key` when absent. A commissioning probe that opened the store would mutate the host on every start with nothing commissioned and would hold a decrypting `*Store` it has no business holding (S11.5: the decision path holds zero secrets). A source scan bans `broker.OpenStore`, `broker.NewServer` and `.Resolve(` from `internal/shell`'s non-test sources, and the byte-identical-directory proof (listing, modes, mtimes, no `master.key`) is a test in `internal/broker`.
- **Only an engine-cred commissions, and the destination constraint lives in ONE place.** A `signing-key` or a `git-ssh-key` sitting under a lane's profile name commissions nothing — the S11.5 destination constraint, enforced inside the reader rather than re-decided by each caller. A corrupt or unparseable record is a lane that is **not commissioned**, never a control plane that refuses to start: the failure an operator can act on is "this lane is not commissioned", not a platform that will not run because one file in a directory is malformed.
- **A lane that cannot be commissioned never enters the map, by the same conjunction the injector uses.** `opencode.Commission` skips any document naming no auth profile or no environment variable, exactly as `laneCredInject` refuses to build an injector for one. Otherwise routing would seat a lane registered as held whose spawn authenticates as nobody — the state `ErrLaneNotCommissioned` exists to make visible. The invariant is pinned as a **property** over 200 fixed-seed draws of (person × lane × kind), not as examples: the composed `(person, providerID)` set must equal exactly the placed-engine-cred subset whose document declares both halves.
- **The entries are the DOCUMENTS' own.** Nothing here builds a `ProviderEntry`, names an endpoint or names a model id: the fill calls `LaneConfig.ProviderEntry()`, and a test asserts the composed entries marshal byte-identically to `lane.Providers()`. The no-lane-constants source scan over `internal/adapters/opencode`, `internal/worker`, `internal/shell` and `internal/stage` stays green (§62/§63 D5).
- **The map is keyed by the broker `who`, and the ambiguity that makes that a decision is carried to the gate rather than resolved here.** The broker derives its socket name AND its store directory from one name (`mode.go`), and `laneCredInjector` dials that socket — so any other key dials a socket for a person the store knows nothing about. But the platform's own person id (`auth.User.ID`, `runs.user_id`, `ProvidersFor(userID)`) is a **different namespace**, and `buildAcceptSurface` reads a third source (`$USER` with a `sinet` fallback). At one operator they coincide, which is why nothing has broken; the household case is **not settled by the spec** and no mapping was invented. The R10 startup line names the commissioned person strings so a mismatch is visible, and the reconciliation is now **LN gate-batch item 3** in the key ceremony (it replaced the item this packet discharged).
- **Disk truth, not a startup probe** (coordinator OQ2). Commissioning reads the store FILE rather than dialling the broker socket, because a startup-time probe would let a transient broker outage **silently uncommission every lane** — a control plane that routes differently depending on whether a daemon answered once is the dishonest-absence class this platform refuses everywhere else. The stated cost, not hidden: a broker started with a non-default `--store-dir` points at a store this derivation will never look at, and that control plane sees nothing placed. `broker.StoreRoot(stateDir)` is where that default LIVES rather than a mirror of it — `sinet broker` calls it for its own `--store-dir` default (drain r1 D1), so the process that WRITES a credential and the process that READS one cannot name different directories. The key ceremony computes the same default in shell and is the remaining third spelling, held by the ceremony's own step-8 output rather than by the compiler. An override knob would be an S00.9 amendment adding an S18 row, never minted here.
- **Commissioning is STARTUP-BOUND, and no reload seam was invented.** Four of the map's five consumers SNAPSHOT it at `stage.New` (coverage, lane→substrate, alternate seats, the injector composition); only `ProvidersFor` reads it live. So a live refill would produce a control plane whose adapter believes a lane is held and whose router never heard of it — worse than a restart. The truth this ships, and the truth the ceremony now tells the operator in those words: **a key placed while the control plane is running is picked up at its next start.** No watcher, no SIGHUP path, no periodic rescan. (`project.Store.Rescan` and `metering.LivePriceTable.Reload` are unrelated seams and neither was touched.)
- **One lane load, because the map and its lane set must be the same set.** `shell.go` called `engineLanes(logger)` five separate times, each re-reading and re-validating the embedded documents. It is evaluated **once** now and shared by the registration, the commissioning read and the four derivations. Not cosmetic: a document that stopped loading between two calls would desynchronise the commissioned map from the lanes it was derived from, silently. (`engineAdapterDeps.Lanes` keeps a zero-value load for a caller that wants only the registration.)
- **Commissioning is observable, and says nothing secret.** One INFO line at the composition root: how many people, which lanes, and per person which lanes — plus the startup-bound note. Auth-profile and env-var names ship in the lane documents and are not secrets; nothing else appears. A control plane that commissioned silently is one where an operator cannot tell a placed key from a typo'd profile name.
- **Selection and DISPATCH were proven at the real call sites, not at the resolver.** §63 drain r2's lesson applies directly ("a correct function reached through a dropped argument is a broken feature"), so the guard drives a stage composed from the **production fill** through the helper-spawn and revise sites against recording adapters and asserts which engine was reached, with a nothing-placed control taking the unchanged claude-cli path. Mutation-verified: neutering the fill collapses the commissioned case into the control and the guard fails.
- **Containment was re-proven for a lane commissioned by the NEW path**, not inherited from LN-2's hand-built map: the sentinel reaches the lowered serve env **exactly once**, and appears in no event payload, no `run_events` row, no park record, no lowered-spec field the instance identity key is computed over, no ops log line, and nowhere in the SQLite file or its WAL. Commissioning changes WHO gets an injector, never HOW the secret travels: resolution is still per spawn inside the closure and the compiled config still names `{env:VAR}`.
- **Nothing placed is byte-identical to the world before this packet**, pinned at both ends: the derivations (`commissionedLanes` → none, `laneSubstrates` → nil, seats → none, `laneCredInjector` → nil for everybody) and the adapter surface (`ProvidersFor(anyone)` → empty, nil error). An absent store root is **not an error**: it is a person, or a host, with nothing placed. No existing test in `internal/shell`, `internal/stage` or `internal/worker` changed an expectation to accommodate the fill.
- **The tier-L mirror became a call** (coordinator OQ3). `live_smoke_test.go`'s `placedEngineCreds`/`brokerStoreRoot` were a second definition of the store layout and the presence rule; they now call the exported reader, which is the whole argument for putting it in `internal/broker`. Identity is by INSPECTION plus an unchanged gate order and unchanged `SANCTIONED SKIP` texts across a before/after suite run — and that run proves less than it looks: at `$0` the suite returns at the `SINET_LIVE_SMOKE` gate before a single changed line executes, so what it establishes is that the first gate and its text did not move, not that the predicate agrees. There is one real DELTA, named rather than smoothed over: the exported reader applies `validProfile` to the person name where the local mirror did not, so a store under an OS username containing a dot, a slash or a NUL now answers "nothing placed" instead of reading the directory. It is unreachable on any host whose username the broker itself would accept — `OpenStore` refuses the same names, so no such store can be written by this platform — and its one direction is FEWER paid calls: the tier-L gate skips where it would have run.
- **Where the pure composer lives, and why it is not `internal/shell`** (the packet's one structural deviation from its brief). `opencode.Commission(lanes, placed)` sits beside `Providers()`/`ProviderEntry()` in the package that owns both input and output types, and takes placement as DATA (person → profile → placed-as-engine-cred), so `internal/adapters/opencode` gains no import and can hold no secret. `internal/shell` keeps the I/O, the wiring and the log line. The forcing reason is the dispatch guard: it must run in `internal/stage`, which **cannot** import `internal/shell` (shell composes the stage), so a composer that lived only in shell could never be exercised through the real call sites — and a guard that cannot see the fill is the isolated-resolver blind spot §63 r2 exists to prevent.
- **What did NOT land, named rather than left to be discovered.** The C5 no-household-personal-data rider stays **RECORDED-NOT-ENFORCED** on `lanedata/kimi.json` (`enforced: false`); there is still no per-lane data-policy enforcement point anywhere in the tree and commissioning the kimi lane does not change that — the routing-policy seam is a gate item. Coverage stays the **union across people**, with its recorded over-approximation; per-person coverage is B6/v1. Seats stay **execution-only**: no zai or kimi model has been measured against the S07.5 bars, and seating one would be inventing a ratification. The S11.5 injection proxy stays deferred to the D6/host batch on `opencode.CredentialInjectionFacts`. `SINET_CANARY_ARM` is untouched, and `tools/lanekey` is not a dependency of any of this.
- **⚙: none consumed, none added.** Commissioning has no number in it: its inputs are the state dir (already a flag/`$STATE_DIRECTORY`), the shipped lane documents and the contents of a broker store. The S18 tally stays **118 keys / 33 domains** and the S18.3 data-surface count stays **3**, both asserted against the spec text rather than assumed (§64 precedent). No new structural constant either, beyond the store's own `.cred` suffix as a file-layout mechanic. No new dependency, `components.lock` untouched, no adopted code modified, `lanedata/*.json` and the classifier fixtures untouched, `web/src` untouched.
- **$0 held absolutely.** No live provider call in any test or code path; every test credential is a fake record with an EMPTY ciphertext in a `t.TempDir()` store, never the operator's; tier L stays behind `SINET_LIVE_SMOKE=1` and was never armed. The only read of the operator's own store this packet made was one directory listing of `broker-store/sinep/`, which on 2026-08-24 held `master.key` and no `.cred` record — so on THIS host both predicates answer "nothing placed" and the tier-L gate cannot open. That is a dated fact about one host, not a proof that the two predicates agree in general; the paragraph above is where that question is actually answered.

### §65 drain round 1 — the failures that were silent, and the guard that was not there (P3-LN-4 D1-D10)

The fill held under mutation. What the evaluation found was a class: **things that go wrong without saying anything**, and one guard whose absence let a hazard back in.

- **D1 · Two processes spelled the store root, and the mutation was invisible.** `sinet broker` built `<state-dir>/broker-store` with its own `filepath.Join`; changing that literal left the ENTIRE suite green while every placed key became invisible to commissioning — a writer and a reader disagreeing, in the one direction nothing observes. `mode.go` calls `StoreRoot` now, `recordPath` uses the `recordExt` the presence read already had, and a test drives the daemon far enough to CREATE its store and asserts where it landed. Mutation-verified both ways. The "collapses three definitions to one" sentence above was itself false when written and is corrected: it collapsed one of three.
- **D2 · A typo'd profile read exactly like an empty host.** The R10 startup line existed so an operator could tell a placed key from a mistyped profile name, and a store holding `zai-coding-plaan` produced a line character-identical to a store holding nothing — the one failure the line was written to surface was the one it hid. The line now reports, per person, every placed engine-cred profile that NO lane document names. Profile names ship in the documents and are not secrets.
- **D3 · A person's whole store could vanish without a word.** A directory the broker refuses to open a store for (a dotted name) was filtered out inside `StorePeople` in silence, while its unreadable sibling warned by name. `StorePeople` reports every directory now; the invalid one reaches `PlacedEngineCreds`, which refuses BY NAME, and the composer warns with the directory and the reason. No writer in this platform can create such a directory — `OpenStore` applies the same check — which is exactly why one existing means somebody made it by hand.
- **D4 · The R6 conjunction had two spellings.** "A document naming no profile or no variable is not commissionable" lived in `Commission` and again in `laneCredInject`, in different packages. R6 said "the same conjunction" to forbid precisely that: one drifting half gives either a lane routing seats whose spawn authenticates as nobody, or a credential path nothing can reach. It is one predicate now (`LaneConfig.Commissionable`), consumed by both, with a test asserting the two refuse the same documents.
- **D5 · The nil-fallback re-created the hazard the hoist removed.** Dropping `Lanes:` from the composition root compiles, runs and leaves the suite green, because `engineAdapters` loads the documents itself — restoring exactly the desync the single load exists to prevent. A source-scan guard now fails when the hoisted value stops reaching the registration, when any consumer stops taking it, or when `engineLanes` is called more than once. Mutation-verified both ways. (The fallback stays: the pre-existing registration test constructs deps without lanes, and editing a pre-existing test to suit new code is the thing this packet may not do.)
- **D6 · The dispatch guard tested a copy of the derivation, not the derivation.** T9 re-implemented `laneSubstrates` locally, so a divergence in production's own version was invisible to the guard that exists to catch divergence. The remedy is the one deviation 1 already argued and then skipped: `CommissionedLanes`, `CommissionedSubstrates` and `CommissionedSeats` are hoisted beside `Commission` — the package that owns the documents and the entry types, and still imports `internal/adapters` and stdlib only — with the three `internal/shell` functions kept as the thin names their consumers know. The guard consumes the production functions now, and all four are tested in their OWN package, so neutering the fill turns `internal/adapters/opencode` red instead of only its consumers.
- **D7 · Two halves, each tested against a stand-in for the other.** `resolveSeat` was proven to seat a zai lane from literal seats and literal coverage; the fill was proven to produce coverage and seats. Nothing joined them, which is the §63 r2 blind spot in its selection form. A test now drives record-on-disk → placement read → fill → coverage + seats → `resolveSeat`, and asserts the placed lane is what selection returns, with the nothing-placed control still producing the unchanged 2.7 subscription-gap advice.
- **D8 · The presence read decoded fields it has no business holding.** It unmarshalled into the full `profileRecord`, pulling the nonce and ciphertext into a process whose whole posture is that it holds no credential material. A kind-only local struct now, so the ciphertext is never even decoded.
- **D9 · An evidence claim that was stronger than its evidence.** The OQ3 "outcome-identical, proven by a before/after suite run" line is corrected above: at `$0` the suite returns at the first gate before any changed line runs. The one real delta is named with its reasoning, and the operator-store sentence is reduced to the dated listing this session actually performed.
- **D10 · The red commit does not build, and that is recorded rather than rewritten.** `eb0b910` is a tests-only tree state written against a producer that did not exist yet, so four packages' test binaries fail to compile there and a bisect landing on it dies rather than answering: **`git bisect skip eb0b910`**. The history stays as it is — a tests-first commit that compiled would have been a commit whose tests were not red for the right reason.

### §65 drain round 2 — a guard that could lie, and a win that was never a contest (P3-LN-4 R1-R3)
